title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. title: Art Cinema for Tots: How to Play a Film
description: Born out of a commitment to the idea that it’s never too early to introduce kids to the pleasures of movies made outside of the commercial mainstream—and the suspicion that young audiences are often more open-minded and curious than their elders when it comes to such matters—Metrograph presents the latest iteration of Art Cinema for Tots, a celebration of handcrafted, kid-friendly films that reconcile the smart and the silly. In this edition, join us for How to Play a Film, a suite of enchanting, adventurous shorts, including Abbas Kiarostami’s early pedagogical documentary Orderly or Disorderly; Baby, D.A. Pennebaker’s document of a trip to the Central Park Zoo, and Francis Alÿs’s Reel/Unreel, which observes the game-playing of a group of Kabul children. Director of Programming (and mom) Inge de Leeuw describes the experience: “The sound levels will be dimmed, and there will be a gentle light on, creating a relaxed atmosphere where young viewers feel at ease. They won’t be confined to their seats; they can move around, explore, and enjoy the wonder of the big screen. It will be a playful, interactive cinematic journey, designed with little explorers in mind. Orderly or Disorderly (Abbas Kiarostami, 1981, 17 mins) Baby (D.A. Pennebaker, 1954, 6 mins) REEL/UNREEL (Francis Alÿs, 2011, 20 mins) Each ticket includes free admission for one child, if you’d like to bring more than one child per ticket, please email [email protected] to book a seat. description: James Broughton, prolific poet-filmmaker and member of Anthology’s own Essential Cinema Selection Committee, was one of many Bay Area experimental filmmakers whose work was distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center. Generally advertised in the “Erotic Fantasy” section of the distributor’s catalogs, Broughton’s films were recontextualized by their inclusion, their sensuality and spirituality understood as components of a holistic understanding of sexuality for the sex educator or therapist. In this special edition of Anthology’s Broughton Essential Cinema program, three characteristic works of the filmmaker’s late 60s-early 70s output are preceded by a very special entry in the National Sex Forum filmography, in which Broughton himself is bathed and massaged by erotic masseur Kenneth Ray Stubbs. Laird Sutton JAMES (1979, 10 min, 16mm-to-DCP) James Broughton THE BED (1968, 19 min, 16mm) James Broughton NUPTIAE (1969, 14 min, 16mm) James Broughton THE GOLDEN POSITIONS (1970, 32 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 80 min.

Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: Paris Was a Woman
description: Drawing on newly discovered home movies and a rich bounty of archival materials, Schiller’s trailblazing documentary, now marking its 30th anniversary, offers up a vibrant and vivacious evocation of the community of female artists and culturati of all stripes—among their number Gertrude Stein, Alice B. Toklas, Djuna Barnes, and Colette—who called Paris’s Left Bank home in the first decades of the previous century. A film that acts on the viewer like a tonic draught of fresh air, Paris Was a Woman is an enthralling evocation of one of the most storied periods in the history of the City of Light and of an anything-goes bohemian enclave that fostered both personal and creative liberation. New 4k Restoration created by IndieCollect in association with Women’s Film Preservation Fund A Zeitgeist Films release Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by broadcast journalist Laura Flanders on Friday, October 16th Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by Jane Gaines, Founder of Columbia University’s Women Film Pioneers Project, on Saturday, October 17th Introduction by Sandra Schulberg, President of IndieCollect, on Sunday, October 18th Book signing of Paris Was A Woman with author Andrea Weiss following all three screenings

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Ivan
description: In making his first sound film, Dovzhenko proved himself every bit as much an innovator in the realm of the aural as he had been in that of the visual, creating a rich sonic tapestry in this melic ode to the construction of the Dnipro Hydroelectric Station and the men and women conscripted into its accomplishment, among them the eponymous Ukrainian villager. (Some critics, however, observed that Dovzhenko took a little too much pleasure in the doings of Ivan’s antagonist, a layabout kulak who refuses to bust his hump slaving away for the glory of the state.) As influential, arguably, as Earth before it, on the Ukrainian poetic cinema of the 1960s, and an achievement of towering stature. 35mm print courtesy of Austrian Filmmuseum, Vienna Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: SCHINDLER'S LIST
description: Winner of seven Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Director, this incredible true story follows the enigmatic Oskar Schindler, who saved the lives of more than 1,100 Jews during the Holocaust. It is the triumph of one man who made a difference and the drama of those who survived one of the darkest chapters in human history because of what he did.

title: MARIE ANTOINETTE / MAKING MARIE ANTOINETTE
description: Oscar winner Sofia Coppola brings to the screen a fresh interpretation of the life of France’s legendary teenage queen MARIE ANTOINETTE. Betrothed to King Louis XVI (Jason Schwartzman), the naïve Marie Antoinette (Kirsten Dunst) at the age of 14, she is thrown into the opulent French court which is steeped in conspiracy and scandal. Alone, without guidance, and adrift in a dangerous world, the young Marie Antoinette rebels against the isolated atmosphere at Versailles and, in the process, becomes France’s most misunderstood monarch.

title: ROY'S WORLD: BARRY GIFFORD'S CHICAGO
description: Hailed as “William Faulkner by way of B-movie film noir, porn paperbacks and Sun Records rockabilly,” poet, author and screenwriter Barry Gifford has given the world more than forty works, including the Sailor and Lula novels that inspired David Lynch’s WILD AT HEART. Featuring Willem Dafoe, Matt Dillon and Lili Taylor, ROY’S WORLD: BARRY GIFFORD’S CHICAGO brilliantly brings to life Gifford’s autobiographical collection of stories, capturing a vanished 1950s Chicago through a jazzy, impressionistic combination of beguiling archive footage, animation and spoken word.

What holds a people together when the story they tell about themselves begins to fracture? THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form – a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive. Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four consequential years, from 2017 to 2021, the film considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy. Additional showtimes for October 16-22 to be announced. Previously screening as part of DOC NYC Selects: Summer 2026

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: EC: OCTOBER
description: (OKTYABR) “An imaginary document projected on actual locations, OCTOBER is the Soviet equivalent of the Sistine Chapel – an artist commissioned by the state has represented the sacred origins of the universe. Woodrow Wilson had famously hailed D.W. Griffith’s THE BIRTH OF A NATION (1915) as ‘history written with lightning,’ but Eisenstein’s cosmic newsreel cum theoretical film poem goes beyond THE BIRTH OF A NATION, as well as his own BATTLESHIP POTEMKIN, in drafting the past to serve the requirements of the present. No less than the revolutionaries who made October, Eisenstein understood himself as history’s tool. Thus consecrated to the Bolshevik faith, his OCTOBER is a perfect tautology – it clarifies and improves on history in the service of objective historical necessity.” –J. Hoberman, THE RED ATLANTIS: COMMUNIST CULTURE IN THE ABSENCE OF COMMUNISM

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 6: EROTIC FANTASY
description: EROTIC FANTASY: BEESON AND BEYOND While the bulk of the National Sex Forum’s (NSF) in-house productions were directed by Laird Sutton, a Methodist minister like co-founder Ted McIlvenna, the organization’s more experimental output was mostly helmed by Constance (or Coni) Beeson. A photojournalist-turned-filmmaker, Beeson’s films on women’s sexuality were cited as inspirations by her contemporary Barbara Hammer. In this program, presented in chronological order, three Beeson films produced for the NSF, each depicting sexual encounters layered in double-exposure and pastoral imagery, are bookended by classic works of expressive erotic cinema that, though not distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center, would be at home in its catalogs. José Rodriguez-Soltero JEROVI (1965, 11 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts.) Coni Beeson THE NOW (1970, 14 min, 16mm) Coni Beeson HOLDING (1971, 15 min, 16mm) Coni Beeson STAMEN (1972, 15 min, 16mm) Chick Strand FEVER DREAM (1979, 7 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: Deadline
description: An anonymous suicide notice at a prestigious private high school force staff and students to confront the pressures of academic achievement, family expectations, and the school system itself.

title: Hell House
description: This church wants to scare the hell out of you . . . literally. HELL HOUSE is a fly-on-the-wall documentary that follows the Trinity Assembly of God Church in Dallas, TX as they build a haunted house for the Y2K Halloween season. But instead of Draculas and Freddy Kruegers, the church recreates scenes that graphically depict modern-day "evils" such as botched abortions, fatal drunk driving crashes, and drug-induced suicides. Shot on gorgeous 16mm film stock by director George Ratliff and friends, this is an outrageous, enthralling, and poignant vérité window into the creative effort and religious zeal behind this over-the-top event. Newly restored from the original 16mm camera negative, HELL HOUSE is a new favorite obsession for fans of AMERICAN MOVIE and MISTER ORGAN.

title: Possession

After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: THE DOLL
description:
“A study of erotic delusion”
Lonesome night watchman Lundgren works the graveyard shift at a Stockholm shopping mall and in desperation steals a mannequin to bring home to keep him company. One night the mannequin comes alive, fulfilling his darkest fantasy but also questioning his grasp on reality. As the chorus of nosy neighbours starts suspecting something untoward in his dingy attic flat, Lundgren’s life begins to unravel.
Arne Mattsson’s sprawling resumes spans over 60 films including a proto-giallo detective series, breezy folk comedies and pulpy-thrillers, but in his mid-career flurry of films he directed Vaxdockan aka The Doll: a darkly poetic arthouse-creeper. British censors were swift to ban it due to “indecency” giving it the infamous “BANNED IN ENGLAND” tagline, but it’s lurid marketing obscured what is a beautifully realised psycho-fairytale about urban alienation and agalmatophilia. With strange and intense performances by Per Oscarsson and (Bergman actress turned “Swedish Sin” icon) Gio Petré, this is undoubtedly the crown jewel of Mattsson’s oeuvre.
Programmed and introduced by Harry Thorfinn-George

After Lowen uncovers what appears to be Verity's chilling autobiographical notes, she wrestles with the disturbing and twisted confessions about Verity’s husband Jeremy (Josh Hartnett), and finds it hard to separate fiction from reality, manipulation from attraction, and opportunity from obsession.

title: Once Upon a Time in China
description: No one wields a ’Scope frame with quite the same flexibility and dynamism as Hark, and the spectacular, Sergio Leone–inspired Once Upon a Time in China—perhaps the crucial film of the 1990s wuxia revival—shows Hark at his most flamboyant, keeping up with the human whirlwind that is Jet Li, here in the role of physician, martial artist, and 19th-century Cantonese folk hero Wong Fei-hung, who’s pitted against unscrupulous gangsters, human traffickers from the West, and his inconvenient feelings for “13th Aunt” Rosamund Kwan. Showstopping set pieces come fast and furious en route to a shoot-the-works shipboard finale; a monumental work of kinetic cinema. Part of Don't Play with Fire: The Films of Tsui Hark

title: The Debut
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book For LFF 2026’s curtain call, writer-director Jesse Eisenberg delivers a rapturous and raucously funny love letter to community theatre, featuring a luminous lead performance by Julianne Moore. Quiet housewife Mona has become a supporting role in her own life; her husband barely acknowledges her presence and their children are on the cusp of fleeing the nest. So when, on an impulse, she auditions for a local production of an original musical, Mona suddenly finds herself in the spotlight when she is cast in a leading role, as Miss Danielle. However, she is unprepared for the theatrical hurricane that is Jerry, her enigmatic director and the ‘biggest name in New Jersey community theatre’. As she continues to be creatively pushed by him, Mona finds herself going to extreme lengths to unlock her character. The Debut once again finds the perfect balance between humour and drama that Eisenberg delivered with his previous films A Real Pain (LFF 2024) and When You Finish Saving the World. It’s both sparklingly witty and laugh-out-loud funny, while every scene works to build on the emotional undercurrents and heartbreaking revelations that make the characters so credible. This time, Eisenberg’s talents even stretch to writing the songs for the fictional stage musical. Moore is in her element, giving one of her finest performances, while Paul Giamatti’s Jerry continues his run from The Holdovers as the master of dramedy. Ultimately, The Debut is an elegant and intelligent coming-of-older-age story about how it’s never too late to find our true selves, and the redemptive powers of community and art. Take your seats... It’s showtime! This screening will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles and will have Audio Description available on request.

title: Poem of the Sea
description: Based on a script left behind by Dovzhenko at his death, Poem of the Sea was finally filmed by his widow, Solntseva, a formidable filmmaker in her own right, her stated intention to work wholly “in accordance with Dovzhenko’s artistic conception, putting aside every trace of my own individual vision.” A companion piece of sorts to Ivan, likewise dealing with the construction of a dam and its impact on the surrounding countryside—in particular one soon-to-be-submerged village, birthplace of one General Fedorchenko (Boris Livanov), whose arrival for a visit in its final days stirs long-dormant memories. The feat of civil engineering documented here is the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant, opened in 1956 and destroyed by Russian forces in 2023, with catastrophic ecological results. 35mm SovScope print courtesy of Austrian Filmmuseum, Vienna Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: BEGOTTEN
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures:  God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed and briefly returned to life by his mother. The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

description: From first kisses to more sinister secrets, all of the loneliness and wonderment and danger and astonishing endurance that distinguish the years we pass between infancy and adolescence are contained here in Truffaut’s string of loosely connected vignettes concerning a group of schoolchildren living in the provincial town of Thiers in central France and their very involved instructor (Jean-François Stévenin). A time capsule of ’80s NYC—particularly Chinatown—and a perfectly delightful blend of odd-couple romance and amiable comedy from Cheung and longtime collaborator Alex Law, who took home Best Screenplay honors at the 7th Hong Kong Film Awards for his work here. title: Nostos: The Return
description: Rather than weighing the merits of one translation of The Odyssey against those of another, Piavoli dispenses with language—or, at least, readily comprehensible language—altogether, giving us an interpretation of the Homeric epic that is first and foremost a sensual, audiovisual experience, what dialogue there is spoken in a hotchpotch of ancient Thessalonian Greek, Sanskrit, and Latin. Free of the anxiety of influence, Piavoli—in his first foray into fiction filmmaking in a career that stretches back to the 1950s—transforms his source into a lyric memory piece, difficult to describe, impossible to forget, and at times positively overwhelming in its beauty. The film was restored in 2K by Cineteca Milano in 2017 from a 35mm positive print. The restoration was carried out under the supervision of Franco Piavoli. Part of Classical Cinema

description:
Babies are vanishing into an underground empire. A masked vigilante, a mercenary and an invisible assassin are drawn into the same fight—and towards the histories that connect them. The city’s future depends on an alliance none of them planned.
Michelle Yeoh, Anita Mui and Maggie Cheung make an unbeatable triangle in Johnnie To’s exhilarating genre collision. Ching Siu-tung’s action sends bodies and blades flying through a world of Gothic monsters, superhero masks and motorcycle stunts. Hong Kong cinema’s imagination running gloriously beyond the speed limit.

title: How Deep Is Your Love
description: Special Screening followed by Q & A with Director Eleanor Mortimer, producer Jacob Thomas, and Dr Muriel Rabone, co-producer and marine biologist. Far out on the open sea, an expedition vessel travels toward one of the most remote regions on Earth, the Clarion–Clipperton Zone, twelve days from the nearest land. Here, darkness, silence, and immense depths conceal an unexplored universe. How Deep Is Your Love follows a group of marine biologists trying to understand life in this unknown world, while grappling with the question of whether their presence risks harming what they seek to protect. A visually hypnotic and deeply absorbing journey in which every discovery reshapes our understanding of the planet. Eleanor Mortimer has created a nature documentary like no other. How Deep Is Your Love weaves awe-inspiring footage of this breathtaking realm with a looming sense of urgency as mankind’s progress threatens to upend these delicate eco-systems.

title: High and Low
description: Kurosawa’s formal genius and rare humanism are on full display in this white-knuckle thriller—source of an upcoming remake by Spike Lee—which transposes the materials of an Ed McBain novel to contemporary Japan, starring Toshiro Mifune as a rich industrialist thrown into a nerve-shredding situation after, first believing his son has been kidnapped, discovering that his chauffeur’s child was taken by accident. Boasting nigh-constant visual invention, geometric precision of framing, an inventive narrative structure, and a bevy of staggering set pieces—the train hand-off! the down-and-dirty G.I. bar!—High & Low is a virtuoso work that’s also a deeply moral one, exploring the meaning of “justice” in a society defined by vast economic disparity. “High and Low has one of the most iconic train scenes of all time. And though it’s only one of many segments, the entire, wildly careening film has the feeling of a train in the slow-motion throes of derailment.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Cinematic Void Presents DR. BUTCHER, MD
description: DR. BUTCHER, M.D. sparked riots on 42nd Street, spawned a generation of VHS gorehounds and forever set an insane standard for Italian mad doctor/zombie/cannibal carnage worldwide. Ian McCulloch (ZOMBIE) and Alexandra Delli Colli (THE NEW YORK RIPPER) star in this blood orgy of gut-munching, eyeball-gouging and face-chopping originally known as ZOMBIE HOLOCAUST, which a notorious American distributor would then re-edit, re-title and re-release as a certified grindhouse masterpiece. As a bonus, this is one of the rare Italian cannibal movies that features zero onscreen animal violence.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 7: PATTERN FILMS, PART 1
description: The majority of Laird Sutton’s work for the National Sex Forum (NSF) consisted of “pattern films,” so termed for their portrayal of a real couple’s (or individual’s, or group’s) sexual pattern. According to a 1979 NSF brochure, “actors are not used in these films; the participants are ordinary people behaving and responding sexually as they usually do…. The persons to be filmed are interviewed about their sexual patterns. Once sexual activity commences, no directions are given. Every effort is made to allow the individuals to feel at ease.” Reflecting their use in structured therapeutic sessions, this selection of pattern films is preceded by a short from the Multi-Media Resource Center’s “Humor and Mood Alteration” collection, meant to dispel unease ahead of these candid portraits. Greg Von Buchau LOVE TOAD (1971, 2 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Laird Sutton POSSIBILITIES (1973, 12 min, 16mm) Laird Sutton QUIET AFTERNOON (1975, 20 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Edd Dundas NICK AND JON (1976, 20 min, 16mm) Laird Sutton BOTH/AND (1975, 25 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 85 min.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: A new kind of horror remake from Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ), starring Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson. After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium. (MUBI)

title: Hereditary
description: Following the death of the Leigh family matriarch, Annie and her children uncover disturbing secrets about their heritage. Their daily lives are not only impacted, but they also become entangled in a chilling fate from which they cannot escape, driving them to the brink of madness.

title: In the Mouth of Madness
description: Directed and scored by John Carpenter, and written by Michael De Luca, this love letter to the work of H. P. Lovecraft sees insurance investigator John Trent (Sam Neill) journey to a mysterious small town, unaware that he is entering the depths of insanity. Taking its name from Lovecraft’s 1936 novella At the Mountains of Madness , the final film in the Apocalypse Trilogy follows Trent as he tracks down horror novelist Sutter Cane (Jürgen Prochnow), who has gone missing after completing his latest book. Word spreads that anyone who reads an advance copy of the novel becomes a homicidal maniac, but Trent is convinced it is all a publicity stunt—until his investigation leads him to an eerie town identical to Cane’s work.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Sandy King

title: KEN RUSSELL'S THE DEVILS
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Paris Was a Woman
description: Drawing on newly discovered home movies and a rich bounty of archival materials, Schiller’s trailblazing documentary, now marking its 30th anniversary, offers up a vibrant and vivacious evocation of the community of female artists and culturati of all stripes—among their number Gertrude Stein, Alice B. Toklas, Djuna Barnes, and Colette—who called Paris’s Left Bank home in the first decades of the previous century. A film that acts on the viewer like a tonic draught of fresh air, Paris Was a Woman is an enthralling evocation of one of the most storied periods in the history of the City of Light and of an anything-goes bohemian enclave that fostered both personal and creative liberation. New 4k Restoration created by IndieCollect in association with Women’s Film Preservation Fund A Zeitgeist Films release Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by broadcast journalist Laura Flanders on Friday, October 16th Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by Jane Gaines, Founder of Columbia University’s Women Film Pioneers Project, on Saturday, October 17th Introduction by Sandra Schulberg, President of IndieCollect, on Sunday, October 18th Book signing of Paris Was A Woman with author Andrea Weiss following all three screenings

title: Frankenstein (1931) and The Bride of Frankenstein (1935)
description: FRANKENSTEIN (1931): Henry Frankenstein pieces together body parts in the hope of bringing a human-like creature to life. The mad scientist’s dreams are shattered by his monstrous creation awakening with rage to a world that hates and fears him. THE BRIDE OF FRANKENSTEIN (1935): Dr. Frankenstein and his monster both turn out to be alive after being attacked by an angry mob. The now-chastened scientist attempts to escape his past, but a former mentor forces him to assist with the creation of a new creature. Presented with a 10-minute break between features.

title: Onslaught
description: A rogue team of genetically engineered super-soldiers breaks loose in the desert, forcing a tough Army sniper to fight fiercely to protect her young daughter.

title: Forgotten Island
description: When two best friends are sucked through a magical portal they find themselves menaced by a dangerous creature and in danger of losing the memories that bond them together.

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
description: In 1972, legendary filmmaker William Greaves gathered an extraordinary group of artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance. After more than 50 years, his son David Greaves has completed his breathtaking miracle of a movie.

title: The Devils
description: Ken Russell’s infamous adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s book, about the apparent possession of a group of nuns after one (Vanessa Redgrave) accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, is at long last available in its full, uncensored splendor.

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: Mulholland Dr.
description: A dark-haired woman (Laura Elena Harring) is left amnesiac after a car crash. She wanders the streets of Los Angeles in a daze before taking refuge in an apartment. There she is discovered by Betty (Naomi Watts), a wholesome Midwestern blonde who has come to the City of Angels seeking fame as an actress. Together, the two attempt to solve the mystery of Rita's true identity. The story is set in a dream-like Los Angeles, spoilt neither by traffic jams nor smog.

title: Pink Palace: J.G.Ballard’s CRASH
description: Ban this perverted filth! Was the headline when David Cronenberg adapted J.G. Ballard’s classic underground novel in 1996, and Westminster Council banned it from screening in central London, even though the film had been given an 18 cert from the BBFC.  This is deeply unsettling psychological cinema...

title: Whalefall
description: A scuba diver in search of his deceased father's remains gets swallowed by an 80-foot, 60-ton sperm whale and has only one hour to escape before his oxygen runs out. After giving up on life, the young man is surprised to find a reason to live in the most dangerous and unlikely of places.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Case 137
description: Case 137 is seemingly just another case for Stéphanie, an investigator at the IGPN, the police of the police. But an unexpected element will trouble Stéphanie and transform case 137 into something more than a simple number.

title: SHOGUN ASSASSIN
description:
After his wife is murdered by agents of a paranoid shogun, former executioner Ogami Ittō takes to the road with his young son Daigoro, pushing him through feudal Japan in a baby cart fitted with an alarming arsenal of hidden weapons. Pursued by ninja assassins and three fearsome Masters of Death, father and son carve a path through ambushes, betrayals and spectacular fountains of blood.
Created for American grindhouse audiences by re-editing and dubbing the first two Lone Wolf and Cub films, SHOGUN ASSASSIN transforms Kenji Misumi’s samurai epics into a lean, hallucinatory barrage of flashing blades, severed limbs and pulsing synthesiser music. Initially notorious in Britain for its extreme violence, the film became a midnight-movie classic whose influence can be felt everywhere from Wu-Tang Clan’s Liquid Swords to Quentin Tarantino’s Kill Bill.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Street Fighter
description: Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li (Callina Liang) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

description: Set in an English boarding school, Extra Geography follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Resident Evil
description: In this sci-fi horror action reboot, a hapless medical courier fights for his life amid an outbreak of a deadly mutagenic virus in an isolated mountain town.

title: The Great Experiment
description: Fri, Oct 16: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing, moderated by filmmaker Laura Poitras ( Citizenfour ) after 7:15 show! Sat, Oct 17: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing & True/False Fest Artistic Director Farihah Zaman, moderated by filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir after 7:15 show! What holds a people together when the story they tell about themselves begins to fracture? THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form – a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive. Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four consequential years, from 2017 to 2021, the film considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy. Additional showtimes for October 16-22 to be announced. Previously screening as part of DOC NYC Selects: Summer 2026

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
description: The Coens’ country-fried, Depression era, quasi-musical take on The Odyssey borrows its title—and more than a bit of its anarchic sense of humor—from Preston Sturges’s Sullivan’s Travels, choreography cues from Busby Berkeley, and rips a few dozen pages out of the Great American Songbook for good measure. Pomaded convict Everett Ulysses McGill (George Clooney) takes a powder from a Mississippi chain gang with dimwit pals John Turturro and Tim Blake Nelson in tow and sets out to scare up his Penelope (Holly Hunter), along the way running afoul of Klansmen, gangsters, sultry creek-side sirens, and a Bible-thumping Cyclops (John Goodman), even taking a quick break en route to record a jubilant rendition of “Man of Constant Sorrow.” Part of Classical Cinema

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: RoboCop - The Director's Cut
description: I’d buy that for a dollar! For a strange few years, beginning with this runaway hit, the perverse imagination and earthy humor of Verhoeven seemed to sync up perfectly with the desires of the American multiplex-going public. In dystopian Detroit, private sector Omni Consumer Products have taken over policing and made the ultimate law enforcement machine from leftover pieces of peace officer Peter Weller—but they didn’t bank on their invention making his way up the corporate ladder of crime. A frightfully funny vision of a post-industrial cybernetic future, with Kurtwood Smith, Ronny Cox, and Muguel Ferrer an impressive trifecta of irredeemable scumbags. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Deadline
description: An anonymous suicide notice at a prestigious private high school force staff and students to confront the pressures of academic achievement, family expectations, and the school system itself.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: Carrie
description: In this chilling adaptation of Stephen King's horror novel, withdrawn and sensitive teen Carrie White (Sissy Spacek) faces taunting from classmates at school and abuse from her fanatically pious mother (Piper Laurie) at home. When strange occurrences start happening around Carrie, she begins to suspect that she has supernatural powers. Invited to the prom by the empathetic Tommy Ross (William Katt), Carrie tries to let her guard down, but things eventually take a dark and violent turn.

title: Verity
description: Adapted from Colleen Hoover's best-selling novel, this seductive, psychological thriller follows renowned author Verity Crawford (Anne Hathaway) and Lowen Ashleigh (Dakota Johnson), a struggling writer who relocates to the remote Crawford estate to ghostwrite for Verity. After Lowen uncovers what appears to be Verity's chilling autobiographical notes, she wrestles with the disturbing and twisted confessions about Verity’s husband Jeremy (Josh Hartnett), and finds it hard to separate fiction from reality, manipulation from attraction, and opportunity from obsession.

title: Nadja
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: An American Werewolf in London
description: David (David Naughton) and Jack (Griffin Dunne), two American college students, are backpacking through Britain when a large wolf attacks them. David survives with a bite, but Jack is brutally killed. As David heals in the hospital, he's plagued by violent nightmares of his mutilated friend, who warns David that he is becoming a werewolf. When David discovers the horrible truth, he contemplates committing suicide before the next full moon causes him to transform from man to murderous beast.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Narrated by Melanie Griffith, this modern fable celebrates the messiness of female interiority with deadpan humour, surrealist flourishes, and interpretative dance numbers. title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 8: PATTERN FILMS, PART 2
description: The majority of Laird Sutton’s work for the National Sex Forum (NSF) consisted of “pattern films,” so termed for their portrayal of a real couple’s (or individual’s, or group’s) sexual pattern. According to a 1979 NSF brochure, “actors are not used in these films; the participants are ordinary people behaving and responding sexually as they usually do…The persons to be filmed are interviewed about their sexual patterns. Once sexual activity commences, no directions are given. Every effort is made to allow the individuals to feel at ease.” Reflecting their use in structured therapeutic sessions, this selection of pattern films is preceded by a short from the Multi-Media Resource Center’s “Humor and Mood Alteration” collection, meant to dispel unease ahead of these candid portraits. Laird Sutton & Bill Chamberlain TITLES AVAILABLE (1972, 7 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Laird Sutton FULLNESS (1975, 13 min, 16mm) Ann Hershey WE ARE OURSELVES (1975, 15 min, 16mm) Laird Sutton JIM & VERN (1979, 15 min, 16mm) Laird Sutton A RIPPLE IN TIME (1975, 20 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Introduced by documentary filmmaker Robert James.

title: D’est (From the East)
description: D’est (From the East). 1993. Belgium/France. Directed by Chantal Akerman. 2K restoration by the Royal Film Archive of Belgium — CINEMATEK and Fondation Chantal Akerman; DCP courtesy Icarus Films. No dialogue. 115 min. Filmed from East Germany to Moscow between the summer and deep winter of 1993, Chantal Akerman’s dispatch from the newly collapsed Soviet Union captures “everything that touched me” through deliberately paced tracking shots, circular pans, and domestic scenes. A travelogue through landscapes and overcrowded urban centers—whose interminable tableaux of train and bus queues become a sobering metaphor of historic upheaval—D’est chronicles everyday Poles, Ukrainians, Germans, and Russians staring down an uncertain future. Claire Atherton recalls editing this landmark film: “It was like a composition, both in the musical and visual sense. We were sculpting in time and space, looking for the right rhythm. We were editing in the same way Chantal had shot the film, following our intuition, without trying to understand. We said simple things to each other about color, clashes, ruptures, night and day, exterior and interior, violence, softness, the sound of footsteps in the snow or of tires screeching on icy roads…. Words only appeared a year later, like echoes to the images, when we were editing the installation D’est, au bord de la fiction (1995). These words became those of the installation’s 25th screen, spoken by Chantal: ‘Yesterday, today, and tomorrow, there were, there will be, there are at this very moment, / people whom history, which no longer even has a capital H, whom history has struck down.’”

What holds a people together when the story they tell about themselves begins to fracture? THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form – a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive. Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four consequential years, from 2017 to 2021, the film considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy. title: Nashville

With overlapping soundtracks of dialogue, political rhetoric, and country music (written and performed by its stars including Karen Black and Ronee Blakley) and a cavalcade of fascinating characters that shoot for stardom, or fall from it, this film is a one-of-a-kind exercise in flawlessly-executed excess. Funny, cynical, and sonically enduring, you won’t want to miss a beat of Nashville .

title: One in a Million
description: Wed, Oct 21: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa, moderated by Julie Goldman, after 7:00 show! Thurs, Oct 22: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa after 7:00 show! Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home? Additional showtimes for Oct 21-27 to be announced.

title: The Great Experiment
description: Fri, Oct 16: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing, moderated by filmmaker Laura Poitras ( Citizenfour ) after 7:15 show! Sat, Oct 17: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing & True/False Fest Artistic Director Farihah Zaman, moderated by filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir after 7:15 show! What holds a people together when the story they tell about themselves begins to fracture? THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form – a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive. Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four consequential years, from 2017 to 2021, the film considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy. Additional showtimes for October 16-22 to be announced. Previously screening as part of DOC NYC Selects: Summer 2026

title: Barrio Triste
description: In an impoverished neighborhood of 1980s Medellín, a group of disaffected teens steal a TV reporter’s camera to document their lives. Piercing the derelict landscape’s oppressive atmosphere with disarming reflections on dreams and death, their understanding of reality and hope begins to erode as reports of mysterious lights falling from the sky coincide with temporal and spatial distortions. In his striking feature debut, long-time Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz captures an intimate, formally daring portrait of Colombia's forgotten youth. Barrio Triste is heightened by a restless, intense debut score from Arca, whose fluid soundscapes anchor the film's vision. Navigating the thin line between desperation and the supernatural, Stillz delivers a beautiful, unclassifiable piece of contemporary cinema.

description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: Extra Geography
description: Set in an English boarding school, Extra Geography follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".

title: The Seven Year Itch
description: One of Monroe’s most successful roles was as The Girl in director Billy Wilder’s The Seven Year Itch , a comedy about a restless husband left to his own devices for the summer. To market the film, photographer Sam Shaw proposed the indelible subway grate moment, which dozens of publicity photographers attended on location in New York City. Due to sound issues, the real scene was shot on the 20th Century-Fox lot in Los Angeles. Outside of this iconic scene, the exhibition Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon also features silk pajamas worn during a pivotal moment in developing Monroe’s girl-next-door character.
director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Charles K. Feldman, Billy Wilder

title: Hellraiser
description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart , horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration. “The best horror film ever to be made in Britain.” – Melody Maker Opens Wed Oct 21, showtimes to be announced.

title: The Age of Innocence
description: One breathtaking composition follows another in Scorsese’s adaptation of Edith Wharton’s Pulitzer Prize–winning masterpiece about social mores (and taboos) amongst New York’s viperous moneyed classes in late 19th-century New York, brought to life by an all-star lineup of craftspeople including cinematographer Michael Ballhaus, editor Thelma Schoonmaker, production designer Dante Ferretti, and composer Elmer Bernstein. In front of the camera there are Daniel Day-Lewis and Michelle Pfeiffer suffering beautifully as wealthy lawyer Newland Archer and Countess Ellen Olenska, the divorced pariah whom he yearns for, and Winona Ryder as Archer’s fiancée and, eventually, wife—outwardly a winsome innocent, but a cunning, cutthroat strategist where affairs of the heart are concerned. It was, Ryder stated during a recent appearance on (of all things) Hot Ones, “The role of a lifetime.” Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Amour
description: For their study of an elderly couple—played by icons of French cinema Jean-Louis Trintignant and Emmanuelle Riva, both superlative—facing final separation by cruel death, Haneke and cinematographer Darius Khondji created a litany of framings that feel brittle in their composed beauty, each marked by an elegant exactitude and slowly suffocating airlessness. Hard and tender, this may be Haneke’s ultimate accomplishment—and, incidentally, a eulogy for the youthful dreams of the 1960s European art cinema. title: By Design
description: Upon seeing a gorgeous chair in a showroom, Camille (Juliette Lewis) realises that she truly envies the life of this perfect piece of furniture. If only she could be someone’s favourite thing. When she and the chair swap forms, Camille learns that she is better liked as an inanimate object than she was as a person: her mother (Betty Buckley) finds her to be a better listener, and her best friends (Samantha Mathis and Robin Tunney) enjoy a newfound, friction-free rapport. As the chair, Camille is unable to speak or move and winds up in the hands of Olivier (Mamoudou Athie), a minimalist bachelor who gradually becomes romantically fixated on his elegant new possession. Narrated by Melanie Griffith, this modern fable celebrates the messiness of female interiority with deadpan humour, surrealist flourishes, and interpretative dance numbers. An absurdist spin on the body-swap comedy, By Design is a bold new work from singular filmmaker Amanda Kramer.

title: Paris Was a Woman
description: Drawing on newly discovered home movies and a rich bounty of archival materials, Schiller’s trailblazing documentary, now marking its 30th anniversary, offers up a vibrant and vivacious evocation of the community of female artists and culturati of all stripes—among their number Gertrude Stein, Alice B. Toklas, Djuna Barnes, and Colette—who called Paris’s Left Bank home in the first decades of the previous century. A film that acts on the viewer like a tonic draught of fresh air, Paris Was a Woman is an enthralling evocation of one of the most storied periods in the history of the City of Light and of an anything-goes bohemian enclave that fostered both personal and creative liberation. New 4k Restoration created by IndieCollect in association with Women’s Film Preservation Fund A Zeitgeist Films release Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by broadcast journalist Laura Flanders on Friday, October 16th Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by Jane Gaines, Founder of Columbia University’s Women Film Pioneers Project, on Saturday, October 17th Introduction by Sandra Schulberg, President of IndieCollect, on Sunday, October 18th Book signing of Paris Was A Woman with author Andrea Weiss following all three screenings

title: SHAKEDOWN
description:
Public defender Roland Dalton is assigned to represent a drug dealer accused of killing an undercover police officer. Convinced that the shooting was self-defence, Dalton turns to renegade narcotics cop Richie Marks for help and uncovers a network of corrupt officers protecting a lucrative drug operation. Their investigation pulls both men into an escalating war fought across the streets, courtrooms and rooftops of New York.
Peter Weller and Sam Elliott tear through James Glickenhaus’s gloriously excessive action thriller, a film that combines hardboiled conspiracy plotting with some of the most outrageous practical stunt work of the 1980s. From a department-store shootout to a climax involving a passenger jet, SHAKEDOWN continually finds new ways to outdo itself while preserving the grit and momentum of a classic urban crime movie.

title: These Violent Delights
description: One Night Only Includes recorded Q & A Scottish Ballet's captivating reimagining of the Shakespeare classic features exceptional choreography, stunning costumes, and seamless cinematography to deliver a distinctive ballet experience. Juliet wakes in The Apothecary, traces of death surrounding them: daggers, spilt poison, Romeo’s body. Rewind. Dragged into a fevered hallucination, Juliet slips between memory and nightmare as shadowy figures pull them back through the moments that led here. They drift between the mirrored dining rooms of the Capulets and Montagues – two families divided by pride and ambition. At the Capulet table, Paris is paraded as a suitor; Juliet refuses the future mapped out for them. At the Montague feast, they are unseen – more ghost than guest. The worlds fracture and reform. Romeo, restless within his family’s restraint, retreats into his journal until Benvolio and his boyfriend Mercutio shatter his solitude, luring him towards a night of abandon. Urged by Nurse to escape expectation, Juliet seeks refuge at The Apothecary, a queer club reclaimed from an abandoned building and presided over by the drag Sisters Laurence and Giovanna. Beneath neon light and pulsing music, Romeo arrives. Across a haze of glitter and sweat, their eyes meet. The connection is immediate, intoxicating. In a flamboyant ritual before the crowd, their love is sanctified. Outside, Tybalt’s resentment curdles. A confrontation erupts; Mercutio is wounded and, in the chaos, Romeo sends Tybalt to his death. Reeling, Juliet agrees to appease their parents by courting Paris while secretly planning to flee. Back at The Apothecary, Juliet takes a pill to escape reality and sends a defiant message, mistaken for a suicide note. Believing Juliet dead, Romeo rushes to them with poison in hand. We end where we began.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: THE GAME
description: An arrogant, isolated investment banker is targeted by an enigmatic entertainment company, plunging into an escalating, reality-bending conspiracy orchestrated by his estranged brother to shatter his emotional detachment.

title: One in a Million
description: Wed, Oct 21: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa, moderated by Julie Goldman, after 7:00 show! Thurs, Oct 22: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa after 7:00 show! Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home? Additional showtimes for Oct 21-27 to be announced.

title: EC: IVAN THE TERRIBLE: PARTS 1 & 2
description: (IVAN GROZNY) “The first time in history a man has committed suicide by cinema,” quipped Dovzhenko. A state-sanctioned production, Ivan’s opulent furs and jewels color the black-and-white machinations by a demonic Czar bent on making his subjects’ lives a living hell – a statement pointed with outrage directly at Stalin.

title: NAZA
description: Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

title: Qui a tué Ali Ziri? 2015. Directed by Luc Decaster
The Great Experiment
description: Fri, Oct 16: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing, moderated by filmmaker Laura Poitras ( Citizenfour ) after 7:15 show! Sat, Oct 17: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing & True/False Fest Artistic Director Farihah Zaman, moderated by filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir after 7:15 show! title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: A new kind of horror remake from Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ), starring Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson. After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium. (MUBI)

title: Bones on 35mm
description: Vidiots is dying to welcome back legendary director Ernest R. Dickerson for a special screening of his cult classic horror starring Snoop Dogg – Bones on glorious 35mm celluloid!

title: An Evening of Short Films by Women Directors
description: Lynne Ramsay ( We Need to Talk About Kevin , 2011) directed Small Deaths (1996), an evocative look at key events in a girl’s life. Nikyatu Jusu’s Suicide by Sunlight (2019) tells of Black vampires in a near-future New York. Silent comedy star Mabel Normand directs herself and Charles Chaplin in Mabel’s Busy Day (1914). Two estranged friends are reunited for a difficult journey in Dominga Sotomayor Castillo’s La Montaña (2008). A mom (Anna Camp) must cope with her daughter’s claim to be the reincarnation of Elvis Presley in Bonnie Kathleen Ryan’s comedy short GraceLand (2020). In Sonia Sebastián’s Yo también (2017), a young woman has to inform her romantic partners about her hepatitis diagnosis.

title: KEN RUSSELL'S THE DEVILS
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

title: The Illiac Passion
description: Markopoulos corralled together the underground’s haute monde—Taylor Mead, Gerard Malanga, Jack Smith, Gregory Battcock and, in the role of Poseidon, Andy Warhol—for his radical reinterpretation of Aeschylus’s Prometheus Bound, in which the filmmaker can be heard on the soundtrack reciting Thoreau’s translation of the source text betwixt snatches of Bartók’s Cantata Profana. A rebel posing a direct challenge to Zeus’s absolute authority, Prometheus was a figure of fascination for Markopoulos, who saw in the outlaw Titan something of a kindred spirit. Hence his vainglorious description of The Illiac Passion: “Metamorphosis of the filmmaker. Passions of the filmmaker. Out of his breast the free flowing blood of the creation of a motion picture which depicts the passions of mankind and of everyman in general.” Part of Classical Cinema

title: Arrows of Desire Book Launch + Friendship’s Death
description: To celebrate the publication of a new anthology of Peter Wollen's texts, Arrows of Desire: Selected Writings 1963–2002 , there will be a screening of his solo feature film Friendship’s Death (1987) and a conversation with the book's editors, Kodwo Eshun, Oliver Fuke and Nicolas Helm-Grovas. There will be a short reception with books available for purchase at 7pm. The conversation with the book’s editors will take place in the cinema at 8.30pm. Arrows of Desire , the first of three new volumes, brings together unpublished and inaccessible writings on counter-cinema, anti-imperialist politics and revolutionary Mexican art. Playful, theoretically rigorous and historically precise, Wollen’s writing reinvented criticism as a formally experimental practice indexing the intellectual, political and artistic histories of the twentieth century. The book presents texts on Eisenstein and Godard alongside essays and interviews tracing developments in film and video from the 1970s to the 1990s. It tracks the political energies running through Wollen’s filmmaking and writing on global politics and culture in relation to Iran, Indonesia, Palestine, Aden and Zanzibar. It also presents texts relating to Wollen’s film, Friendship’s Death , adapted from his science fiction story, published in Bananas, Emma Tennant’s literary magazine, in 1976. Starring Tilda Swinton as an alien android from Procyon, who lands in Amman, Jordan, days before the events sometimes referred to as ‘Black September’, the film and short story are, in part, informed by Wollen’s experience as a political journalist, writing on global politics for New Left Review and International Socialist Journal. The texts presented in Arrows of Desire illuminate the film and testify to Wollen’s enduring commitment to anti-imperialist politics.

title: Pink Palace: IT CAME FROM KUCHAR
description: A much requested repeat from earlier this year that a lot of you missed out on, Pink Palace presents a loving tribute to the multifaceted careers of underground filmmaking legends and gay twin brothers George and Mark Kuchar (SINS OF THE FLESHOPOIDS, HOLD ME WHILE I'M NAKED). Exploring their vast bo...

title: Onslaught
description: A rogue team of genetically engineered super-soldiers breaks loose in the desert, forcing a tough Army sniper to fight fiercely to protect her young daughter.

title: Forgotten Island
description: When two best friends are sucked through a magical portal they find themselves menaced by a dangerous creature and in danger of losing the memories that bond them together.

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
description: In 1972, legendary filmmaker William Greaves gathered an extraordinary group of artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance. After more than 50 years, his son David Greaves has completed his breathtaking miracle of a movie.

title: The Devils
description: Ken Russell’s infamous adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s book, about the apparent possession of a group of nuns after one (Vanessa Redgrave) accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, is at long last available in its full, uncensored splendor.

title: The Others
description: Academy Award® winner Nicole Kidman (Best Actress, The Hours, 2003) delivers an unforgettable performance in this gothic supernatural thriller. In 1945, Grace (Kidman) and her two children wait for her husband's return from the war, living an unusually isolated existence behind the locked doors and drawn curtains of a secluded mansion in Jersey. Three mysterious new servants arrive and it becomes chillingly clear that there is far more to this house than can be seen, and Grace finds herself in a terrifying fight to save her children and preserve her sanity. Acclaimed by critics, the unpredictable twists and turns of this compelling psychological horror classic will keep you on the edge of your seat.

title: THE SOCIAL RECKONING
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the hel...

title: Whalefall
description: A scuba diver in search of his deceased father's remains gets swallowed by an 80-foot, 60-ton sperm whale and has only one hour to escape before his oxygen runs out. After giving up on life, the young man is surprised to find a reason to live in the most dangerous and unlikely of places.

title: Video Bazaar presents: Possession (North American Cut)
description: Video Bazaar is thrilled to present a rare screening of the North American theatrical cut of Possession as part of our…

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show!
