title: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: Digger
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise. The most powerful man in the world (Cruise) embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything. This wildly hilarious satire was shot entirely in VistaVision.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Akinola Davies presents ROCKERS
description: Legendary reggae artists play themselves in this exuberant tale of struggle and triumph. Leroy (Horsemouth) Wallace and Richard (Dirty Harry) Hall recruit a Robin-Hood band of friends to get even with some oppressive mafia types. The cast includes Burning Spear, Jacob Miller, Gregory Isaacs, Kiddus ...

title: Street Fighter
description: Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li (Callina Liang) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

title: THE MAD BOMBER (ON 16MM)
description:
William Dorn, a disturbed Los Angeles man whose life has been destroyed by personal tragedy, begins planting and detonating bombs around the city against people and places he blames for society’s problems. When one of his attacks is witnessed by a serial rapist, police detective Geronimo Minelli is forced to track down both the bomber and the dangerous criminal who may hold the key to identifying him.
A grimy piece of early-1970s exploitation cinema, Bert I. Gordon’s crime thriller mixes police procedural, psychological study, and urban nightmare. Chuck Connors gives the film its unsettling centre as a man consumed by rage and paranoia, while the collision between the bomber, the detective, and the rapist creates a bleak portrait of violence and social decay.

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
description: In 1972, legendary filmmaker William Greaves gathered an extraordinary group of artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance. After more than 50 years, his son David Greaves has completed his breathtaking miracle of a movie.

title: Deadline
description: An anonymous suicide notice at a prestigious private high school force staff and students to confront the pressures of academic achievement, family expectations, and the school system itself.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Member Screening: Making Marie Antoinette
description: Join us for a special advance screening of Making Marie Antoinette with remarks by Sofia Coppola and an introduction by Sophie Cavoulacos, Curator, Department of Film. For the first time, Coppola’s dynamic craftsmanship in creating Marie Antoinette (2006) is on full display in this diary shot by her mother, filmmaker Eleanor Coppola, on the film’s set in Versailles in 2005. Narrated by Diane Lane, reciting Eleanor’s journals from the time, this is a rare behind-the-scenes glimpse that is both process-oriented and touchingly personal. Making Marie Antoinette. 2026. USA. Directed by Eleanor Coppola. DCP courtesy MUBI. 86 min. Accessibility FM assistive-listening devices (headsets and neck loops for T-coil compatibility) are available for sound amplification. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available for public programs upon request with two weeks’ advance notice. MoMA will make every effort to provide accommodation for requests made with less than two weeks’ notice. Please contact members_programs@moma.org to make a request for these accommodations.

title: Resident Evil
description: In this sci-fi horror action reboot, a hapless medical courier fights for his life amid an outbreak of a deadly mutagenic virus in an isolated mountain town.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: Hellraiser
description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart , horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration. “The best horror film ever to be made in Britain.” – Melody Maker Opens Wed Oct 21, showtimes to be announced.

title: Medea (1969)
description: Returning to the well of Greek myth, Pasolini fixed on the figure of Medea, the pagan priestess loved and left behind by the questing Jason, whose story became for Pasolini a symbol of the colonization of the classical world and the vanquishing of the precious forces of the irrational. Opera star Maria Callas, not singing and barely speaking in her only dramatic role, is riveting in her interpretation of the Medea of Euripides’s tragedy, a woman manipulated by a power-hungry adventurer, driven to vengeance by deceit. Part of Classical Cinema

description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. title: Mermaids
description: It’s 1963, and different-drummer single mother Cher has decided to move from Oklahoma to smalltown Massachusetts, uprooting her two daughters, nine-year-old Kate and Catholicism-obsessed 15-year-old Rachel (Winona Ryder, who provides the narration). What follows includes JFK assassination trauma, a pregnancy scare, mother-daughter sexual competition, and one miraculous rescue, with devastating dynamic duo Cher and Ryder pushing one another to histrionic heights. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: The Great Experiment
description: Fri, Oct 16: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing, moderated by filmmaker Laura Poitras ( Citizenfour ) after 7:15 show! Sat, Oct 17: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing & True/False Fest Artistic Director Farihah Zaman, moderated by filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir after 7:15 show! title: JIGOKU
description: Shocking, outrageous and poetic, JIGOKU (HELL, a.k.a. THE SINNERS OF HELL ) is the most innovative creation from Nobuo Nakagawa, the father of the Japanese horror film. After a young theology student flees a hit-and-run accident, he is plagued by both his own guilt-ridden conscience and a mysterious, diabolical doppelgänger. But all possible escape routes lead straight to hell—literally. In the gloriously gory final third of the film, Nakagawa offers up his vision of the underworld in a tour de force of torture and degradation. A striking departure from traditional Japanese ghost stories, JIGOKU, with its truly eye-popping (and -gouging) imagery, created aftershocks that are still reverberating in contemporary world horror cinema.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: Case 137
description: Case 137 is seemingly just another case for Stéphanie, an investigator at the IGPN, the police of the police. But an unexpected element will trouble Stéphanie and transform case 137 into something more than a simple number.

title: The Sacrifice
description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s visionary final film unfolds in the hours before a nuclear holocaust. Erland Josephson, in an award-winning role, plays retired actor Alexander who is celebrating his birthday with family and friends when a crackly TV announcement warns of an imminent nuclear catastrophe. Alexander makes a promise to God that he will sacrifice all he holds dear, if the disaster can be averted. The next day dawns and, as if in a dream, everything is restored to normality. But Alexander must keep his vow. Among many other awards, The Sacrifice won the Cannes Grand Prix in 1986, the same year that Tarkovsky died of cancer in Paris at the age of 54.

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

Set against a surrealist, futuristic metropolis, the story follows Elle (Sophie Thatcher), a rising movie star preparing to shoot a space odyssey alongside her ex-lover turned stepmother (Havana Rose Liu). Elsewhere in the haze, an American GI (Charles Melton) wanders the desolate streets on a desperate search for his daughter. The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: ROSALYN DREXLER: WHO DOES SHE THINK SHE IS?
description: Rosalyn Drexler (1926-2025) was a category-defying creative force. Over the course of her multidecade career, she worked as a painter (creating some of the first examples of Pop art), a novelist, an Obie-award-winning playwright, a film critic, an occasional nightclub singer, and briefly, a professional wrestler. The documentary WHO DOES SHE THINK SHE IS? (1975) provides a window into Drexler’s extraordinary creative universe. Set against the backdrop of the lost artistic demimonde of 20th-century New York, the film – directed by Patricia Lewis Jaffe and Gaby Rodgers – shows the artist rehearsing her madcap cabaret performances, cooking for her family in her art-strewn Manhattan apartment, and speaking candidly about her art, writing, and life. As Newsweek critic Jack Kroll remarks in the film, “[Drexler’s] essential insight is that people and things are completely insane, and she speaks from inside the whale.” The documentary will be accompanied by never-before-seen home movies shot by Drexler and her husband Sherman in the 1940-50s, as well as a panel discussion. The screening coincides with a major exhibition of her work from the 1960s at Garth Greenan Gallery at 25 Greene Street; for more info about the exhibition visit: https://www.garthgreenan.com/

title: Open Art Space: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
description: Make art. Meet people. Eat snacks. Explore ideas. Be yourself. MoMA Teens Open Art Space is pleased to announce monthly teen film screenings on Thursday evenings! Join us on Thursday, October 22 from 4:00 to 7:30 p.m. for a special screening of The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975). When newly engaged couple Brad and Janet find themselves stranded on a dark and stormy night, they seek help at a mysterious mansion—and stumble into the outrageous world of Dr. Frank-N-Furter. The genre-bending musical has become a cult phenomenon celebrated for its campy humor, unforgettable characters, and gleeful celebration of the outcast and spooky. Doors open at 4:00 p.m. for snacks and hanging out before the film begins promptly at 4:30 p.m. An after-party with food and drag makeup activities will follow. Come in costume and get ready for a night of camp, cult cinema, and all things Rocky Horror. Open Art Space meets on Thursdays at MoMA’s Lewis B. and Dorothy Cullman Education and Research Building, located at 4 West 54th Street, near Fifth Avenue. This program is free and open to all high school–age participants. No previous art-making experience is necessary. Snacks, OMNY cards, and supplies will be provided. Register here. Email questions to momateens@moma.org or fill out our contact form. Accessibility The Lewis B. and Dorothy Cullman Education and Research Building entrance has a power-assist door. Seating options include chairs with backs. Gallery stools, wheelchairs, and rollators are available by request at all Museum entrances, on a first-come, first-served basis. Accessible and all-gender restrooms are located in the mezzanine level of the Lewis B. and Dorothy Cullman Education and Research Building. Guide dogs and other trained service animals are always welcome. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation and live captioning (CART) are available for public programs upon request with two weeks’ advance notice. MoMA will make every effort to provide accommodation for requests made with less than two weeks’ notice. Please email momateens@moma.org or call (212) 333-6543 to make a request for these services.

As she searches for the truth her inquiry collides with institutional resistance and pressure mounts as the case takes a personal turn when she discovers the victim is from her hometown.

title: Backrooms: Everything Must Go Edition With Bonus Footage
description: A strange doorway appears in the basement of a furniture showroom.

title: The Devils
description: Ken Russell’s infamous adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s book, about the apparent possession of a group of nuns after one (Vanessa Redgrave) accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, is at long last available in its full, uncensored splendor.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: Never Watching Movies: EMPIRE RECORDS
description: Ever wondered what it's like working in the UK's longest running cinema? Join Never Watching Movies for a special Rio Forever screening of EMPIRE RECORDS (1995) + Q&A!  Follow the story of Empire records, the coolest music store in town. After one of the employees blows the store's cash, the team fa...

title: Whalefall
description: A scuba diver in search of his deceased father's remains gets swallowed by an 80-foot, 60-ton sperm whale and has only one hour to escape before his oxygen runs out. After giving up on life, the young man is surprised to find a reason to live in the most dangerous and unlikely of places.

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: The Independent Free Thinkers: Ali & Ava
The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Solve Along A Murder She Wrote
description: Cult hit event Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote returns to the Prince Charles Cinema with an interactive screening of a classic Murder, She Wrote episode. Watch as Cabot Cove gets caught up in a murder mystery only JB Fletcher (or you!) can solve! Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. See the show Time Out rated one of 2021 and 2019’s 50 Great Nights Out in London that has played to sell-out audiences across the UK and Australia. Hosted by super-fan Tim Benzie, Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote features: * A race to solve to the crime, via the Fameometer and the Suspiciometer! * A Cabot Cove quiz! * A singalong to the theme tune with new lyrics! * Clips and biogs of the campy guest stars! Tim Benzie is obsessed with Murder, She Wrote, having watched the original series when it was first broadcast, and now relishing the repeats on television everywhere. Tim is the writer/performer of “It’s a Mystery!”, all about our love of whodunnits. An award-winning playwright and co-writer of the Royal Vauxhall Tavern’s 2017-2023 pantos (‘Goosed’, ‘Rubbed’, ‘Slipped’, ‘Pricked’, ‘Cracked’ and ‘Tossed’). He is the co-producer of the camp club night PopHorror. Visit us at www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com , or follow us on Instagram, Twitter and Facebook @solvealonga. 2026 SCHEDULE: Tuesday 8th September 2026 "Dead Man's Gold" Directed by Seymour Robbie Starring Angela Lansbury, Leslie Nielsen, Tom Bosley 1986 | 120mins | USA Thursday 22nd October 2026 Encore Halloween special - "The Witch's Curse" Directed by Jerry Jameson Starring Angela Lansbury, Robert Vaughn, Mary Crosby 1992 | 120mins | USA Thursday 26th November 2026 New episode TBC Thursday 17th December 2026 Encore screening - "A Christmas Secret" Directed by Anthony Pullen Shaw Starring Angela Lansbury, Larry Wilcox, Amy Brenneman 1992 | 120mins | USA *** The Critics speak! “You’ll be swept away with Jessica Fletcher feels … it has the BEST HOST.” - Time Out London "A cinematic, theatrical and hilarious experience ... title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: THE SOCIAL RECKONING
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the hel...

title: Street Fighter
description: Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li (Callina Liang) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
description: In 1972, legendary filmmaker William Greaves gathered an extraordinary group of artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance. After more than 50 years, his son David Greaves has completed his breathtaking miracle of a movie.

title: NAZA
description: Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

title: TOKYO DRIFTER
description:
Tetsu wants to leave the yakuza behind. Loyalty keeps dragging him back. Sent away from Tokyo, he becomes a wandering target in a gangster story that seems to shed another piece of realism with every mile.
Seijun Suzuki turns a studio assignment into pure pop-art invention: snowbound pursuits, neon nightclubs, startling colour and a final space almost abstract enough to swallow the actors. Tetsuya Watari’s cool presence and recurring theme song hold the delirium together. A crime film that dances away from the rules while still carrying a gun.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Resident Evil
description: In this sci-fi horror action reboot, a hapless medical courier fights for his life amid an outbreak of a deadly mutagenic virus in an isolated mountain town.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: Hellraiser
description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart , horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration. “The best horror film ever to be made in Britain.” – Melody Maker Opens Wed Oct 21, showtimes to be announced.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: The Great Experiment
description: Fri, Oct 16: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing, moderated by filmmaker Laura Poitras ( Citizenfour ) after 7:15 show! Sat, Oct 17: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing & True/False Fest Artistic Director Farihah Zaman, moderated by filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir after 7:15 show! What holds a people together when the story they tell about themselves begins to fracture? THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form – a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive. Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four consequential years, from 2017 to 2021, the film considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy. Additional showtimes for October 16-22 to be announced. Previously screening as part of DOC NYC Selects: Summer 2026

title: BEGOTTEN
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures:

title: Onslaught
description: A rogue team of genetically engineered super-soldiers breaks loose in the desert, forcing a tough Army sniper to fight fiercely to protect her young daughter.

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Psycho
description: Phoenix secretary Marion Crane (Janet Leigh), on the lam after stealing $40,000 from her employer in order to run away with her boyfriend, Sam Loomis (John Gavin), is overcome by exhaustion during a heavy rainstorm. Traveling on the back roads to avoid the police, she stops for the night at the ramshackle Bates Motel and meets the polite but highly strung proprietor Norman Bates (Anthony Perkins), a young man with an interest in taxidermy and a difficult relationship with his mother.

title: Rob Zombie's Halloween (2007) • Director's Cut
description: After being committed for 15 years, Michael Myers, now a grown man and still very dangerous, escapes from the mental institution and immediately returns to Haddonfield to find his baby sister, Laurie.

title: DRACULA
description: Towering ominously among the shadows of the Carpathian Mountains, Castle Dracula strikes fear in the hearts of the Transylvanian villagers below. After a naïve real estate agent succumbs to the will of Count Dracula (Bela Lugosi), the two head to London where the vampire sleeps in his coffin by day and searches for potential victims by night.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: It's Alive! Candy Kugel and Vincent Cafarelli
Tron
description: The cross-breeding of video games and cinema began in earnest with Tron, one of the first films to extensively employ CGI, here depicting the darkly glittering digital world inside a mainframe computer that programmer Jeff Bridges must compete in a series of gladiatorial contests in order to escape. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: Brief Encounter
description: Lean’s simple, tender, and terribly emotionally direct film, featuring never-better Noël Coward dialogue and a Rachmaninoff theme that grows insuperably sad with repetition, follows an affair between a middle-class couple (Celia Johnson and Trevor Howard) who happen to be inconveniently married to other people, their mutual love and mutual agony increasing over the course of seven meetings and departures that begin with a chance in a railway station buffet. One of the great screen romances, full stop. “The trains are mercilessly exact in Brief Encounter—there’s only three minutes between the departures of the trains that take Laura and Alec away from each other, and they’re never late.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue 35mm print provided courtesy of the American Genre Film Archive. Introduction by Genevieve Yue on Saturday, September 5th Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Aliens
description: When a deep-space salvage crew discovers an escape shuttle containing Ellen Ripley (Sigourney Weaver) decades after her first alien encounter, she’ll accompany a team of marines back to where the terror started. Director James Cameron ratchets up the action in his high-tension follow-up to the Ridley Scott classic, crafting one of the most pulse-pounding adventures ever sent into space: thoroughly entertaining, eminently quotable, and jam-packed with a dream team cast and an impressive array of visual effects.

title: Alantutorial
description: We will be screening the legendary youtube series Alantutorial in it's entirety!

title: The Seven Year Itch
description: One of Monroe’s most successful roles was as The Girl in director Billy Wilder’s The Seven Year Itch , a comedy about a restless husband left to his own devices for the summer. To market the film, photographer Sam Shaw proposed the indelible subway grate moment, which dozens of publicity photographers attended on location in New York City. Due to sound issues, the real scene was shot on the 20th Century-Fox lot in Los Angeles. Outside of this iconic scene, the exhibition Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon also features silk pajamas worn during a pivotal moment in developing Monroe’s girl-next-door character.
director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Charles K. Feldman, Billy Wilder

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: The Shining
description: This Stephen King adaptation crawls with atmospheric dread from the opening scene to the closing credits, inhabiting a special place in the psyche of all those who have witnessed its bloody, psychotic mastery.  Jack Nicholson stars as Jack Torrance, a down-on-his-luck writer who accepts a caretaker job at the historic Overlook Hotel. After packing up the wife and child, this family fraught with their own demons embarks on a journey of isolation, madness, and mystical mind games culminating in a terrifying fever dream. A quintessential horror from one of America’s greatest directors and one of our most popular novelists.

title: Rob Zombie's Halloween II (2009) • Director's Cut
description: Laurie Strode struggles to come to terms with her brother Michael's deadly return to Haddonfield, Illinois; meanwhile, Michael prepares for another reunion with his sister.

title: Oldboy
description: Homer with a ball-peen hammer. Kidnapped and stuffed in a hole without explanation for 15 years of solitary confinement, when Oh Dae-su (Choi Min-sik) is suddenly let loose on the streets, he’s stone-cold pissed off and very, very dangerous. Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes and an international pop phenomenon, Oldboy was a revenge thriller unlike any that had come before, featuring passages of pure bravura filmmaking (that one-shot hallway donnybrook!) and surreal sicko humor that’ll put you off of sushi for a while. “Put together with brutally uncompromising style [and] the cold-steel edge of a knife against your throat. A dark and thrillingly horrible adventure into the realms of the unthinkable.” —The Guardian Part of Classical Cinema

title: Strangers on a Train
description: “Criss cross.” Hitchcock’s adaptation of Highsmith’s 1951 page-turner kicks off with a casual encounter that reads like a same-sex pickup, as tennis star Guy Haines (Farley Granger) inadvertently agrees to “swap murders” with preening rich kid Bruno Anthony (Robert Walker, in a career performance), and continues through some of the finest set pieces of Hitch’s career: a tennis match at Forest Hills, Bruno stalking his prey through a vulgar county fair, and an out-of-control carousel. “In Hitchcock, the people you meet on trains can spell romance, adventure, or, in the case of Strangers on a Train’s Guy Haines, a colossal headache! Tip: beware anyone wearing spectator shoes.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: WINGS
description: Decades before TOP GUN, there was WINGS, establishing atrial battle sequences that still rank among the best in motion picture history. Meticulously restored and featuring a dynamic soundtrack based on the original score, this timeless story of love and loss follows two men who go to war, and the girl they leave behind. The first Oscar winner for Best Picture, this grand spectacle from the early days of cinema features “It-girl” Clara Bow alongside Richard Arlen, Charles “Buddy” Rogers and Gary Cooper in a legendary cameo appearance.

title: ANATOMY OF HELL
description:
A woman invites a man she meets at a nightclub to spend several days with her in a remote seaside house, offering him money to observe her in private moments of intimacy and vulnerability. What begins as an unusual arrangement becomes an increasingly confrontational exchange about desire, disgust, power, and the limits of looking.
Anatomy of Hell is a deliberately austere and confrontational dialogue between two bodies and two perspectives, stripping away narrative comfort in favour of philosophical provocation. The film’s static framing and clinical tone push its themes of sex, shame, and perception into uncomfortable territory, forcing attention onto gaze and reaction rather than conventional plot.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Oldest Person in the World
description: Join us in the microcinema for an-all-too-human triumph of documentary filmmaking, Sam Greene’s profound and entertaining affirmation of life, The Oldest Person in the World. Green creates a decade-long odyssey chronicling the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. As the title inevitably passes from one supercentenarian to the next, acclaimed filmmaker Sam Green traverses the globe to meet each new record holder, his personal fascination with what the title means becoming entangled with events and milestones in his own life. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.

title: Freaked
description: Selected by Sammy Harkham: “A movie to see if you love drugs or have a large collection of mad magazines or listen to 90s hard rock or jack off to Basil Wolverton drawings or jack off to Gumby jacking off or laugh at Will Elder’s chicken fat or rent movies if Screaming Mad George is in the credits or watch YouTube clips of old borscht belt comedians or only like Steve Johnson when he’s more coked out than usual or you think Randy Quaid is under appreciated or you just like watching kids falling out of airplanes, Freaked is for YOU.”

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari with Live Score
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max The rich timbre of the viola perfectly captures the aura of Robert Wiene's The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari. My improvisations translate the film's angular painted shadows into unnerving melodies inspired by musical techniques that were evolving during the 1920s. The nefarious showmanship of Caligari invites theatrical and macabre sounds, in contrast with ghostly gestures evoking ‘the somnambulist' who is compelled to act against his will. THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI : One of the most iconic masterpieces in cinema history, Robert Wiene's Das Cabinet des Dr Caligari shook filmgoers worldwide and changed the direction of the art form. Now presented in a definitive restoration, the film's chilling, radically expressionist vision is set to grip viewers again. At a local carnival in a small German town, hypnotist Dr. Caligari presents the somnambulist Cesare, who can purportedly predict the future of curious fairgoers. But at night, the doctor wakes Cesare from his sleep to enact his evil bidding… Incalculably influential, the film's nightmarishly jagged sets, sinister atmospheric and psychological emphasis left an immediate impact in its wake (horror, film noir, and gothic cinema would all be shaped directly by it).

title: Virgina
description: When a fourth daughter is born to a family “cursed” by superstition to bear no male heirs, the decision is made to raise the child with a boy’s name—Stevan—as well as a man’s rights and responsibilities… though as Stevan passes adolescence, first love and a brush with personal tragedy will spark rebellion in his breast. An acutely observed study of a 19th-century peasant culture steeped in misogyny, and a strikingly sensual story of self-discovery, presented in a new 2K restoration in its NYC premiere. “I’ve gotten to do many cool and amazing things in my work over the years, but tracking down the negative of Virgina, after the director Srđan Karanović thought it had been lost in the aftermath of the Yugoslav Wars, is definitely one of the highlights of my career. Virgina is a stunning film, a complex and interesting narrative about gender, with unique pleasures for a queer audience.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist The new 2K restoration was completed by the Department for Digitisation and Digital Restoration of the Yugoslav Film Archive in Belgrade. The film was scanned from a 35mm internegative using an ArriscanXT scanner with archival gate overscan, with color correction by Masha Badalić under the supervision of director Srđan Karanović. Audio was sourced from the original 35mm mono sound negative and restored by the Sound Department of the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad. An Altered Innocence release Introduction and post-screening discussion by Jenni Olson on Friday, October 23rd Introduction by Jenni Olson on Saturday, October 24th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: Halloween (1978)
description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: All That Heaven Allows
description: Perhaps the very finest of Sirk’s Ross Hunter-produced melodramas, All That Heaven Allows pairs Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson as, respectively, a well-off widow in country club Connecticut, and the broad-necked, Thoreau-reading gardener who she falls for. Her priggish children, aghast, conspire to break off the pairing, an endeavor that ends in a bone-chilling Christmas conciliation—the presentation of a gift television set as a kind of death sentence. Of this scene Rainer Werner Fassbinder, profoundly marked by his encounter with Sirk’s film, would write: “At that point everyone in the moviehouse breaks down. They suddenly understand something about the world and what it does to people.” Right on. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: CHAMPAGNE AND BULLETS
description:
Former police officer Rick Bode is forced from the department after refusing to participate in the schemes of corrupt judge Norman. Reunited with his old partner Huck, Rick sets out to expose a criminal network involving blackmail, murder and a satanic cult. Along the way he finds time for romance, martial arts, country music, spiritual contemplation and the irresistible dance sensation known as the Shimmy Slide.
Written, produced by and starring John De Hart, CHAMPAGNE AND BULLETS is an extraordinary vanity-project action epic whose ambition is matched only by its profound eccentricity. Its awkward dialogue, sudden tonal shifts and complete sincerity have made it a cult phenomenon, especially in its alternate incarnation as GETEVEN. Far more than a conventional bad-movie curiosity, this is personal cinema in its purest and most bewildering form.

title: Possible Love (15)
description: South Korea’s master filmmaker Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry ) returns with an intertwined drama on two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires.

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood (70mm)
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
description: One, two… Freddy’s coming for you! The teenagers on Elm Street are having a hard time sleeping – some creep with knives for fingers keeps terrorizing them in their dreams. When her friends begin to die off one by one, Nancy Thompson has got to find a way to track the madman in her own nightmares in order to stop him once and for all in the waking world. Wes Craven’s original nightmare and the start of a monstrous 20-year franchise, this first installment of Freddy remains the most terrifying of the series and is considered one of the best horror movies of all time. So, get your hall pass and head down to the boiler room, because the man of your dreams is waiting for you!

title: The George Stevens Lecture on Directing presents Giant in 4K
description: George Stevens ( A Place in the Sun , 1951) earned his second Directing Oscar for this character-centered adaptation of Edna Ferber’s 1952 bestseller about wealthy Texan Jordan “Bick” Benedict Jr. (Rock Hudson); his blueblood bride, Leslie (Elizabeth Taylor); and ambitious ranch hand Jett (James Dean, in his final performance). Visionary for its depictions of progressive social justice themes and Taylor’s bold depiction of a staunch feminist, Giant is an epic story that spans generations and tackles the conflicting mores that governed behavior in America during the first half of the 20th century. Alongside Stevens’s win for Directing, the film received 10 Oscar nominations , including Best Picture, Supporting Actress (Mercedes McCambridge), two Best Actor nominations for James Dean and Rock Hudson, as well as for Dimitri Tiomkin’s original score, in what was the composer’s only collaboration with Stevens. Initiated in 1982, the George Stevens Lecture on Directing was the first of the Academy’s ongoing lectures dedicated to the art of filmmaking. For this edition, six-time Academy Award-nominated cinematographer Caleb Deschanel joins us to discuss Giant ’s visual language and social impact before the screening, which is presented in a beautiful, 4K restoration. Programmed by K.J. Relth-Miller.
director: George Stevens PRODUCED BY: George Stevens, Henry Ginsberg

title: CLOSURE
description: After his teenage son, Chris, is last seen by a surveillance camera on a bridge over Warsaw’s turbulent Vistula River, Daniel embarks on an all-consuming search. Armed with self-built boats, drones and underwater cameras, he relentlessly scours the river’s depths. As months pass, while his own family struggles to live with the uncertainty of Chris’s disappearance, Daniel begins helping other families with missing loved ones find answers – and, at times, the closure that continues to elude him.

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
Imperium
description: Imperium. 2026. Germany/Italy/France/Lithuania. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. North American premiere. DCP courtesy Coproduction Office. In Russian, Ukrainian, Kazakh, Uzbek, Georgian, other indigenous languages of the Eastern Soviet Union; English subtitles. 175 min. MoMA presents the North American premiere of Imperium, Sergei Loznitsa’s newest work, an epic vision of the Soviet Union drawn from footage shot in the early 1970s by an Italian communist film crew. Films across the century—including Dziga Vertov’s A Sixth Part of the World (1926), Mikhail Kalatozov’s Salt for Svanetia (1930), and Uldis Brauns, Biruta Veldre, and Laima Zurgina’s 235 000 000 (1967)—have tried to capture the vast and diverse empire that was the Soviet Union, from the Saami people in the icy northern climes to the heat-tortured Uzbek in the landlocked south. Intending to make a monumental television series as a corrective to the Western image of the USSR, the film crew, perhaps by virtue of their Leninist-Marxist bona fides, was granted access to the farthest reaches of the territory by Soviet authorities, from the Arctic Circle and the Caucasus Mountains to the deserts of Central Asia. (Somehow the gulags were closed off to them.) In the end, only a few episodes were broadcast, and only now, 55 years later, has Loznitsa mined the archives for a more multifaceted vision of “A Sixth Part of the World,” the bombastic phrase coined by Imperial Russians and then taken up after the First World War by a “newer,” “more efficient,” and “happier” Soviet empire. Imperium is a densely woven tapestry of contrasts and contradictions that allows subtle critiques of colonialism, collectivization, and basic human want to creep in: the expression of Indigenous folkloric traditions and languages in the face of cultural erasure (including Ukrainian speech, as Loznitsa wryly notes), of fashion shows and department stores offering unattainable luxury goods, and of Christmas ceremonies in Russian Orthodox churches and prayer in Islamic mosques despite the official policy of atheism in this supposedly “godless utopia.” What astonishes is not so much that the Kremlin was able to hold it all together for so long but that ancient customs and peoples stubbornly resisted some 75 years of forced labor, dogma, and terror. Russia today is another story altogether.

title: Colony
description: Our microcinema is going to the undead with horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s ( Train to Busan ) new Korean zombie thriller starring Gianna Jun and Koo Kyo-hwan. Professor Se-jeong (Jun) is thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. With new and fascinating ideas that bring the zombie genre into brilliant new territory of collective consciousness and mold networks, and the kind of action and pathos Yeon Sang-ho is best at, this is a no brainer for any horrorphile!

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: A new kind of horror remake from Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ), starring Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson. After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium. (MUBI)

title: Vampires with Memoirs of an Invisible Man
description: Vampires in 4K Based on John Steakley’s novel of the same name, John Carpenter’s Vampires is the master of horror’s sole foray into the realm of vampirism. The film may be full of style and tropes influenced by classic Westerns, including a setting in New Mexico, but the heroes brandish wooden stakes and crossbows instead of rifles and six-shooters. Jack Crow (James Woods) leads a team of grizzled, Vatican-sponsored vampire hunters who seek to exterminate Valek (Thomas Ian Griffith), the first vampire, now on a quest to gain immunity from the sun. Balancing action and one-liners with scares and gore, all set to a Carpenter score, Vampires is a fresh, contemporary take on the classic monsters of Universal and Hammer horror fame.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Sandy King

title: THE EXORCIST
description: William Friedkin directs one of the most horrifying movies ever made. When a charming 12-year-old girl takes on the characteristics and voices of others, doctors say there is nothing they can do. As people begin to die, the girl’s mother realizes her daughter has been possessed by the devil–and that her daughter’s only possible hope lies with two priests and the ancient rite of demonic exorcism.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors
description: A psychiatrist, familiar with the knife-wielding dream demon Freddy Krueger, helps teens at a mental hospital battle the killer who is invading their dreams.

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

title: Scooby-Dooble Feature
description: Don't miss the return of the original SCOOBY-DOOBLE FEATURE : featuring the loveable 2002 live-action adaptation of the classic Hanna-Barbera cartoon series, SCOOBY-DOO , and its 2004 sequel, SCOOBY DOO 2: MONSTERS UNLEASHED , back-to-back from 35mm prints in one night! Accept no imitations! SCOOBY-DOO (2002) : Zoinks! Two years after a clash of egos forced Mystery Inc. to close its doors, Scooby-Doo and his clever crime-solving cohorts Fred (Freddie Prinze Jr.), Daphne (Sarah Michelle Gellar), Shaggy (Matthew Lillard) and Velma (Linda Cardellini) are individually summoned to Spooky Island to investigate a series of paranormal incidents at the ultra-hip Spring Break hot spot. SCOOBY-DOO 2: MONSTERS UNLEASHED (2004) : In this live-action sequel, the lovable dog Scooby-Doo once again joins his pals Shaggy (Matthew Lillard), Velma (Linda Cardellini), Fred (Freddie Prinze Jr.) and Daphne (Sarah Michelle Gellar) as they stumble into another seemingly supernatural mystery. In addition to facing off against various monsters that are tormenting their town, the gang must deal with television journalist Heather Jasper-Howe (Alicia Silverstone), who is out to discredit their investigations.

title: Alantutorial
description: We will be screening the legendary youtube series Alantutorial in it's entirety!

title: Almost Famous
description: Before breaking into movies with his screenplay for Fast Times at Ridgemont High, Cameron Crowe was a teenage journalist with a regular byline in Rolling Stone magazine in the hedonistic early 1970s, and he draws from a deep well of memories of those pot-hazy days in his poignant-funny, semi-autobiographical Almost Famous, starring Patrick Fugit as a fresh-faced rock rag writer on the road with hesher idols Stillwater, Kate Hudson as road-warrior Stillwater superfan “Penny Lane,” and Philip Seymour Hoffman as an impassioned, opinionated, marvelously disheveled Lester Bangs. “In Almost Famous, a loose, affectionate look back on his earlier career as a teenage music journalist, Mr. Crowe has devoted a whole movie to the love of rock 'n' roll. The soul he lays open—a sweet, forgiving and generous one—is his own … He may be the least cynical director working in Hollywood today.” —A.O. Scott, The New York Times Introduction by Jon Caramanica and Joe Coscarelli of “Popcast” on Friday, October 16th Part of The New York Times presents Stop the Presses

title: DOC'N ROLL: NOFX: 40 YEARS OF F*N’ UP!
description: 40 Years of Fuckin' Up is Spinal Tap, but real. It's a film about the infamous, fairly un-famous, and beloved punk rock band NOFX. This is the unbelievable story about how a group of untalented drug-addled teenage punks somehow became the most successful independent band in history. And they did it ...

title: Night on Earth
description: Jarmusch’s career-long fascination with at-home-in-the-world wanderers finds its perfect expression in this anthology piece with a Tom Waits soundtrack and Independent Spirit Award-winning cinematography by Elmes, set simultaneously in five different cabs in five different cities around the world. In Los Angeles casting agent Gena Rowlands cross-examines driver Winona Ryder, Isaach De Bankolé drives a mysterious young blind woman through Paris, and the backseat operates everywhere as an analyst’s sofa, loneliness and urban anomie proving to know no national bounds. “Mr. Jarmusch again demonstrates his mastery of comedy of the oblique.”—The New York Times Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Halloween III: Season of the Witch
description: After a terrified toy salesman is mysteriously attacked and brought to the hospital clutching the year's most popular Halloween mask, Dr. Daniel Challis sets out to investigate the strange events and finds himself thrust into a nightmarish conspiracy.

title: Klara and the Sun
description:
Based on the bestselling novel from Nobel Prize-winner Kazuo Ishiguro and written and directed by Academy-Award® winner Taika Waititi. 

Klara is an artificial intelligence friend who wants nothing more than to find the perfect home. It soon meets Josie, a young woman who has a fraught relationship with her mother. But Klara's innocent wonder and unwavering loyalty soon start to heal the family and bring some light to Josie's complicated world.

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: MYSTERY EROTIC HORROR
description:
Mystery Erotic Horror presents undisclosed deep cuts from cinema’s most feverish and forbidden corners - where desire collides with religious mania, occult ritual, sadism and bloodshed. Expect perverse passions, sacrilegious imagery, decadent excess and exquisitely bad decisions, as sex and death become dangerously intertwined. Come blind, surrender to the mystery and discover a film you may never otherwise have thought to see.
These screenings are strictly for adult audiences and may contain explicit sexual content, violence and other potentially offensive material. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition. Adults only.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Hellraiser
description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart , horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration. “The best horror film ever to be made in Britain.” – Melody Maker Opens Wed Oct 21, showtimes to be announced.

title: Mimic
description: Don’t bug out – we’ve got the creature feature your Friday night has been missing – a Guillermo del Toro giant mutant cockroach movie starring Mira Sorvino and international superstar Giancarlo Giannini! After wiping out a massive population of disease-carrying cockroaches in Manhattan with a genetically engineered mutant cockroach breed, scientists discover they’ve created something much more deadly – an enormous breed of bug that can mimic the human form. If you’ve been waiting for the time to watch Oscar winners battle giant bugs on our big screen, your wait is over!

title: A SERBIAN FILM
description: Milos, a retired porn star, leads a normal family life with his wife Maria and six-year old son Petar in tumultuous Serbia, trying to make ends meet. A sudden call from his former colleague Layla will change everything. Aware of his financial problems, Layla introduces Milos to Vukmir – a mysterious, menacing and politically powerful figure in the pornographic business. A leading role in Vukmir’s production will provide financial support to Milos and his family for the rest of their lives. A contract insists on his absolute unawareness of a script they will shoot. From then on, Milos is drawn into a maelstrom of unbelievable cruelty and mayhem devised by his employer, “the director” of his destiny. Vukmir and his cohorts will stop at nothing to complete his vision. In order to escape the living cinematic hell he’s put into, and save his family’s life, Milos will have to sacrifice everything – his pride, his morality, his sanity and maybe even his own life.

title: Ju-on: The Grudge
description: When a social worker is sent to check on a traumatized elderly woman whose family have moved in at the site of a notorious murder case, she unwittingly unleashes a cycle of terror that transmits via its victims.

title: Rushmore
description: Extracurricular-mad but otherwise unpromising 15-year-old student Max Fisher (Jason Schwartzman) is too busy competing (or so he thinks) with sad sack industrialist Bill Murray for the affections of teacher Olivia Williams to survive “sudden death academic probation” in Anderson’s deeply funny, deeply melancholic—and very class-conscious—sophomore feature. A back-to-school perennial, all dressed up in prep school navy blue and the muted colors of north Texas autumn, positively thrumming with the upstart energy of British Invasion anthems. (“Anderson,” noted admirer Martin Scorsese, “has a fine sense of how music works against an image.”) An irresistible, disarmingly original, delicately wrought comic fable. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
description: An ardent aficionado of the work of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, Cushing takes over the chambers at 221B Baker Street with aplomb and gives us a Sherlock for the ages in Fisher’s adaptation of the 1902 Holmes adventure of the same name, in which our hero is called to Dartmoor to investigate the mysterious death-by-fright of one Sir Charles Baskerville, leaving his estate in the hands of his heir and nephew, Henry (Christopher Lee). With the invaluable assistance of Jack Asher’s subdued Technicolor photography, Fisher wrings every drop of atmosphere out of Doyle’s tale of mist-shrouded moors and ancestral curses, making this one of Holmes’s very finest big-screen outings. (Special mention is due to Fisher’s ingenious use of child stand-ins for his leads to establish the terrible proportions of the eponymous mastiff.) Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: Creepshow
description: Five grisly tales from a kid's comic book about a murdered father rising from his grave, a bizarre meteor, a vengeful husband, a mysterious crate's occupant, and a plague of cockroaches.

title: Category H: THE LURE + PHANTOM OF THE PARADISE
description: Warm up your vocal chord for the October edition of Category H’s Rio Forever/Rio Never Ever season screening, we are bringing you Musical Madness with a late night of horror musicals THE LURE X PHANTOM OF THE PARADISE. Screening for this Halloween season on the 23rd of October, and join us at 23:30 ...

title: From Dusk Till Dawn
description: George Clooney and Quentin Tarantino star as brothers on the lam from the law, hightailing it to Mexico with a kidnapped family in tow. But when they stop at an isolated strip club, they’ll have to try and survive From Dusk Till Dawn while battling the bar’s bloodthirsty denizens in Robert Rodriguez’s pulpy, stylish & hyper-violent cross-genre blast penned by its co-star. Featuring Harvey Keitel, Juliette Lewis & Salma Hayek plus an all-star cast of character actor greats including Cheech Marin, Fred Williamson, Danny Trejo and Tom Savini!

title: Onslaught
description: A rogue team of genetically engineered super-soldiers breaks loose in the desert, forcing a tough Army sniper to fight fiercely to protect her young daughter.

title: Rodan
description: A mining engineer investigates the deaths of his colleagues, discovering prehistoric nymphs and a creature capable of flying - and wreaking havoc - at supersonic speeds.

title: Hackney Children’s Film Fest: THE WILD ROBOT
description: Hackney Children’s Film Festival | Sat 24 - Sat 31 October Tickets £5 or £3 with a Hackney Library Card A Rio Cinema Project  The kids have waited long enough! This October half term, the Rio brings Hackney its first ever Children's Film Festival, with a lively and enchanting film programme curated ...

title: Parent & Baby Screening: Possible Love (15)
description: South Korea’s master filmmaker Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry ) returns with an intertwined drama on two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires.

title: Hotel Transylvania
description: A hapless young backpacker (voiced by Andy Samberg) stumbles upon an Eastern European resort and falls for the owner’s daughter (Selena Gomez), unaware that he’s discovered a hotel for monsters and that his prospective father-in-law is Dracula himself. Adam Sandler leads the stellar comedic voice cast as the Count, with Kevin James as Frankenstein’s monster, Fran Drescher as his bride, Steve Buscemi as a werewolf, and David Spade as the Invisible Man. Director Genndy Tartakovsky’s inventive visuals are an ideal match for the script’s winning mixture of humor and sentiment. The film would spawn three sequels and a TV series.
director: Genndy Tartakovsky PRODUCED BY: Michelle Murdocca

title: The Aristocats
description: A big-screen outing for this flight of feline fun from the Disney vaults, the last animated feature to be signed off on by Walt himself is a purr-fect Parisian period piece featuring a family of nose-in-the-air cats who, after being kidnapped away from the accustomed baronial splendor of their home, have to rely on the streetwise wiles of alley cat O’Malley to keep them safe. Featuring animation supremely attentive to the syntax of kitty motion and the vocal talents of Eva Gabor and Scatman Crothers who gets to lead on the boppin' classic “Everybody Wants to Be a Cat.” Part of It Started With A Mouse: Hand-Drawn Classics on 35

title: Medea (1988)
description: Based on an unfilmed screenplay by Carl Theodor Dreyer and, of course, Euripides’s tragedy of the same title, von Trier’s made-for-television film—save for two epiphanic eruptions—is uncharacteristically austere, the enfant terrible of Danish cinema making himself a medium for the Old Master’s vision, setting the source material in a pre-Christian Denmark. “An experimental film in the true sense of the word… Taking the greatest limitation of video—the medium’s lack of depth of field—Mr. von Trier turns it into a strength, flattening perspectives in a way that collapses his foreground characters into the tumultuous backgrounds (waves, wind-swept fields) that surround and dominate them.” —Dave Kehr, The New York Times Part of Classical Cinema

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Mummy [1999]
description: The Mummy is a rousing, suspenseful and horrifying epic about an expedition of treasure-seeking explorers in the Sahara Desert in 1925. Stumbling upon an ancient tomb, the hunters unwittingly set loose a 3,000-year-old legacy of terror, which is embodied in the vengeful reincarnation of an Egyptian priest who had been sentenced to an eternity as one of the living dead.

title: The Flavor of Green Tea Over Rice
description: Ozu’s satirical—and ultimately quite touching—portrait of a marriage first seen in a state of quiet unraveling stars Kogure Michiyo and Saburi Shin as a well-off, childless middle-aged couple who find discreet outlets to express their disappointments and resentments towards one another: the Westernized wife through habitual practice of harmless deceptions and put-downs of the husband that she likens to a sluggish carp in a koi pond; her husband by supporting a niece (Keiko Tsushima) in her flight from proposed marriage arrangement interviews. “There’s stillness, and then there’s Ozu stillness. After an argument with her husband, Taeko sets off on a train journey. The stops sweep by, but she doesn’t take notice. Defiantly, petulantly, and a bit woefully, she sits.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: BROADWAY MELODY OF 1940
description: Fred Astaire, Eleanor Powell and George Murphy sing and dance to the music of Cole Porter in this musical spectacular about the problems that arise when the wrong partner of a ballroom dance team lands a starring role on the Great White Way in BROADWAY MELODY OF 1940.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Elisa, My Life
description: After a 20-year separation, Elisa (Chaplin) reunites with her father, Luis, who walked out on the family long ago—the aging author is played by Buñuel regular and Spanish national treasure Fernando Rey, in a performance that earned him Best Actor plaudits at the Cannes Film Festival. An intoxicating whorl of memory, fantasy—in his literary output Luis dwells on his daughter’s imagined life, depicted here along with her own daydreams—and hard-to-swallow reality, in which an act of mandatory “reconciliation” becomes an unveiling of terrible, naked grief. “As in all of her Saura films, [Chaplin] reveals qualities of feeling, control and beauty that no other directors have ever found.” —The New York Times Part of The Remembered Lives of G. Chaplin & C. Saura

title: Hotel Transylvania
description: Pack a bag, grab the family, and head to Vidiots for the vacation of your deathtime! Welcome to Hotel Transylvania , Dracula’s lavish five-stake resort, where monsters and their families can live it up and no humans are allowed. One special weekend, Dracula has invited all his best friends to celebrate his beloved daughter Mavis’s 118th birthday. For Dracula catering to all of these legendary monsters is no problem but the party really starts when one ordinary guy stumbles into the hotel and changes everything! Bring your little monster-lovers for this super fun monster mash!

title: Monster House
description: Monsters under the bed are scary enough, but what happens when an entire house is out to get you? Three teens aim to find out when they go up against a decrepit neighboring home and unlock its frightening secrets.

title: Klara and the Sun
description:
Based on the bestselling novel from Nobel Prize-winner Kazuo Ishiguro and written and directed by Academy-Award® winner Taika Waititi. 

Klara is an artificial intelligence friend who wants nothing more than to find the perfect home. It soon meets Josie, a young woman who has a fraught relationship with her mother. But Klara's innocent wonder and unwavering loyalty soon start to heal the family and bring some light to Josie's complicated world.

title: The Cat and the Canary (1939)
description: You’ll shiver with fright and shake with laughter! Even your goosepimples will have goosepimples! Following the death of an eccentric millionaire, six family members convene at his decaying old mansion for the reading of his will. But when it’s discovered that the sole inheritor (Paulette Goddard) will relinquish her new fortune if she goes insane, it’s up to a wise-cracking Bob Hope to make sure she keeps her mind and survives the night. The Cat and the Canary is Bob Hope at his best, laughing his way through hilarious heroics and hoping a gag’s as good as a gun to get ghosts on the go!

title: THE SHINING
description: Jack Nicholson and Shelley Duvall star in director Stanley Kubrick’s disturbing adaptation of Stephen King’s blockbuster horror novel. When writer Jack Torrance (Nicholson)–who has a history of alcoholism and child abuse–takes a job as winter caretaker for a hotel high in the Rocky Mountains, he, his wife (Duvall) and their psychic young son will be isolated until spring. But once the first blizzard closes the road out, the accumulated power of evil deeds committed at the hotel begins to drive Jack mad. Now there may be no escape for his wife and son in this haunting madness, memory and family violence.

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Hackney Children's Film Fest: Young Neurospicy: Family Shorts
description: Hackney Children’s Film Festival | Sat 24 - Sat 31 October Tickets £5 or £3 with a Hackney Library Card A Rio Cinema Project  The kids have waited long enough! This October half term, the Rio brings Hackney its first ever Children's Film Festival, with a lively and enchanting film programme curated ...

title: Blade
description: A vampire hunter known as Blade (Wesley Snipes) uses his superhuman abilities to protect humanity from neck-biting undead under the guidance of mentor Abraham Whistler (Kris Kristofferson). The half-undead, half-human daywalker also seeks revenge for his mother’s murder at the hands of a vampire during her pregnancy. Based on the comic book series of the same name, Blade was the first film produced by Marvel Studios. An unexpected box-office success, the film helped pave the way for the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Snipes’s undeniable charisma as the leather-clad slayer and his decades of training in martial arts helped cement the character’s place in pop culture.
director: Stephen Norrington PRODUCED BY: Peter Frankfurt, Wesley Snipes, Robert Engelman

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events.
