When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: THE BABY
description:
Set in Los Angeles, The Baby follows Ann Gentry, a social worker assigned to investigate the unusual Wadsworth household. Living there is a fully grown man known only as “Baby,” who is treated by his domineering mother and manipulative sisters as if he were still an infant. He is kept in a crib, dressed in diapers, and discouraged from developing beyond a childlike state. As Ann spends more time with the family, she becomes increasingly disturbed by the strange dynamics and psychological control that keep Baby trapped in permanent infancy.
Blending psychological horror with dark melodrama, The Baby explores themes of power, dependency, and manipulation within a deeply dysfunctional family. As Ann attempts to intervene and free Baby from his abusive environment, hidden motives and unsettling secrets begin to surface. The story builds toward a shocking twist that forces the audience to reconsider the characters and their intentions, leaving the boundaries between victim and perpetrator disturbingly unclear.

title: Peppermint Frappé
description: Chaplin and Saura’s electric creative partnership began with this perverse play on Alfred Hitchcock’s (already quite perverse!) Vertigo, in which meek doctor José Luis López Vázquez becomes besotted with his childhood friend’s bride (Chaplin), and sets about making over a doting assistant (Chaplin, again) at the radiology clinic where he works into the image of the woman he yearns for but cannot have. A delirious and seriously deviant psychological thriller. “I got home quite late and turned on the television; a film in Spanish with subtitles, that I knew absolutely nothing about... It was hard for me to follow and understand but, at the same time, I was convinced it was the film of a great director. I watched the rest of the film glued to the TV set and when it was over I picked up a newspaper and saw that it was Peppermint Frappé.” —Stanley Kubrick Part of The Remembered Lives of G. Chaplin & C. Saura

title: We're All Going to the World's Fair
description: Reality and fantasy begin to blur when a teenager, alone in her attic bedroom, immerses herself in a role-playing horror game online.

title: Something Special (Willy/Milly)
description: Frustrated by a world in which boys seem to get the best of everything, 14-year-old Milly (Pamela Adlon) makes a wish to swap her sex, and wakes up to find her—or, rather, his—wish has come true. “In my obsession with Something Special, I purchased this 35mm print of it almost 30 years ago. There are a handful of ‘teenage girls passing as boys’ films (She’s the Man is probably the best known). In so many films with gender-crossing characters, the passing is so unconvincing that it renders the film ultimately unsatisfying for a queer audience. But Pamela Adlon’s performance here as Willy is absolutely spectacular.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist Introduction and post-screening discussion by Jenni Olson moderated by filmmaker, film critic and writer Drew Burnett Gregory on Saturday, October 24th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: Get in the spooky spirit with a trip to the delightful nightmare world of Halloween Town with Jack Skellington and his gruesome band of ghoulfriends. Tired of the monotony of scaring humans every October 31 with the same old bag of tricks, Jack Skellington, the spindly king of Halloween Town, has a plan to kidnap Santa Claus and turn Christmas creepy. But as the winter holiday approaches, Jack’s rag-doll girlfriend, Sally, tries to foil his misguided plans and bring back Christmas merriment. A stop-motion delight for everyone with extraordinary animation, iconic songs, and a whole world of creepy creatures to fall in love with!

title: The Craft
description: “We are the freaks.” Black lipstick, Wicca, and Catholic school angst — THE CRAFT is CARRIE by way of CLUELESS. When troubled teen Sarah (Robin Tunney, EMPIRE RECORDS) transfers to a new high school in LA, she is quickly befriended by a trio rumored to be witches — Bonnie (Neve Campbell, SCREAM), Rochelle (Rachel True, NOWHERE), and Nancy (Fairuza Balk, AMERICAN HISTORY X). It is not long before the spells and curses cast by the budding coven take on a life of their own. Less content to rest on hijinks and popularity contests than its contemporaries, the script by FLATLINERS scribe, Peter Filardi, crafts a broody atmosphere as thick as its protagonist’s eyeliner and continues to resonate with girl gangs and misfits who’ve long outgrown the braces and rosary combo. Co-starring Skeet Ulrich (SCREAM) and Breckin Meyer (ROADTRIP). Screening in 35mm!

title: THE BLACK CAULDRON
description: Fantasy, magic and fun are all brewed together in this legendary adventure. Whoever releases the mysterious Black Cauldron’s power will be invincible. The fearsome Horned King will do anything to possess it, but he is challenged by the most unlikely adversary: a young assistant pig keeper named Taran, who dreams of doing heroic deeds. With a motley team including the brave Princess Eilonwy, a minstrel named Fflewddur Fflam and Hen Wen, a remarkable pig who can predict the future, Taran embarks on a quest to stop the Black Cauldron’s evil once and for all. Will he have the courage to succeed?

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
HACKNEY CHILDREN'S FILM FEST: Paddington & Storytime
description: Hackney Children’s Film Festival | Sat 24 - Sat 31 October Tickets £5 or £3 with a Hackney Library Card A Rio Cinema Project  The kids have waited long enough! This October half term, the Rio brings Hackney its first ever Children's Film Festival, with a lively and enchanting film programme curated ...

title: My Joy (СЧАСТЬЕ МОЕ)
description: My Joy (СЧАСТЬЕ МОЕ). 2010. Germany/Ukraine/Netherlands. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. With Viktor Nemets, Vlad Ivanov, Olga Shuvalova. DCP courtesy Kino Lorber. In Russian; English subtitles. 128 min. The first Ukrainian film ever to compete in the main competition at Cannes, My Joy opens, cryptically, with a corpse, a shakedown, a child prostitute, and a ballad from the Soviet-Afghan War. Ostensibly a circular road movie involving the strange and haunting tribulations of a taciturn truck driver, Sergei Loznitsa’s debut fiction feature treats Russian history like a festering trauma—the Hobbesian fable, though not without gallows humor, of a nation afflicted with the sins of war, occupation, and corruption. Loznitsa crowds his images with layers of activity and meaning, through grimy windshields and across bleak unloved landscapes, leaving the audience to puzzle through the film’s elliptical chronology, its many compulsive acts of brutality and occasional acts of thankless charity, the scowling faces of strangers full of menace or guile, and the identities of characters who are used, abused, and summarily dispensed with, only to resurface in mysterious and enigmatic ways.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: BLACK DEVIL DOLL FROM HELL (ON VHS)
description:
A lonely and pious woman finds herself drawn to a mysterious antique doll whose malevolent influence quickly escalates from unsettling pranks to violent, supernatural terror. As the doll’s control tightens, her life spirals into chaos, and those around her fall victim to its relentless, demonic will.
A shot on video masterpiece from former church organist, Chester N. Turner, Black Devil Doll from Hell revels in low-budget excess and devilish theatrics. The film leans into grotesque violence, uncanny puppetry, and unrepentant exploitation, creating a nightmarish energy that is as absurd as it is frightening.

title: The Oldest Person in the World
description: Join us in the microcinema for an-all-too-human triumph of documentary filmmaking, Sam Greene’s profound and entertaining affirmation of life, The Oldest Person in the World. Green creates a decade-long odyssey chronicling the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. As the title inevitably passes from one supercentenarian to the next, acclaimed filmmaker Sam Green traverses the globe to meet each new record holder, his personal fascination with what the title means becoming entangled with events and milestones in his own life. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.

title: Perfect Blue
description: A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show.

title: ACE Presents: Rosemary's Baby
description: “He has his father’s eyes…” Satanists are on the loose in Central Park West in Polanski’s slow-burn thriller, which slips almost imperceptibly from the quotidian into the profane, and gives new meaning to the phrase “pregnancy scare.” Young marrieds Mia Farrow and John Cassavetes make friendly with their elder neighbors Ruth Gordon and Sidney Blackmer, but when Farrow’s abandoned and isolated Rosemary goes into a paranoiac tailspin while expecting her first child, she begins to wonder why everyone is so very eager for her to take her daily dosage of tannis root… A masterclass in slow-building, spine-tingling suspense, aided immeasurably by the dab-handed work of legendary editor Sam O’Steen. Q&A with film historian Bobbie O’Steen moderated by music editor Suzana Peric on Saturday, October 24th Part of Filmcraft: American Cinema Editors

title: I Saw the TV Glow
description: Teenager Owen is just trying to make it through life in the suburbs when his classmate introduces him to a mysterious late-night TV show — a vision of a supernatural world beneath their own. In the pale glow of the television, Owen’s view of reality begins to crack.

title: FUGS FILM!
description: Formed in late 1964 by Ed Sanders and Tuli Kupferberg, alongside drummer Ken Weaver – anarchic East Village beat poets who could barely play their instruments – The Fugs are credited as the first true underground band. Their lo-fi folk music could be challenging and weird but they had a knack for catchy pop songs, such as “Supergirl” and ‘Slum Goddess”. One of the most crucial figures in countercultural history, Sanders founded the Peace Eye bookstore and the arts journal “F*** You: A Magazine of the Arts”, and, among other late-1960s antics, attempted to levitate the Pentagon and staged a funeral for flower power in San Francisco. Chuck Smith’s vital documentary features eye-popping archival footage and interviews with Sanders, Aline & R. Crumb, Lenny Kaye, Penny Arcade, Jeffrey Lewis, and many others, to tell the story of NYC’s original punks. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with Penny Arcade, Steven Taylor and other participants from the film!

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Amadou & Mariam: The Blind Couple from Mali (15*)
Virgina
description: When a fourth daughter is born to a family “cursed” by superstition to bear no male heirs, the decision is made to raise the child with a boy’s name—Stevan—as well as a man’s rights and responsibilities… though as Stevan passes adolescence, first love and a brush with personal tragedy will spark rebellion in his breast. An acutely observed study of a 19th-century peasant culture steeped in misogyny, and a strikingly sensual story of self-discovery, presented in a new 2K restoration in its NYC premiere. “I’ve gotten to do many cool and amazing things in my work over the years, but tracking down the negative of Virgina, after the director Srđan Karanović thought it had been lost in the aftermath of the Yugoslav Wars, is definitely one of the highlights of my career. Virgina is a stunning film, a complex and interesting narrative about gender, with unique pleasures for a queer audience.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist The new 2K restoration was completed by the Department for Digitisation and Digital Restoration of the Yugoslav Film Archive in Belgrade. The film was scanned from a 35mm internegative using an ArriscanXT scanner with archival gate overscan, with color correction by Masha Badalić under the supervision of director Srđan Karanović. Audio was sourced from the original 35mm mono sound negative and restored by the Sound Department of the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad. An Altered Innocence release Introduction and post-screening discussion by Jenni Olson on Friday, October 23rd Introduction by Jenni Olson on Saturday, October 24th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: Death Becomes Her
description: Meryl Streep and Goldie Hawn are bitter rivals in an all out bitch-fest war. The elixir of youth won’t stand in either of their ways to beat each other, and Bruce Willis gets dragged along as a poor schmuck witness to it all, to boot.

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood (70mm)
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: PHANTOM OF THE PARADISE
description: A disfigured composer sells his soul for the woman he loves so that she will perform his music. However, an evil record tycoon betrays him and steals his music.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: State Funeral (ГОСУДАРСТВЕННЫЕ ПОХОРОНЫ)
description: State Funeral (ГОСУДАРСТВЕННЫЕ ПОХОРОНЫ). 2019. Netherlands/Lithuania. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy MUBI. In Russian; English subtitles. 135 min. The shock of the nation was palpable on March 5, 1953, as though a god had forsaken his people: Comrade Stalin is dead! Long live Comrade Stalin! Sergei Loznitsa provides a riveting forensic study of Josef Stalin’s cult of personality, stitching together largely unseen archival images of his funeral and the gatherings of thousands of mourners across the Soviet Union, from the streets of Leningrad to the steppes of Eurasia. Described in Pravda, the Soviet newspaper, as “the Great Farewell,” the ceremony carried on for days, with loudspeakers blaring rhapsodic tributes and pledges to redouble efforts to carry out the great leader’s Five-Year Plans, with factories ceremoniously shut down and mountains of flowers piling up, with leaders of the Eastern Bloc flying in to pay their respects, and with grim-faced crowds waiting patiently to gaze upon his body lying in state. As we see countless mourners shedding genuine tears or performing their grief, Loznitsa brings the film—and the hero worship—to a sudden and damning halt.

title: BLOODY MUSCLE BODY BUILDER IN HELL
description:
Set in a dingy Tokyo apartment, a self-absorbed bodybuilder sets out to film a showcase of his sculpted physique with the help of his ex-girlfriend and a cameraman, only to discover that the room is haunted by a furious spirit determined to drag them into chaos.
A frenzied splatter comedy forged in pure DIY ambition, Bloody Muscle Body Builder in Hell channels the scrappy inventiveness of cult cabin-in-the-woods horror while leaning hard into slapstick absurdity. Shot on gritty video and exploding with handmade practical effects, it transforms one claustrophobic location into a whirlwind of possession, rubbery monstrosities, and delirious blood soaked spectacle.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: A new kind of horror remake from Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ), starring Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson. After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium. (MUBI)

title: Horror of Dracula
description: The stars (Peter Cushing, Christopher Lee), screenwriter (Jimmy Sangster), and director (Terence Fisher) of Hammer Films’ 1957 breakout hit The Curse of Frankenstein reunited for this exciting adaptation of Bram Stoker’s classic novel. Cushing brought subtlety and intelligence to the character of Dr. Van Helsing, which he would play four more times for Hammer, and Lee’s quietly charismatic portrayal of the Count (a role he would reprise in six sequels) made him one of the most iconic interpreters of the role. With its bold Technicolor cinematography by Jack Asher and the thunderous orchestral score by Hammer regular James Bernard, the film helped establish the studio as a brand name in big-screen horror.
director: Terence Fisher PRODUCED BY: Anthony Hinds

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: V/H/S/Mixtape
description: V/H/S/MIXTAPE cranks the franchise's signature found-footage horror up to eleven with an electrifying new anthology where music and sound become the source of terror. United by a theme that explores the power of music, rhythm, and audio to haunt, possess, transform, and destroy, the film blends cosmic horror, psychological suspense, outrageous splatter, and groundbreaking practical effects into one unforgettable mixtape of nightmares.

title: Colony
description: Our microcinema is going to the undead with horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s ( Train to Busan ) new Korean zombie thriller starring Gianna Jun and Koo Kyo-hwan. Professor Se-jeong (Jun) is thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. With new and fascinating ideas that bring the zombie genre into brilliant new territory of collective consciousness and mold networks, and the kind of action and pathos Yeon Sang-ho is best at, this is a no brainer for any horrorphile!

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

title: Possible Love (15)
description: South Korea’s master filmmaker Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry ) returns with an intertwined drama on two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: Hacks breakout star Hannah Einbinder and, in a playful bit of meta-casting, Gillian Anderson (The X Files, Sex Education) headline this heady, gory slasher homage from writer-director Jane Schoenbrun. Like Schoenbrun’s previous films I Saw the TV Glow and We’re All Going to the World’s Fair, it uses a horror genre lens to explore a rich array of themes and ideas – queer identity and sexuality, memory and nostalgia, the nature of female desire, the state of the entertainment industry – with humour, vulnerability and affection. After years of slapdash sequels, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic, cerebral young director (Einbinder) – who credits the first film with her own queer awakening – to resurrect. But fantasy and reality collide when she visits the original film’s star (Anderson), now a mysterious recluse living on its old set, and the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of fear, desire and delirium

title: Tron
description: The cross-breeding of video games and cinema began in earnest with Tron, one of the first films to extensively employ CGI, here depicting the darkly glittering digital world inside a mainframe computer that programmer Jeff Bridges must compete in a series of gladiatorial contests in order to escape. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: OUTRIDER
description: With Anne Waldman. Producer: Sarah Riggs; Executive Producer: Martin Scorsese. Poet/filmmaker Alystyre Julian’s OUTRIDER is a kinetic portal into fast-speaking poet Anne Waldman’s transcendent role as a visionary word-worker, from her “hearthome” in Greenwich Village and The Poetry Project at St. Mark’s Church, to the Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics at Naropa University in Boulder, Colorado, and outwards to Big Sur, Morocco, and Mexico. OUTRIDER is a portal to her path of imagination, her vow to poetry and activism, and her vortex of artists/collaborators: Patti Smith, Bob Dylan, Thurston Moore, Meredith Monk, Allen Ginsberg, Laurie Anderson, Douglas Dunn, Eileen Myles, Amiri Baraka, James Brandon Lewis, Cecilia Vicuña, Pat Steir, Ha-Yang Kim, Daniel Carter, Eleni Sikelianos, Bob Holman, Janice Lowe, No Land, Akilah Oliver, Lee Ann Brown, Brenda Coultas, and many others. Guided by ancestors of the Beat generation and poetic kinships with radical female musicians, OUTRIDER channels the ancient, bardic tradition – celebrating the thunderous power of poetry. Preceded by: Richard Levine AFTER BASHŌ 2026, 8 min, DCP Twenty haikus by Bob Holman – written while he was following “A Narrow Path Into the Interior,” the walk that Japan’s National Poet, Matsuo Bashō, took in 1689 – are the starting point of this animated collaboration by filmmaker Richard Levine, musician Phillip Johnston, and poet Bob Holman. The poems originally appeared in The New Yorker magazine. Followed by a Q&A with Alystyre Julian & Anne Waldman!

title: The Independent Free Thinkers: Under the Skin
Doc'n Roll: THE BEST SUMMER + Q&A
description: The Best Summer plunges audiences into the 1995 Summersault tour, as Beastie Boys, Sonic Youth, Foo Fighters, Pavement, Rancid, The Amps and Bikini Kill travel across Australia and Southeast Asia.   Shot entirely on Tamra Davis’s handheld camera, the film captures explosive performances alongside ca...

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: REFLECTIONS OF EVIL
description:
A rage-filled street vendor wanders through a warped Los Angeles, stumbling into encounters that twist the city into a feverish labyrinth of paranoia, failed dreams, and collapsing timelines. Haunted by the ghost of his sister and tormented by forces both mundane and uncanny, he barrels through the chaos in a spiral of frustration that borders on apocalyptic.
A ferocious blend of abrasive satire and surreal nightmare, Reflections of Evil channels cultural decay into an overwhelming sensory assault. The film becomes a darkly comic and disorienting vision of obsession, alienation, and a world fraying at every edge.

title: Rosemary’s Baby
description: A young couple, Rosemary and Guy, moves into an infamous New York apartment building, known by frightening legends and mysterious events, with the purpose of starting a family.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Curse of Frankenstein
description: Cherished by no less a personage than Martin Scorsese for its “totally uncalled for” graphic violence, The Curse of Frankenstein was a watershed film for both Fisher and Hammer, earning 30 times its budget back in the US alone and establishing the studio as the world’s preeminent purveyor of Gothic horror. Awaiting the guillotine, Victor Frankenstein (Peter Cushing) ruminates on the catastrophic fallout of his attempt at creating an exemplary being from scavenged bits of the dead, which results in his cracked creation (Christopher Lee) going on a murderous rampage. Extravagantly colorful, generous with the gruesomeness, and performed with zest—all the hallmarks of Hammer in its prime are in place here, in a shining new 4K restoration. Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: CLASS OF NUKE ‘EM HIGH
director: Richard W. Haines, Michael Herz, and Lloyd Kaufman

title: Def by Temptation
description: One of the best films to be released on Troma’s label, James Bond III’s Def by Temptation is a smart, slick, and stylish tale of faith, temptation, and demons! Joel grew up in the church but has recently started questioning his beliefs. After sensing a supernatural presence from his deceased father, Joel becomes compelled to visit his cousin in New York. But shortly after arriving, they become embroiled in a series of mysterious homicides of local men, all of whom were last seen in the company of a mysterious and beautiful woman. Beautifully photographed by Ernest Dickerson and starring Kadeem Hardison and Samuel L. Jackson, this sole directorial effort from child actor James Bond III is a macabre, neon-tinged portrait of late 1980s Brooklyn. The movie blends supernatural horror and religious mysticism, punctuated by an electrifying hip hop and R&B soundtrack. Newly restored from the original 35mm camera negative!

title: "Venus on the Half-Shell" / THE BEAST
description: “Venus on the Half-Shell,” 1975, Dir. Walerian Borowczyk, 5 Mins, Tamasa Distribution, France

title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut
description: While so many special effects spectacles are lost in time like tears in the rain, Blade Runner remains the template for imagining the neon-wreathed downer of the future, every bit as influential in its vision as was Fritz Lang’s Metropolis over a half century before. Working from a novel by cult writer Philip K. Dick to create a film that would become the gold standard for sci-fi noir, director Scott shares credit here with “visual futurist” Syd Mead’s design concepts and synth pioneer Vangelis’s atmospheric score. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: Mystery Horror Movie Marathon
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS Please Note: We will have a late licence on the night, and the bar will close at 2am. Don't miss a MYSTERY HORROR MOVIE MARATHON, featuring 5 random horror films that have been plucked from the history of the genre! No Clues! No Hints! No Refunds! Only Dread! Tickets are only £20 Members / £22.50 Non-Members! That's an incredible deal for 5 films; so why not take a chance and let a little mystery into your life!?! MYSTERY HORROR MOVIE MARATHON line-up • MYSTERY MOVIE 1 • MYSTERY MOVIE 2 • MYSTERY MOVIE 3 • MYSTERY MOVIE 4 • MYSTERY MOVIE 5 (We will update end time shortly) ------------------------ NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! AGE RESTRICTIONS: This event is strictly 18+

title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
description: That the world of the future was to be increasingly shaped by Asia was a central tenet of cyberpunk, and so it should come as no surprise that one of the greatest of cyberpunk films came from the Land of the Rising Sun. Man and machine feel the urge to merge in Tsukamoto’s utterly indescribable midnight movie staple, an assault-on-the-senses body horror running of the gauntlet which centers on an anonymous salaryman who begins to transform himself into a man of steel, his waking nightmare captured in twitchy camerawork and lurid, gritty black-and-white 16mm. A symphony of sex, steel, and scarification, set to a scraping industrial clangor. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: Creepshow
description: Five grisly tales from a kid's comic book about a murdered father rising from his grave, a bizarre meteor, a vengeful husband, a mysterious crate's occupant, and a plague of cockroaches.

title: Classic Horror Marathon
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS THE THING : In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one. THE EXORCIST (Extended Cut) : When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job. THE SHINING : Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family. A NIGHTMARE ON ELM STREET: In Wes Craven's classic slasher film, several Midwestern teenagers fall prey to Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), a disfigured midnight mangler who preys on the teenagers in their dreams -- which, in turn, kills them in reality. After investigating the phenomenon, Nancy (Heather Langenkamp) begins to suspect that a dark secret kept by her and her friends' parents may be the key to unraveling the mystery, but can Nancy and her boyfriend Glen (Johnny Depp) solve the puzzle before it's too late? THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE : When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape. Marathon is due to end at 08:38am Please Note: The Bar closes at 11pm ------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT! NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! AGE RESTRICTIONS: This event is strictly 18+
director: John Carpenter, William Friedkin, Stanley Kubrick, Wes Craven, Tobe Hooper

title: Maniac Cop 2
description: You have the right to remain silent… forever! Undead cop Matthew Cordell is back for a new killing spree across the streets of NYC. Director William Lustig and screenwriter Larry Cohen reunite for a supercharged sequel, a spectacularly entertaining action horror hybrid packed with a solid cast (Robert Davi, Claudia Christian, Bruce Campbell) and jaw-dropping stunts and practical effects work.

title: Hackney Children's Film Fest: PENGUIN HIGHWAY
description: A fourth-grader, Aoyama-kun, investigates the mysterious reason behind the sudden appearance of penguins in his village, which is somehow related to a power from a young woman working at a dental clinic.  This screening is presented by our friends at Japanese Film Club! Sayumi’s famous cookies will ...

title: Día de los Muertos Celebration
description: Vidiots invites you to join us for our third annual Día de los Muertos Celebration – a special community event in remembrance of our loved ones. Join us in the MUBI microcinema for face-painting and arts and crafts for all ages. Plus Día de los Muertos inspired treats, a community ofrenda in our lobby all week long, and more Vidiots surprises, it’s a day for community, for family, and for reverence to the dearly departed in our hearts.

title: Art Cinema for Tots: How to Play a Film
description: Born out of a commitment to the idea that it’s never too early to introduce kids to the pleasures of movies made outside of the commercial mainstream—and the suspicion that young audiences are often more open-minded and curious than their elders when it comes to such matters—Metrograph presents the latest iteration of Art Cinema for Tots, a celebration of handcrafted, kid-friendly films that reconcile the smart and the silly. In this edition, join us for How to Play a Film, a suite of enchanting, adventurous shorts, including Abbas Kiarostami’s early pedagogical documentary Orderly or Disorderly; Baby, D.A. Pennebaker’s document of a trip to the Central Park Zoo, and Francis Alÿs’s Reel/Unreel, which observes the game-playing of a group of Kabul children. Director of Programming (and mom) Inge de Leeuw describes the experience: “The sound levels will be dimmed, and there will be a gentle light on, creating a relaxed atmosphere where young viewers feel at ease. They won’t be confined to their seats; they can move around, explore, and enjoy the wonder of the big screen. It will be a playful, interactive cinematic journey, designed with little explorers in mind. Orderly or Disorderly (Abbas Kiarostami, 1981, 17 mins) Baby (D.A. Pennebaker, 1954, 6 mins) REEL/UNREEL (Francis Alÿs, 2011, 20 mins) Each ticket includes free admission for one child, if you’d like to bring more than one child per ticket, please email [email protected] to book a seat. This is a general admission screening with no reserved seating. Part of Screen Time at Metrograph

title: The Addams Family
description: Among the most perfectly cast Hollywood studio films of the last half-century, cinematographer-cum-director Sonnenfeld’s adaptation of Charles Addams’s macabre recurring New Yorker feature stars Raul Julia as the suave patriarch of the Addams clan (“You lady-killer…” “Acquitted!”), Anjelica Huston as his waxen, witchy bride, and an outstanding preadolescent Christina Ricci as doomy daughter Wednesday. A drolly dark comedy that moves with the fearsome speed of a 1930s screwball, thanks to the surgical precision of Dede Allen’s editing. Part of Screen Time at Metrograph

title: All We Imagine as Light
description: Winner of the Grand Prix at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival, Kapadia’s fiction feature debut concerns itself with the intimate, everyday concerns of Kani Kusruti and Divya Prabha as Prabha and Anu, roommates and co-workers at a Mumbai hospital, and their recently retired co-worker Parvaty, played by Chhaya Kadam, facing homelessness in the aftermath of an act of slum clearance. Formally and structurally audacious, in its rich color palette and its free movement between slice-of-life realism to transcendental mysticism, and throughout deeply humane. “On some of the older cars in Mumbai’s local railway, the doors don’t close. This is how we meet Prabha, her hands on a pole, the wind in her hair, the city’s lights gently blurred behind her. Aboard the ladies compartment, there’s a sense of ease that she doesn’t find elsewhere in her life, in this crowded city. Among these other women, who chat, listen to music, or doze, she seems to notice just how good the air feels.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: Coco en Español
description: Join Vidiots as we celebrate Día de Los Muertos with the stunning and beloved Pixar film Coco . Miguel is a boy who dreams of musical stardom despite his family’s ban on music. Finding himself in the Land of the Dead, he sets off on a journey to learn the true secrets of his family and a path to the music he loves. A true triumph of animation with dynamic visuals, compelling storytelling and a story of family, tradition, and loss that anyone can enjoy.

title: Avital Ash Presents THE ARTIST
description: George Valentin is a silent movie superstar. The advent of the talkies will sound the death knell for his career and see him fall into oblivion. For young extra Peppy Miller, it seems the sky’s the limit – major movie stardom awaits. THE ARTIST tells the story of their interlinked destinies.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Night of the Living Dead (1968)
description: New 4K Restoration! A disparate group of individuals takes refuge in an abandoned house when corpses begin to leave the graveyard in search of fresh human bodies to devour. The pragmatic Ben (Duane Jones) does his best to control the situation, but when the re-animated bodies surround the house, the other survivors begin to panic. As any semblance of order within the group begins to dissipate, the zombies start to find ways inside. One by one, the living humans become the prey of the deceased ones. "Night of the Living Dead was restored by the Museum of Modern Art and The Film Foundation, with funding provided by the George Lucas Family Foundation and the Celeste Bartos Preservation Fund."

title: An Autumn Afternoon
description: Ozu’s gorgeous 53rd and final feature is a return to a favorite theme, the poignant comedy of marriage, with beloved regular Chishu Ryu as a father giving away his daughter and preparing for another, final goodbye. Good Morning’s satire of creeping consumerism has become more bitter here, the feeling of incoming winter chill is sharper, the entire project imbued with a tang of regret—incidentally, the title literally translates to “The Taste of Autumn Mackerel.” Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: FFW: Howl's Moving Castle (U)
description: Adapted from Dianna Wynne Jones’ magical novel, this Ghibli masterpiece follows a young girl’s transformation into an old woman by the Witch of the Waste.

title: THE WICKER MAN
description:
When a devout Christian police sergeant travels to the remote Scottish island of Summerisle to investigate the disappearance of a young girl, he encounters a close-knit community whose pagan beliefs and seasonal rituals stand in stark contrast to his own. As his investigation deepens, every answer seems only to raise more disturbing questions, leading him towards a revelation he could never have anticipated.
Directed by Robin Hardy from a screenplay by Anthony Shaffer, The Wicker Man overturns the conventions of the traditional horror film, replacing monsters and haunted houses with folklore, religious conflict and mounting psychological unease. Christopher Lee considered Lord Summerisle to be his finest performance, while Paul Giovanni's extraordinary folk-inspired soundtrack became inseparable from the film's haunting atmosphere. Initially released in a heavily truncated version, it has since been restored and is now widely regarded as one of the greatest British horror films ever made.

title: Austerlitz
description: Austerlitz. 2016. Germany. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. In English, German; English subtitles. 94 min. W. G. Sebald was inspired to write his last novel, Austerlitz, in 2001 after watching a BBC television program about the Kindertransport titled “Whatever Happened to Susi?” A story of family secrets and historical erasure, memorialization and forgetting, Sebald’s novel in turn inspired Sergei Loznitsa to offer his own meditations on these themes in his eponymous film study of a contemporary concentration camp museum. Observing the rituals of visitors at a former Nazi death camp, many of them dutifully dragged there in school groups and tourist packages to seize just one more photo op, Loznitsa reflects on the potency and meaning of Holocaust remembrance, which with every passing generation threatens to fade into obscurity, irrelevance, or commodification. The tourists’ T-shirts seem to say it all: “Today is your lucky day,” “Jurassic Park,” “F**kin’ problems,” “Cool story, bro.”

title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (Silent with Live Music Score)
description: In 1920, one brilliant movie jolted the postwar masses and catapulted the German Expressionist film movement into history. That movie was The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari , a plunge into the mind of insanity that severs all ties with the rational world. Director Robert Wiene and a team of visionary designers crafted a nightmare realm in which light, shadow and substance are abstracted, a world in which a demented doctor and a carnival sleepwalker perpetrate a series of ghastly murders in a small community. (Kino Lorber)

title: Men in Black
description: A New York police officer is recruited into a secret government organization that helps hide the existence of extraterrestrial visitors from the public, and teams up with a more experienced operative to track down a malicious alien that has taken over a human host. Tommy Lee Jones and Will Smith make an unexpectedly ideal mismatched pair of heroes, later reuniting for two sequels, and are supported by witty performances from Linda Fiorentino, Rip Torn, and a physical tour-de-force from Vincent D’Onofrio as the possessed farmer. Rick Baker and David LeRoy Anderson won Oscars for their imaginative alien makeup designs; Danny Elfman was nominated for his lively score; and production designer Bo Welch and set decorator Cheryl Carasik were nominated for the film’s art direction, which deftly combined retro-futurist sets and authentic New York locations.

title: ED WOOD
description: Director Ed Wood refuses to let hostile studios, terrible reviews and unfinished scenes from fulfilling his dreams of making movies in Hollywood. Tim Burton directs Martin Landau, Sarah Jessica Parker, Patricia Arquette and Lisa Marie as Vampira to capture Wood’s trajectory from Hollywood flop to beloved cult classic icon.

title: Hackney Children's Film Fest: FILM AFRICA:  CROCODILE
description: Hackney Children’s Film Festival | Sat 24 - Sat 31 October Tickets £5 or £3 with a Hackney Library Card A Rio Cinema Project  The kids have waited long enough! This October half term, the Rio brings Hackney its first ever Children's Film Festival, with a lively and enchanting film programme curated ...

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Imamura: Nishi Ginza Station + My Second Brother
Nous (We)
description: A Malian mechanic; the filmmaker’s sister, a healthcare worker; the acclaimed author Pierre Bergounioux; banlieue teenagers playing Uno… What ties the disparate subjects of Diop’s film together is, in one sense, geographical happenstance—they all live in proximity to the RER B line that runs northeast to southwest—but in following the contours of the commuter train, she gives a panoramic view of another Paris, far from postcard views of the 16 arrondissements. “The people who ride the RER B, a commuter line that connects Paris to its outer periphery, are those who are least visible in the city, the largely Black and immigrant auto mechanics, cleaners, and care workers who depart early and return late. For Diop, they are her neighbors, her family, and more: the ‘we’ of the film’s title placed in the center of her tender city symphony.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: Halloween (1978)
description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: Girl, Interrupted
description: Based on a 1993 memoir of the same name by Susanna Kaysen, Mangold’s powerhouse picture sets its scene at a New England psychiatric hospital c. 1967 where Winona Ryder (in the Kaysen role; also a producer on the film) lands after suffering a nervous breakdown. Among the committed at Claymoore are a hall-of-fame lineup of ’90s female acting talent, including self-harmer Brittany Murphy, schizophrenic burn victim Elisabeth Moss and, in a star-making turn, Angelina Jolie as sociopath agitator Lisa Rowe. Ryder’s is not the flashiest role here, but she holds the film together with her quiet, alert intensity, offering a springboard for her co-stars to dive off into the deep end. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Shaun of the Dead
description: There comes a day in every man's life when he has to get off the couch…and kill some zombies. When flesh-eating zombies are on the hunt for a bite to eat, it's up to slacker Shaun and his best pal to save their friends and family from becoming the next entrée.

title: EYES OF FIRE
description:
A group of settlers in 18th-century Appalachia flee their village after a mysterious tragedy, only to confront the forest itself, haunted, malevolent, and alive with supernatural forces. As fear and superstition deepen, their bonds fracture, and the wilderness becomes both a physical and psychological nightmare.
A slow, atmospheric blend of folk horror and period drama, Eyes of Fire transforms the untamed landscape into a character itself, exploring human fragility, guilt, and the unseen terrors lurking in nature and the mind.

title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial on 35mm
description: Everyone’s favorite wig-wearing, Reese’s Pieces-eating alien is back on our big screen! An all-time classic, Steven Spielberg’s moving and magical tale soars with the wonders and fears of childhood and the enduring power of intergalactic friendship. When Elliot brings home a marooned alien, he and his siblings do whatever it takes—hiding in closets, wrecking their Speak & Spell, flying their bikes across the moon—to help their interstellar friend find his way home. Bring your family and your favorite alien to experience this heartwarmer on the big screen, the way it was meant to be seen!

title: To All the Books
description: Filmmaker/author/musician Josh Malerman has done it all. He’s a New York Times best-selling author. His books have been adapted into major films, including Bird Box , the most-watched movie on Netflix starring Sandra Bullock. He wrote the theme song to the Emmy Award winning eleven season series Shameless . He spent six years on tour traveling the world, and to this day lives a carnival-esque life filled with artistic endeavors in Michigan. And yet with every new novel and creative venture, Josh must face the terror of the blank page and accept the rollercoaster ride of living the life of an artist. Now the audience can ride alongside Josh as he traverses the ups and downs of writing his next book. From producers Scott Beck and Bryan Woods (A Quiet Place, Haunt, Heretic).

title: IT
description: When she first sets eyes on her new boss, the wealthy Cyrus Waltham Jr. (Antonio Moreno), department store clerk Betty Lou Spence (Clara Bow) is convinced he’s got “it,” an indefinable quality that makes one irresistible to the opposite sex. Betty Lou charms her employer on a date, but Cyrus suddenly cools when he hears a false story that Betty Lou has mothered an illegitimate child. Crushed by Cyrus’ assumption, the shopgirl ramps up the sex appeal to win her man back and teach him a lesson.

title: The Natural History of Destruction
description: The Natural History of Destruction. 2022. Germany/Netherlands/France. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. In German, English; English subtitles. 109 min. At a time when the traditional rules of wartime engagement are increasingly violated, civilian populations are used as human shields, and cities are targeted and laid to waste without consequence or legal redress, W. G. Sebald’s book On the Natural History of Destruction has assumed an even deeper moral gravity than when he wrote it in 1999. Sergei Loznitsa’s brilliantly edited archival documentary uses German, British, and American wartime footage in ironic counterpoint to evoke not only the appalling devastation of the Allied air raids that decimated some 131 German cities and towns in the last years of the war, including Cologne, Dresden, and Hamburg (the latter in “Operation Gomorrah”), but also the sense of willed national amnesia—the widespread appeal of kitschy Heimat nostalgia to banish feelings of shame, complicity, and defeat—that Sebald diagnoses and exposes in postwar German society.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: Colony
description: Our microcinema is going to the undead with horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s ( Train to Busan ) new Korean zombie thriller starring Gianna Jun and Koo Kyo-hwan. Professor Se-jeong (Jun) is thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. With new and fascinating ideas that bring the zombie genre into brilliant new territory of collective consciousness and mold networks, and the kind of action and pathos Yeon Sang-ho is best at, this is a no brainer for any horrorphile!

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: La Raulito
description: A tough and tender telling of the early life of Club Atlético Boca Juniors superfan Maria Esther Duffau who, as a teenager, hustled to survive on the mean streets of Buenos Aires between stints in juvie hall and the psych ward, adopting a male identity (the “Little Raul” of the title) along the way. “I feel like I’m in a perpetual quest to discover new (old) films depicting transmasc, butch, and gender nonconforming characters and stories. I first came across La Raulito in 2022, but it’s taken all these years to finally track it down and be able to show it. Like all of the films in this series, La Raulito has a wonderful quality of melodramatic earnestness. As someone who has always embraced sincerity in my own work as a filmmaker, I think this is one of the most beautiful and brave examples you’ll ever see of telling the story of a hero (a real-life national hero in Argentina) who you absolutely cannot resist falling in love with.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist Introduction and Q&A with guest curator and filmmaker Jenni Olson moderated by filmmaker Julia Solomonoff on Sunday, October 25th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
YOU F*RS FIGURE IT OUT: A JASON MOLINA STORY + Q&A
description: Conjure the spirit of indie-rock icon Jason Molina (1973-2013) with Ohio insiders who illuminate the truth about his coming of age on Lake Erie, escaping artless steel town indifference, and manifesting the legendary band, Songs: Ohia, as they celebrate contradictions that tether Jason’s raunchy hum...

title: IN THE MOMENT: WORLD POETRY DUELS AND IMPROVISATIONS
description: IN THE MOMENT features charismatic poets and musicians who are masters of the art of improvisation, dueling with one another and commenting on the meaning of these traditions and of life itself in improvised rhymes. The film introduces viewers to payadores, emboladores, decimistas, band bertsolari poets, as well as freestyle rap. The poets hail from Argentina, Canary Islands, Brazil, Portugal, Italy, Trinidad, the Basque region of Spain, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and the U.S. Preceded by: Richard Levine AFTER BASHŌ 2026, 8 min, DCP Twenty haikus by Bob Holman – written while he was following “A Narrow Path Into the Interior,” the walk that Japan’s National Poet, Matsuo Bashō, took in 1689 – are the starting point of this animated collaboration by filmmaker Richard Levine, musician Phillip Johnston, and poet Bob Holman. The poems originally appeared in The New Yorker magazine. Followed by Q & A with Steve Zeitlin and Amanda Dargan!

title: Nosferatu with Live Score
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . "I first saw Murnau’s Symphony of Horror when I was nine years old. The film’s expressionistic images continue to haunt me, the chiaroscuro compositions tapping vividly into timeless subconscious fears. My improvisations on viola and piano draw inspiration from the leitmotifs and sound effects of 70s horror soundtracks and the languages of Second Viennese School composers contemporary to Murnau, also Jewish Traditional Music that informs my personal approach to creating a score for the film." - Hugo Max Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work. Photo Credit - Richard Ecclestone An iconic film of the German expressionist cinema, and one of the most famous of all silent movies, F. W. Murnau's Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror continues to haunt — and, indeed, terrify — modern audiences with the unshakable power of its images. By teasing a host of occult atmospherics out of dilapidated set-pieces and innocuous real-world locations alike, Murnau captured on celluloid the deeply-rooted elements of a waking nightmare, and launched the signature "Murnau-style" that would change cinema history forever. In this first-ever screen adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, a simple real-estate transaction leads an intrepid businessman deep into the superstitious heart of Transylvania. There he encounters the otherworldly Count Orlok — portrayed by the legendary Max Schreck, in a performance the very backstory of which has spawned its own mythology — who soon after embarks upon a cross-continental voyage to take up residence in a distant new land... and establish his ambiguous dominion. As to whether the count's campaign against the plague-wracked populace erupts from satanic decree, erotic compulsion, or the simple impulse of survival — that remains, perhaps, the greatest mystery of all in this film that's like a blackout...

title: The Return of the Living Dead
description: When foreman Frank (James Karen) shows new employee Freddy (Thom Mathews) a secret military experiment in a supply warehouse, the two klutzes accidentally release a gas that reanimates corpses into flesh-eating zombies. As the epidemic spreads throughout Louisville, Ky., and the creatures satisfy their hunger in gory and outlandish ways, Frank and Freddy fight to survive with the help of their boss (Clu Gulager) and a mysterious mortician (Don Calfa).

title: PHENOMENA
description:
A young American girl enrolled at a Swiss boarding school begins experiencing strange psychic connections with insects after a series of brutal murders targeting students in the area. As she uses her abilities to investigate, she becomes increasingly entangled in a mystery involving a serial killer and the surrounding forest.
The film blends giallo horror with supernatural elements, combining elaborate set pieces, dream logic, and graphic violence. Its structure moves between investigative mystery and surreal fantasy, creating a disorienting atmosphere where psychic perception and physical danger constantly overlap.

title: Oldboy
description: Homer with a ball-peen hammer. Kidnapped and stuffed in a hole without explanation for 15 years of solitary confinement, when Oh Dae-su (Choi Min-sik) is suddenly let loose on the streets, he’s stone-cold pissed off and very, very dangerous. Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes and an international pop phenomenon, Oldboy was a revenge thriller unlike any that had come before, featuring passages of pure bravura filmmaking (that one-shot hallway donnybrook!) and surreal sicko humor that’ll put you off of sushi for a while. “Put together with brutally uncompromising style [and] the cold-steel edge of a knife against your throat. A dark and thrillingly horrible adventure into the realms of the unthinkable.” —The Guardian Part of Classical Cinema

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: A new kind of horror remake from Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ), starring Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson. After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium. (MUBI)

title: American Theater
description: For fans of films like American Movie and Dancin’ Outlaw , a “canceled” theater director summons a troupe of conservative actors to an abandoned cabin in rural Georgia to plot revenge on the Atlanta theater community with a musical retelling of the 1692 Salem witch trials. Winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the Slamdance Film Festival.

title: Christine
description: Adapted from Stephen King's 1983 novel, John Carpenter's Christine follows bullied high schooler Arnie (Keith Gordon) and his growing attachment to his sentient car. As Arnie transforms into a revenge seeker, blindly loyal Christine abets Arnie in hunting down bullies and questioners of the bewildering relationship. The '58 Plymouth Fury is also, seemingly, indestructible, reverting to mint condition whenever tarnished, thanks to the work of Academy Award-nominated visual effects supervisor Roy Arbogast ( Close Encounters of the Third Kind , 1977 ). This cult classic is the perfect blend of King's thriller and Carpenter's unique take on the supernatural.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Richard Korbitz

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood (70mm)
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: LAST NIGHT IN SOHO
description: In acclaimed director Edgar Wright’s psychological thriller, Eloise (Thomasin McKenzie, JOJO RABBIT, OLD), an aspiring fashion designer, is mysteriously able to enter the 1960s, where she encounters a dazzling wannabe singer, Sandie (Anya Taylor-Joy, EMMA, THE QUEEN’S GAMBIT). But the glamour is not all it appears to be, and the dreams of the past start to crack and splinter into something far darker.

title: ABBOTT AND COSTELLO MEET FRANKENSTEIN
description: The Wolf Man tries to warn a dimwitted porter (Lou Costello) that Dracula wants his brain for a monster’s body.

title: ROSEMARY'S BABY
description: A young New York couple (Mia Farrow and John Cassavetes) moves into a new apartment building, where they’re quickly befriended by lovable Ruth Gordon and husband Sidney Blackmer. All is not as it seems, though, and Farrow soon comes to suspect that her neighbors have truly sinister plans in store for her and her unborn baby. This eerie supernatural thriller builds shivery atmosphere through each successive scene, right up until the shattering climax.

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

title: Vera
description: A pioneering work of transmasc cinema inspired by the life of Brazilian poet Anderson Bigode Herzer starring Ana Beatriz Nogueira as Bauer, a trans man who struggles to overcome a painful early life via the embrace of art and the love of a sympathetic young librarian (Aida Leiner). “When Caden Mark Gardner and I co-curated Vera as part of the original Masc series in 2022, Caden did some amazing research on the film. Together we determined that it is one of the earliest (and also one of the best) portrayals in world cinema of a transmasculine character. And the film’s protagonist, Bauer (the film’s title is his dead name), shines through as an incredible transmasc hero. As he confidently proclaims to the powers that be, ‘I’m not what everyone thinks I am. You hear me? I’m different. I’m something else. Something else.’” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist Introduction by Jenni Olson on Sunday, October 25th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: Colony
description: Our microcinema is going to the undead with horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s ( Train to Busan ) new Korean zombie thriller starring Gianna Jun and Koo Kyo-hwan. Professor Se-jeong (Jun) is thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. With new and fascinating ideas that bring the zombie genre into brilliant new territory of collective consciousness and mold networks, and the kind of action and pathos Yeon Sang-ho is best at, this is a no brainer for any horrorphile!

title: AZUL
description: AZUL is a documentary about the poetic soul of Nicaragua. Twenty-four poems interweave with interviews to create a narrative of Nicaragua’s poetry and the historical contexts and individuals who formed it. With poems from the creator of Modernismo, Rubén Darío, to Ernesto Cardenal, Carlos Rigby, and Gioconda Belli, to people reciting spontaneously in the street and soldiers workshopping poems on the frontlines, AZUL reveals a nation alive with the creative spirit and a profound belief in poetry as a crucible for change and expression. Originally filmed during the height of the Contra War, the film has been restored digitally. Preceded by: Richard Levine AFTER BASHŌ 2026, 8 min, DCP Twenty haikus by Bob Holman – written while he was following “A Narrow Path Into the Interior,” the walk that Japan’s National Poet, Matsuo Bashō, took in 1689 – are the starting point of this animated collaboration by filmmaker Richard Levine, musician Phillip Johnston, and poet Bob Holman. The poems originally appeared in The New Yorker magazine. Followed by a Q&A with co-producer and editor Joanna Kiernan!

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Backrooms: Everything Must Go Edition With Bonus Footage
description: A strange doorway appears in the basement of a furniture showroom.

title: Rosemary's Baby
description: “He has his father’s eyes…” Satanists are on the loose in Central Park West in Polanski’s slow-burn thriller, which slips almost imperceptibly from the quotidian into the profane, and gives new meaning to the phrase “pregnancy scare.” Young marrieds Mia Farrow and John Cassavetes make friendly with their elder neighbors Ruth Gordon and Sidney Blackmer, but when Farrow’s abandoned and isolated Rosemary goes into a paranoiac tailspin while expecting her first child, she begins to wonder why everyone is so very eager for her to take her daily dosage of tannis root… A masterclass in slow-building, spine-tingling suspense, aided immeasurably by the dab-handed work of legendary editor Sam O’Steen. Part of Filmcraft: American Cinema Editors

title: A LIZARD IN A WOMAN'S SKIN
description:
Carol Hammond, the daughter of a prominent politician, is tormented by increasingly vivid dreams involving her glamorous, free-spirited neighbour Julia Durer. When Julia is found brutally murdered, the line between Carol's nightmares and reality begins to dissolve, drawing her into a labyrinth of murder, hallucination and psychological manipulation where nothing can be trusted.
Directed by Lucio Fulci before his celebrated cycle of gore films, A Lizard in a Woman's Skin is one of the masterpieces of the Italian giallo. Combining surreal dream imagery, elaborate murder set pieces and psychedelic visual design, the film reflects the influence of the sexual revolution while pushing the boundaries of censorship with its graphic violence and eroticism. Featuring a mesmerising score by Ennio Morricone and standout performances from Florinda Bolkan, Stanley Baker and Anita Strindberg, it remains one of Fulci's most elegant and accomplished works.

title: Jump Scare
description: The female metal band ‘JUMP SCARE’ retreat to a remote cabin to write their next album only to be terrorized by the family of cannibals next door. This phantasmagoric blend of genres, tones, and colors is equal parts cannibal movie, slasher, rock opera, and with a touch of renegade humor thrown in for extra sauce. It’s your new cult favorite! Featuring everyone’s favorite working actor, Eric Roberts, his 8,000th film from 2026 .

title: Virgina
description: When a fourth daughter is born to a family “cursed” by superstition to bear no male heirs, the decision is made to raise the child with a boy’s name—Stevan—as well as a man’s rights and responsibilities… though as Stevan passes adolescence, first love and a brush with personal tragedy will spark rebellion in his breast. An acutely observed study of a 19th-century peasant culture steeped in misogyny, and a strikingly sensual story of self-discovery, presented in a new 2K restoration in its NYC premiere. “I’ve gotten to do many cool and amazing things in my work over the years, but tracking down the negative of Virgina, after the director Srđan Karanović thought it had been lost in the aftermath of the Yugoslav Wars, is definitely one of the highlights of my career. Virgina is a stunning film, a complex and interesting narrative about gender, with unique pleasures for a queer audience.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist The new 2K restoration was completed by the Department for Digitisation and Digital Restoration of the Yugoslav Film Archive in Belgrade. The film was scanned from a 35mm internegative using an ArriscanXT scanner with archival gate overscan, with color correction by Masha Badalić under the supervision of director Srđan Karanović. Audio was sourced from the original 35mm mono sound negative and restored by the Sound Department of the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad. An Altered Innocence release Introduction and post-screening discussion by Jenni Olson on Friday, October 23rd Introduction by Jenni Olson on Saturday, October 24th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

description: Effi bounces between unemployment, clubbing and hangovers in the hills of Northern Wales, in Marc Evans ' hard-hitting, Welsh language drama.
