title: Manhunter : The Final Cut
description: A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast , including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen (The Contender, 2000) as his blind love interest. -- This new 4K Final Cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version. Shot in 1985, MANHUNTER was on a frontier in both its subject matter and film form, initiating an impressive list of subsequent films and series. “40 years ago – though armed with Thomas Harris’ excellent novel, “Red Dragon” – its subject matter, the profiling of serial killers, as well as being shocking and raw, was unknown. When adapting, I wanted to make its storytelling deliver audiences into a certain state of threat and emotional engagement. Integral to that was the visualization and use of music with lyrics sometimes working like a libretto. We have carefully remastered the film to try to evoke that mood and intensity, heightened with audio sourced from the original 5.1 35mm analog masters. This latest iteration is that version of the film with which I’m most satisfied.” said director Michael Mann. Under the guidance of Mann, this 4K scan of the original 35mm negative – with a few shots from an interpositive - was conformed and digitally restored at L’Immagine Ritrovata in Bologna. Both the theatrical version and the UHD HDR & SDR video color gradings were performed by Stefan Sonnenfeld at Company 3 in Los Angeles with the director. Sound restoration was done at Audio Mechanics from an original 35mm magnetic 6-track printmaster to release a new 5.1 mix by Luke Schwartzweller at Fox . Technical coordination and deliveries were managed by L’Immagine Ritrovata . This project was supervised by Becca Mann and STUDIOCANAL team, Jean-Pierre Boiget and Delphine Roussel . For Michael Mann, the process is about renewing the film’s immediacy for contemporary audiences: “If the picture was left the way it was, it would be interesting, but you’d feel some distance …you’d be observing it somewhat. I’m more interested in its original intent impacting you the same way it may have in 1986…that is, to bring you into it again in the original way.” As a film distinguished by its striking visual style, including Colleen Attwood’s costume design, Academy Award- winner Mel Bourne’s art direction, Dante Spinotti’s lighting, Mann worked with his long-time collaborator, Stefan Sonnenfeld (Company 3), to develop a new color grade for ‘The Final Cut’ that engages a contemporary audience while honoring the film’s lasting legacy. “A good example is the use of primaries and secondaries in combinations that don’t occur in nature for an unsettling ambiance or the use of blue for night-time imagery. We’ve changed values subtly sometimes, but significantly, to enhance the impact without changing the dramatic intent of the film,” said Stefan Sonnenfeld. He adds: “Michael… wants you to understand the story and the mood and the environment… and then asks you to interpret that in colour… He also tells you what emotion he’s trying to evoke from the scene.” The new version also introduces an HDR presentation, offering an intensified new experience. “So that nobody’s ever seen the movie like that,” noted Sonnenfeld.

title: Under the Skin (2013)
description: An alien entity inhabits the earthly form of a seductive young woman who combs the Scottish highways in search of the human prey it is here to plunder. It lures its isolated and forsaken male victims into an otherworldly dimension where they are stripped and consumed. But life in all its complexity starts to change the alien. It begins to see itself as 'she', as human, with tragic and terrifying consequences.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: Relaxed Screening: Teenage Sex and Death (15)
The Cable Guy
description: * ON SALE 23rd SEP * Oddball cable installer Chip Douglas (Jim Carrey) attempts to strike up a friendship with customer Steven Kovacs (Matthew Broderick) by offering him premium channels at no cost. When Steven rebuffs Chip's frequent need for companionship, Chip goes from a mildly eccentric acquaintance to a full-fledged psycho stalker. Though it's increasingly apparent to Steven that the cable guy is dangerous, convincing his friends, family and the authorities of that is another matter entirely.

title: FLESH FOR FRANKENSTEIN 3D
description: Presented by The Evolution of Horror: Baron Frankenstein pursues a grotesque scientific mission to construct a perfect master race, harvesting bodies and limbs from the peasantry to assemble his ideal creations. As his experiments descend into obsession, sexual pathology, and farce, the boundaries between aristocratic authority and abject violence collapse. Excessive, confrontational, and deliberately artificial, Paul Morrissey’s Flesh for Frankenstein reframes the horror myth as a corrosive satire of power, reproduction, and class, presenting a diseased vision of Europe where ideology and flesh are equally disposable.

title: Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood (70mm)
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: Cinematic Void Presents EVILSPEAK
description: Clint Howard goes all in as a nebbish military school cadet who uses an Apple II with 4K of RAM, a skull-smashing broadsword and a horde of bloodthirsty devil pigs to exact revenge! Horror movies about teens with supernatural powers are nothing new, but EVILSPEAK adds the juicy novelty of WARGAMES-era home computing into the mix. Add in some of the Eighties’ tastiest gore scenes and the battiest treatment of a cute puppy in cinema history, and you’ve got the kind of tasteless, utterly watchable celluloid gold they just don’t make anymore.

title: An Evening with Rose Salane
description: Artist Rose Salane has excavated New York City archives of all kinds, from the MTA’s repository of counterfeit subway tokens to a collection of photographs taken from the World Trade Center’s Windows on the World. In her debut film, she assembles her own archive, celebrating “the many lives that the city hosts…[using] the art form of cinema to help hold their synchronicity and share the serendipity that is felt while moving across New York City.” Mercurial New York unfolds as a series of conversations—staged but largely improvised, with everyday New Yorkers playing versions of themselves—taking place from day to night across the five boroughs. Exchanges between friends, family members, and lovers, recorded in 20 languages in a testament to the city’s rich cultural diversity, offer glimpses into the life experiences of city residents and the conditions that shape them. Through the use of telephoto lenses and plucky on-location shoots, the film’s beguiling camera perspectives travel, as New Yorkers do, between the heights of skyscraper towers and subterranean tunnels and everything in between. Finding great intimacy in shared spaces, Salane’s kinetic, tender portrait pulses with the geometries, sounds, and textures of contemporary city life. The screening is presented in conjunction with Storefront for Art and Architecture and will be followed by a conversation with Salane moderated by Sophie Cavoulacos, Curator, Department of Film. Mercurial New York. 2025–26. USA. Directed by Rose Salane. 67 min. New York premiere.

title: Insiang
description: Vidiots, The Cinegogue , and A Bunch of Savages are thrilled to present an ultra-rare screening of Lino Brocka’s masterful melodrama Insiang .

title: They Live by Night
description: Before Terrence Malick’s Badlands (1973), before Arthur Penn’s Bonnie and Clyde (1967), there was Nicholas Ray’s They Live by Night (1948), a book-to-screen adaptation about young lovers on the run. After busting out of prison, Bowie (Farley Granger) hides out at a filling station owned by a dad with alcoholism and his daughter Keechie (Cathy O’Donnell) and starts knocking off banks with his fellow escapees. After a spending spree leaves Bowie injured and vulnerable to the law, Keechie falls for him, and the couple sets off an ill-fated journey, hopeful for a new life. In Ray’s remarkable debut feature, classic noir elements blend effortlessly with melodrama to create something entirely new, making They Live by Night a standout of the period, realized with lived-in dialogue beautifully adapted from Edward Anderson’s source material and shot primarily on location in greater Los Angeles. The film is notable too for its innovative camera techniques and tracking shots, especially in the driving sequences. This warm-up for Rebel Without a Cause (1955) finds Ray arriving on the scene fully formed with a confident and inimitable style. A favorite of cartoonist Nathan Gelgud and critic A. S. Hamrah, the screening is followed by a conversation about Ray and his oft-overlooked influence on American filmmaking. In a separately ticketed event before the film, Gelgud and Hamrah sign copies of their newest books. Programmed and note by K.J. Relth-Miller.

title: Scream
description: Wes Craven re-invented and revitalised the slasher-horror genre with this modern horror classic, which manages to be funny, clever and scary, as a fright-masked knife maniac stalks high-school students in middle-class suburbia. Craven is happy to provide both tension and self-parody as the body count mounts - but the victims aren't always the ones you'd expect.

title: DOC'N ROLL: SHORTS NIGHT
description: This year’s Doc'n Roll FF shorts programme is united by a distinctly punk ethos,  not a genre, but an attitude. From London’s underground rap and hardcore scenes to Black musicians making noise in Texas, resistance on the dancefloor and the cultural battles around gangster rap, these five films cele...

title: Obsession (2026)
description: After breaking the mysterious "One Wish Willow" to win his crush's heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for but soon discovers that some desires come at a dark, sinister price.

title: DRILLER KILLER
description:
The rent is due, the painting will not come together and the band next door will not stop. For a downtown artist hanging on by his fingernails, New York’s constant noise starts sounding like a command.
Abel Ferrara stars in his own grimy portrait of creative collapse, where punk rehearsal rooms and cramped apartments matter as much as the notorious violence. This is horror made out of unpaid bills, sleepless nights and a city coming apart. A raw document of late-seventies downtown life with a power tool at its centre.

title: The Crow (1994)
description: Exactly one year after young rock guitarist Eric Draven and his fiancée are brutally killed by a ruthless gang of criminals, Draven—watched over by a hypnotic crow—returns from the grave to exact revenge.

title: KILLER KLOWNS FROM OUTER SPACE
description: Truly one-of-a-kind alien-invasion sci-fi featuring blood-drinking intergalactic clowns harvesting a small city of its plasma.

title: Funeral Home             / Blue Monkey
description: Some things never rest in peace… When the easily scared Heather (Lesleh Donaldson) comes to town to help her grandmother turn a decaying funeral home into a charming bed-and-breakfast, strange happenings and unexplained murders begin to threaten their plans. Will Heather be able to work up the courage to investigate the funeral home’s dark and mysterious past? More importantly, will she survive long enough to solve the mystery? Long available only on video, William Fruet’s Funeral Home (also known as Cries in the Night ) is an essential yet underseen piece of Canadian horror history. (American Genre Film Archive)

description: In Wes Craven's classic slasher film, several Midwestern teenagers fall prey to Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), a disfigured midnight mangler who preys on the teenagers in their dreams -- which, in turn, kills them in reality. After investigating the phenomenon, Nancy (Heather Langenkamp) begins to suspect that a dark secret kept by her and her friends' parents may be the key to unraveling the mystery, but can Nancy and her boyfriend Glen (Johnny Depp) solve the puzzle before it's too late?

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: Friday The 13th
description: A group of teenage camp counselors attempt to re-open an abandoned summer camp with a tragic past, but they are stalked by a mysterious, relentless killer.

title: Portrait (ПОРТРЕТ)
description: Portrait (ПОРТРЕТ). 2002. Russia. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. No dialogue. 28 min. Ominous rain clouds, a recurring trope of Sergei Loznitsa’s early films, once again gather as the curtains open on Portrait. Like some contemporary August Sander, Loznitsa documents the Russian peasantry in stark frontal poses. The commonality of rural life anywhere and everywhere—the familiar weather-bitten faces, the stock expressions of humility and resilience, the well-handled tools of the trade, whether axe or logging sled or wheelbarrow—is belied by the evocative specificity of their particular circumstances: the two men who could pass for twins, the lumberjack with his crosscut saw poised in mid-action, the hobo (hobo?) who with his rucksack seems to be just heading off to the train behind him. These characters, or their types, seem frozen in time and place, but the landscape is perpetually changing, from the icy winter with its unforgiving winds to the spring thaw of birdsong, dandelion seeds, and freshly tilled earth in shimmering heat. Settlement (ПОСЕЛЕНИЕ). 2001. Russia. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. 80 min. Winner of a jury prize at the Karlovy Vary Film Festival, Sergei Loznitsa’s debut feature observes the daily lives of people with mental disabilities in Oksochi, a communal psychiatric hospital in the Russian countryside. There is an air of peaceful contentment as the men and women tend the livestock, air the carpets, write letters, and read books, but darker images also intrude: images of collective fieldwork, silent canteen meals, and uniformly shaved heads that seem to echo a Soviet past of castigation, confinement, and rote labor. Loznitsa’s language is vernacular and unvarnished, his camera positioned frontally or at a remove, his soundscape an almost hyperreal concatenation of buzz saw, crackling fire, and muttered chatter. The film’s denouement, a progression of portraits set to Vladimir Vavilov’s “Ave Maria,” ennobles and enriches this marginalized community. Tragically, in 2013, 12 years after the film’s release, a fire tore through the 19th-century timber hospital, killing 36 patients and a nurse who tried to rescue them.

description: A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show.

title: HIRUKO THE GOBLIN
description:
When a teacher disappears beneath a rural school, his archaeologist colleague Hieda arrives to investigate a recently uncovered burial mound. He joins forces with the missing man’s teenage son, Masao, whose classmates are being transformed into grotesque spider-legged heads. Together they must descend into the ancient chambers below the school and prevent a gateway to the world of demons from opening completely.
Following the industrial nightmare of Tetsuo, Shinya Tsukamoto turned to folk horror and creature comedy for this wildly kinetic adaptation of Daijiro Morohoshi’s manga. HIRUKO THE GOBLIN combines handmade effects, frantic camerawork and school-holiday adventure with images of genuine nightmare intensity. Playful, disgusting and constantly inventive, it reveals a more colourful but no less unruly side of Tsukamoto’s cinema.
Introduced by James Balmont - film critic and writer.

description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape. * The first 35 customers to have tickets scanned in each of these performances will recieve an exclusive limited edition " I SURVIVED THE TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE" badge. VIOLENCE VOYAGER
description:
American schoolboy Bobby and his friend Akkun take a shortcut through the mountains and discover a mysterious amusement park called Violence Voyager. Armed with water pistols, they enter what appears to be an innocent adventure game, but soon find children trapped inside a cruel experiment involving chemical weapons, grotesque mutations and an army of mechanical monsters.
Created using Ujicha’s distinctive gekimation technique, in which hand-painted cardboard figures are manipulated before the camera, VIOLENCE VOYAGER transforms childhood adventure into a tactile, psychedelic nightmare. The deliberately limited movement makes every eruption of blood and bodily transformation feel disturbingly physical. Funny, imaginative and increasingly horrifying, the film occupies a unique space between picture-book innocence, underground animation and extreme body horror.
Introduced by James Balmont - film critic and writer.

title: Ghost Town + Q&A
description: In a Japanese coastal town still haunted by the 2011 tsunami, a taxi becomes a moving confession booth. Over the course of one night, a series of conversations between drivers and their passengers reveal how those who survived live with the dead – as ghostly tales, dreams and everyday life merge in a magical drift between reality and imagination. The screening at the ICA on Tuesday 27 October is the London Premiere of Ghost Town .

title: Prince Charles Cinema Film Quiz
description: Put your cinematic knowledge to the test with The Prince Charles Cinema Film Quiz! This is a full-blown, no-holds-barred celebration of cinematic chaos, cult classics, and endless movie trivia. Hosted by Chevy Mclaren live in the heart of London cinema - this is your chance to test your film knowledge in this night of movie madness! Expect limited-edition PCC merch, free cinema tickets, exclusive movie prizes, live performances, and bonkers audience games. Bring your cinephile friends (teams up to 5), grab a drink, and prepare to scream, guess, act, and laugh your way through the most chaotic quiz night in London!

title: Doc 'n Roll: KING OF THEM ALL - The Story of King Records+ Q&A
description: King of Them All chronicles the underdog label that launched James Brown and transformed American music.  Founded by Syd Nathan in the 1940s, King Records pioneered an “all under one roof” operation, recording, pressing and shipping groundbreaking music at remarkable speed. Rare archival recordings ...

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
The Mummy [1999]
description: The Mummy is a rousing, suspenseful and horrifying epic about an expedition of treasure-seeking explorers in the Sahara Desert in 1925. Stumbling upon an ancient tomb, the hunters unwittingly set loose a 3,000-year-old legacy of terror, which is embodied in the vengeful reincarnation of an Egyptian priest who had been sentenced to an eternity as one of the living dead.

title: JIGOKU
description: Shocking, outrageous and poetic, JIGOKU (HELL, a.k.a. THE SINNERS OF HELL ) is the most innovative creation from Nobuo Nakagawa, the father of the Japanese horror film. After a young theology student flees a hit-and-run accident, he is plagued by both his own guilt-ridden conscience and a mysterious, diabolical doppelgänger. But all possible escape routes lead straight to hell—literally. In the gloriously gory final third of the film, Nakagawa offers up his vision of the underworld in a tour de force of torture and degradation. A striking departure from traditional Japanese ghost stories, JIGOKU, with its truly eye-popping (and -gouging) imagery, created aftershocks that are still reverberating in contemporary world horror cinema.

description: In 1945, Grace Stewart (Nicole Kidman) and her two children live an unusually isolated existence behind the locked doors and drawn curtains of a secluded mansion on one of the Channel Islands. The arrival of mysterious new servants (Fionnula Flanagan, Ed Sykes) and her apparently war-fatigued husband Charles (Christopher Eccleston), raise the unworldly feeling that there is far more to this house than can be seen, provoking Grace into a terrifying fight to save her children and preserve her sanity. title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

description: When their plan to book a show at the Rivoli goes horribly wrong, Matt and Jay accidentally travel back to the year 2008.

title: The Natural History of Destruction
description: The Natural History of Destruction. 2022. Germany/Netherlands/France. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. In German, English; English subtitles. 109 min. At a time when the traditional rules of wartime engagement are increasingly violated, civilian populations are used as human shields, and cities are targeted and laid to waste without consequence or legal redress, W. G. Sebald’s book On the Natural History of Destruction has assumed an even deeper moral gravity than when he wrote it in 1999. Sergei Loznitsa’s brilliantly edited archival documentary uses German, British, and American wartime footage in ironic counterpoint to evoke not only the appalling devastation of the Allied air raids that decimated some 131 German cities and towns in the last years of the war, including Cologne, Dresden, and Hamburg (the latter in “Operation Gomorrah”), but also the sense of willed national amnesia—the widespread appeal of kitschy Heimat nostalgia to banish feelings of shame, complicity, and defeat—that Sebald diagnoses and exposes in postwar German society.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: Brother
description: Legendary comedian and TV host turned director Takeshi Kitano writes, directs, and stars in his first and only American co-production. Disgraced yakuza Yamamoto (Kitano) seeks refuge in Los Angeles, reconnecting with his younger half-brother Ken (Claude Maki) after his clan suffered defeat at the hands of a rival gang back in Tokyo. Cool and detached, Brother marries Japanese and American disillusionment in Kitano’s signature violent minimalist style through the growing bonds between Yamamoto and the multinational gang that he cultivates in L.A. Brother is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

description: One wild night on the streets of Kyoto as a student plans the perfect meet-cute from the irrepressible anime auteur, Masaaki Yuasa .

description: More than an archbishop, Desmond Tutu was a moral force whose courage, compassion and unwavering belief in justice helped transform South Africa and inspired the world. title: SPIDER BABY
description:
A decrepit mansion houses the Merrye family, whose surviving children suffer from a bizarre, degenerative disease that makes them increasingly violent, cunning, and feral. As outsiders arrive, the family’s twisted games and macabre antics escalate, revealing their darkly comic, horrifying nature and the strange, grotesque world they inhabit.
Spider Baby blends black comedy, gothic horror, and campy thrills into a deliriously twisted fable. With its eccentric characters, claustrophobic setting, and outrageous yet eerie atmosphere, the film has become a cult classic of macabre American cinema.

title: Austerlitz
description: Austerlitz. 2016. Germany. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. In English, German; English subtitles. 94 min. W. G. Sebald was inspired to write his last novel, Austerlitz, in 2001 after watching a BBC television program about the Kindertransport titled “Whatever Happened to Susi?” A story of family secrets and historical erasure, memorialization and forgetting, Sebald’s novel in turn inspired Sergei Loznitsa to offer his own meditations on these themes in his eponymous film study of a contemporary concentration camp museum. Observing the rituals of visitors at a former Nazi death camp, many of them dutifully dragged there in school groups and tourist packages to seize just one more photo op, Loznitsa reflects on the potency and meaning of Holocaust remembrance, which with every passing generation threatens to fade into obscurity, irrelevance, or commodification. The tourists’ T-shirts seem to say it all: “Today is your lucky day,” “Jurassic Park,” “F**kin’ problems,” “Cool story, bro.”

description: Vidiots invites you back for more celluloid strangeness with Sweet 16mm: Halloween Haunts , a ghostly night of obscure, rare, goofy, and haunting short films and cartoons all on 16mm celluloid. From the 1930s through the 1980s, this beyond-rare collection of esoteric spookiness features devilish cartoons, obscure and demonic literary adaptations, antique movie monsters, horrifying vintage trailers, and our annual reprise of the infamous educational short Halloween Safety – it’s sure to be a one-of-a-kind night of witches, demons, ghosts, razorblades in apples, and creeps galore! Everything screened on 16mm film.

title: CREATURE FROM THE BLACK LAGOON 3D
description: A group of scientists on the hunt for fossilized evidence of aquatic creatures in the Amazon get more than they bargained for when a mysterious “Gill-man” starts terrorizing the expedition. While the men chase after this strange new discovery, the beautiful Kay Lawrence (Julia Adams) in thrown into grave peril.

title: EL GUARDIÁN
description: Basilio is hired to watch over a remote beach on Mexico's Baja California coast, a seemingly idyllic stretch of shoreline where little appears to happen. But beneath the tranquil surface lies a community governed by its own codes, where illicit activities coexist with everyday life. Guided by an unwavering moral compass, Basilio is determined to do what he believes is right – only to discover that justice is far more elusive than he imagined. Set against a breathtaking coastal landscape, EL GUARDIÁN, the striking fiction debut by acclaimed documentary filmmaker Nuria Ibáñez (THE NAKED ROOM, A WILD STREAM), is a gripping and quietly unsettling meditation on ethics, belonging, and the fragile boundaries between duty and survival.

title: Ginger Snaps
description: A teen horror for the true weirdos – Ginger Snap s is not only one of the best werewolf films of the new millennium, it’s also one of its best Coming-of-Age classics as well!  Ginger and Brigitte have always been outcasts, and proud of it. After an attack by a vicious lycanthropic animal, Ginger’s really starting to change – for the weirder. Now, she’s more confident than ever; owning her sexuality even while hiding her newly acquired fur and claws. As Ginger’s transformation gets more alarming – and deadly – Brigitte has to find a way to save her sister and herself. Smart, funny, cool, and gross, don’t miss this toothy terror with a crowd on our big screen!

title: Possession
description: A young woman left her family for an unspecified reason. The husband determines to find out the truth and starts following his wife. At first, he suspects that a man is involved. But gradually, he finds out more and more strange behaviors and bizarre incidents that indicate something more than a possessed love affair.

title: Road to Perdition
description: Director Sam Mendes’s next film after his 1999 Best Picture winner American Beauty is a somber and gorgeously crafted gangster drama, based on a graphic novel series by Max Allan Collins and Richard Piers Rayner. Tom Hanks plays Michael Sullivan, a loving father and stoic enforcer for an Irish-American crime family (led by supporting actor nominee Paul Newman), who must flee with his young son. Conrad L. Hall won a posthumous Oscar for his dark, moody cinematography, and the film was also nominated for its art direction (Dennis Gassner, Nancy Haigh), Thomas Newman’s moving score, and the atmospheric contributions of supervising sound editor Scott A. Hecker and sound mixers Scott Millan, Bob Beemer and John Patrick Pritchett.

title: Andy Warhol's Prison + Dorothy Dean Book Launch
description: Éditions 1989 celebrates the launch of the second edition of Who Are You Dorothy Dean? When Dorothy Dean (1932–1987) entered the 1960s New York underground scene, she quickly became one of its key figures, starring in six of Andy Warhol's films and inspiring the likes of Robert Mapplethorpe and Robert Creeley. Said to be the first woman ever hired as a fact-checker at The New Yorker , Dean held brief editorial and proofreading positions at publications such as Vogue before launching her very own bulletin of film reviews, the All-Lavender Cinema Courier , in 1976. But in histories of the era, she has often been overlooked. The evening will feature a special 40-minute excerpt from Andy Warhol's Prison (1965), inspired by Bibbe Hansen's experiences in a juvenile detention centre and featuring Dean. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with author Anaïs Ngbanzo, moderated by Róisín Tapponi. Books will be available for purchase and signing.

title: NFTS Collective Visions of Pleasure: I.K.U
BABY BLOOD
description:
A parasitic creature escapes from the body of an exotic animal and takes refuge inside Yanka, a performer in a travelling circus. Now carrying an unnatural pregnancy, she hears the creature speaking to her and is compelled to satisfy its endless demand for human blood. As Yanka cuts a violent path across France, the relationship between mother and unborn monster becomes increasingly intimate and difficult to escape.
Alain Robak’s splattery French body-horror comedy combines the biological nightmare of early Cronenberg with the unruly energy of European exploitation cinema. Emmanuelle Escourrou gives a fearless physical performance, shifting between terror, fury and reluctant maternal attachment as the carnage mounts. Grotesque, funny and unexpectedly sympathetic towards its heroine, BABY BLOOD has grown into a fiercely loved cult discovery.

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

It’s a night full of zany fun and comic chaos once the tricky 300-year-old trio set out to cast a spell on the town and reclaim their youth…but first they must get their act together and outwit three kids and a talking cat.

Eventually, gentle Louis resolves to leave his violent maker, but Lestat guilts him into staying by turning a young girl -- whose addition to the "family" breeds even more conflict.

title: From Dusk Till Dawn
description: After kidnapping a father and his two kids, the Gecko brothers head south to a seedy Mexican bar to hide out in safety, unaware of its notorious clientele.

title: FFW: Howl's Moving Castle (U)
description: Adapted from Dianna Wynne Jones’ magical novel, this Ghibli masterpiece follows a young girl’s transformation into an old woman by the Witch of the Waste.

title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
description: Count Dracula, a 15th-century prince, is condemned to live off the blood of the living for eternity. Young lawyer Jonathan Harker is sent to Dracula's castle to finalise a land deal, but when the Count sees a photo of Harker's fiancée, Mina, the spitting image of his dead wife, he imprisons him and sets off for London to track her down.

title: HACKNEY CHILDREN'S FILM FEST: MAYA, GIVE ME A TITLE!
description: Hackney Children’s Film Festival | Sat 24 - Sat 31 October Tickets £5 or £3 with a Hackney Library Card A Rio Cinema Project  The kids have waited long enough! This October half term, the Rio brings Hackney its first ever Children's Film Festival, with a lively and enchanting film programme curated ...

title: Sinners
description: From Ryan Coogler—director of “Black Panther” and “Creed”—and starring Michael B. Jordan comes a new vision of fear: “Sinners.” Trying to leave their troubled lives behind, twin brothers (Jordan) return to their hometown to start again, only to discover that an even greater evil is waiting to welcome them back. “You keep dancing with the devil, one day he’s gonna follow you home.” Written and directed by Academy Award-nominated filmmaker Coogler, “Sinners” stars Jordan (the “Black Panther” and “Creed” franchises) in a dual role, joined by Oscar nominee Hailee Steinfeld (“Bumblebee,” “True Grit”), Jack O’Connell (“Ferrari”), Wunmi Mosaku (“Passenger”), Jayme Lawson (“The Woman King”), Omar Miller (“True Lies”), and Delroy Lindo (“Da 5 Bloods”). The film is produced by Zinzi Coogler, Sev Ohanian and Ryan Coogler. The executive producers are Ludwig Göransson, Will Greenfield and Rebecca Cho.

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: Nosferatu with Live Score
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . "I first saw Murnau’s Symphony of Horror when I was nine years old. The film’s expressionistic images continue to haunt me, the chiaroscuro compositions tapping vividly into timeless subconscious fears. My improvisations on viola and piano draw inspiration from the leitmotifs and sound effects of 70s horror soundtracks and the languages of Second Viennese School composers contemporary to Murnau, also Jewish Traditional Music that informs my personal approach to creating a score for the film." - Hugo Max Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work. Photo Credit - Richard Ecclestone An iconic film of the German expressionist cinema, and one of the most famous of all silent movies, F. W. Murnau's Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror continues to haunt — and, indeed, terrify — modern audiences with the unshakable power of its images. By teasing a host of occult atmospherics out of dilapidated set-pieces and innocuous real-world locations alike, Murnau captured on celluloid the deeply-rooted elements of a waking nightmare, and launched the signature "Murnau-style" that would change cinema history forever. In this first-ever screen adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, a simple real-estate transaction leads an intrepid businessman deep into the superstitious heart of Transylvania. There he encounters the otherworldly Count Orlok — portrayed by the legendary Max Schreck, in a performance the very backstory of which has spawned its own mythology — who soon after embarks upon a cross-continental voyage to take up residence in a distant new land... and establish his ambiguous dominion. As to whether the count's campaign against the plague-wracked populace erupts from satanic decree, erotic compulsion, or the simple impulse of survival — that remains, perhaps, the greatest mystery of all in this film that's like a blackout...

title: Nadja • 4K Restoration • London Premiere
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda (Tesla, Experimenter, Hamlet) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja. The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video, looking better than ever in this new 4K restoration of the director’s cut. London Premiere of the New 4K restoration of the director’s cut c/o Arbelos Films and Radiance Films.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Possible Love (15)
description: South Korea’s master filmmaker Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry ) returns with an intertwined drama on two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires.

title: Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood (70mm)
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: AVITAL ASH WORKSHOPS HER SUICIDE NOTE
description: Ever since she was a baby and her birth mother took her own life, Avital Ash has felt summoned to the other side. But she’d hate to be called a copycat, plus, who wants to turn into their mother? Ash’s critically acclaimed solo show was filmed live at The Elysian Theater in Los Angeles and explores depression, growing up an Orthodox Jew, queer identity and generational Holocaust trauma, all while being hilarious. The results are an irreverent show where Avital expertly bounces from black humor to jokes so stupid you almost miss the gospel in them.

title: EC: THE FALL OF THE HOUSE OF USHER
description: (LA CHUTE DE LA MAISON USHER) Epstein deploys slow-motion, intricate lighting, and stylized sets to create an atmosphere of doom in this famous avant-garde expressionist Poe adaptation (combining both the eponymous tale and another Poe story, “The Oval Portrait”). Starring Marguerite Gance, wife of French director Abel Gance, it was also made with the participation of a young Luis Buñuel, who served as Epstein’s second assistant. “Since the French Impressionist school has always considered the cinema to be like a visual symphony, we might call this film by Epstein the cinematic equivalent of Debussy’s works.” –Henri Langlois Preceded by: Jean Epstein THE THREE-SIDED MIRROR / LA GLACE À TROIS FACES (1927, 38 min, 35mm. French intertitles with English voiceover.) “[Epstein’s] dependence on the close-up, his obsession with the totemic power of the object, his freewheeling mastery of cutting, variation of camera speed, and trust in the interpretive abilities of the audience, all come to a head with THE THREE-SIDED MIRROR. The fractured narrative follows the relations of three separate women…with a handsome, stylish, affluent young man. In the course of the film, he breaks an engagement with each of them in turn, tooling off in a sports car to his eventual demise.” –Brad Weismann, SENSES OF CINEMA

title: An American Werewolf in London
description: John Landis is in his primest form, seamlessly blending horror and comedy in this remarkably witty tale of horrific metamorphosis. Set on the moody moors of so many a classic horror tale, two American tourists are attacked by a werewolf that none of the locals will admit exists, now one is dead and one is changing… into something horrifying. Surreal visions, incredible practical special effects, and a grim sense of humor still keep this classic as fresh as it was 45 years ago! Don’t miss your. chance to see one of the most iconic transformation scenes in cinema on our big screen to see every human-made detail!

title: Hansan: Rising Dragon
description: he second installment of the epic Yi Sun-sin trilogy by director Kim Han-min stars Park Hae-il as the 48-year-old Yi Sun-sin, an admiral of the Joseon dynasty (1392-1910) venerated for seemingly miraculous victories over the Japanese naval forces during the Imjin War period. The film focuses on the 1592 Hansan Island battle against a fleet overseen by daimyo (feudal lord) Wakisaka Yasuharu, who plans to conquer the Joseon peninsula on a quest to devour the entire Ming Dynasty. Yi’s famously optimized Turtle battleship appears in grandiose, precisely executed glory under Yi’s orchestration. Spectacular visual compositions, complemented by remarkable visual effects and a magnificent score, come together to deliver one of most gratifying naval war scenes ever shown on the Korean big screen.

title: KWAIDAN
description: After more than a decade of sober political dramas and socially minded period pieces, the great Japanese director Masaki Kobayashi shifted gears dramatically for this rapturously stylized quartet of ghost stories. Featuring colorfully surreal sets and luminous cinematography, these haunting tales of demonic comeuppance and spiritual trials, adapted from writer Lafcadio Hearn’s collections of Japanese folklore, are existentially frightening and meticulously crafted.

title: Pink Palace: ARIA
description: Pink Palace presents this operatic anthology of ten shorts films by ten directors interpreting their favourite aria’s which become the soundtrack to their segments. Rarely screened and largely forgotten about this cinematic gem features grand costumed dramas, gritty urban thrillers, outlandish fanta...
director: Robert Altman, Derek Jarman, Ken Russell, Jean-Luc Godard, Nicolas Roeg, Julien Temple, Charles Sturridge
