AGE RESTRICTIONS: This event is strictly 18+

title: Halloween: H20
description: Twenty years after the horrific events of Halloween , Laurie Strode must battle the Shape one last time. Jamie Lee Curtis triumphantly returns to the role that made her a scream queen, playing Strode as a woman haunted by her past and living under an assumed name as the headmistress of a private boarding school. But when her rebellious son and his friends skip their school trip to party on the quiet campus, knife-wielding maniac Michael Myers sees them as perfect victims for his belated bloodbath. A game cast of fresh faces, including Josh Hartnett, Michelle Williams, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, and Jodi Lyn O’Keefe, co-star alongside LL Cool J and Janet Leigh.

title: Trick 'r Treat
description: Five interwoven stories that occur on Halloween: An everyday high school principal has a secret life as a serial killer; a college virgin might have just met the guy for her; a group of teenagers pull a mean prank; a woman who loathes the night has to contend with her holiday-obsessed husband; and a mean old man meets his match with a demonic, supernatural trick-or-treater.

title: Homicidal             / Mr. Sardonicus
description: In the small town of Solvang, there’s a killer on the loose… and a bizarre household may hold the key to murder. Nurse Emily takes care of her husband Warren’s childhood guardian, a wheelchair-bound stroke victim. But this nurse’s bedside manner is to die for. As Warren’s half-sister closes in on the truth, she uncovers a town’s most chilling mystery… and her family’s darkest secret. (Sony)

title: The Bride of Frankenstein
description: Mary Shelley reveals the main characters of her novel survived: Dr. Frankenstein, goaded by an even madder scientist, builds his monster a mate.

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween – until the…

title: The Addams Family
description: Among the most perfectly cast Hollywood studio films of the last half-century, cinematographer-cum-director Sonnenfeld’s adaptation of Charles Addams’s macabre recurring New Yorker feature stars Raul Julia as the suave patriarch of the Addams clan (“You lady-killer…” “Acquitted!”), Anjelica Huston as his waxen, witchy bride, and an outstanding preadolescent Christina Ricci as doomy daughter Wednesday. A drolly dark comedy that moves with the fearsome speed of a 1930s screwball, thanks to the surgical precision of Dede Allen’s editing. Part of Screen Time at Metrograph

title: Donnie Darko [Theatrical Cut]
description: During the presidential election of 1988, a teenager named Donnie Darko sleepwalks out of his house one night and sees a giant, demonic-looking rabbit named Frank, who tells him the world will end in 28 days. When Donnie returns home, he finds that a jet engine has crashed into his bedroom. Is Donnie living in a parallel universe, is he suffering from mental illness - or will the world really end?

title: FFW: Howl's Moving Castle (U)
description: Adapted from Dianna Wynne Jones’ magical novel, this Ghibli masterpiece follows a young girl’s transformation into an old woman by the Witch of the Waste.

title: Wicker
description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

title: Sam Wasson Presents ARSENIC AND OLD LACE
description: Cary Grant stars as the one sane member of a charmingly lunatic family in director Frank Capra’s classic comedy, ARSENIC AND OLD LACE.

title: Resident Evil (2026)
description: Have a bloody good time in our microcinema as Zach Cregger’s newest horror triumph takes over for Halloween Weekend! From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling — and terrifying — reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

title: Black History Month:  Alain Gomis' DAO
description: DAO weaves together two ceremonies marking one family’s journey through love and loss. In the French countryside, Gloria marries off her daughter Nour; in Guinea-Bissau, she honours her late father, welcomed among the ancestors. Blending documentary and fiction, with the cast playing tender, unguard...

title: All That Heaven Allows
description: Perhaps the very finest of Sirk’s Ross Hunter-produced melodramas, All That Heaven Allows pairs Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson as, respectively, a well-off widow in country club Connecticut, and the broad-necked, Thoreau-reading gardener who she falls for. Her priggish children, aghast, conspire to break off the pairing, an endeavor that ends in a bone-chilling Christmas conciliation—the presentation of a gift television set as a kind of death sentence. Of this scene Rainer Werner Fassbinder, profoundly marked by his encounter with Sirk’s film, would write: “At that point everyone in the moviehouse breaks down. They suddenly understand something about the world and what it does to people.” Right on. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Sans Soleil
description: Marker's voyage through memory, history, and video games is a free-flow of images shot largely in Japan (a cat temple, sacred phalluses, horror movies, sleeping subway riders, an animatronic JFK), with detours to Guinea-Bissau, Iceland, and, for an extended homage to Vertigo, San Francisco. An alien travelog? The world’s most profound home movie? There’s nothing quite like it in the history of cinema. “Some of Sans Soleil’s trains carry dozing commuters, others travel to distant planets. The film itself moves like a ride through an ever-shifting landscape, shuttling between dreams and waking, here and there.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Beetlejuice
description: Tim Burton’s afterlife spooktacular is an energetic mix of goth fantasy and laugh-out-loud comedy! When two newlyweds (Geena Davis & Alec Baldwin) die in a car accident, they must haunt their recently departed home and scare away the obnoxious replacement residents (Jeffrey Jones & Catherine O’Hara), while befriending the new tenants’ teenage daughter (Winona Ryder). But they get more trouble than they bargained for when they recruit Michael Keaton’s rambunctious “bio-exorcist” Beetlejuice to help.

title: Nova '78
description: A time capsule of the 1978 Nova Convention, bringing together never-before-seen footage recovered from Howard Brookner’s archive, featuring William S. Burroughs, Philip Glass, Frank Zappa, Patti Smith, Laurie Anderson and other cultural radicals at the explosive crossroads of punk, performance, literature and the avant-garde.

title: THE NICKEL’S PSYCHOTRONIC HALLOWEEN MYSTERY MOVIE MASH - DAY TWO 1/11
description:
DAY TWO ONLY – 1/11
Four secret horror films. One long Sunday on the wrong side of respectability. Our Halloween Mystery Movie Mash digs up regional nightmares, exploitation oddities and video-era mutations that deserve a roomful of unsuspecting witnesses.
Every title stays hidden until showtime. Expect the unruly invention and disreputable shocks of films that slipped through horror history’s cracks. Come for the day, or make a weekend of it.
Films screen at 2:00pm, 4:15pm, 6:30pm and 9pm on Sunday 1 November. Weekend passes and Saturday 31 October day tickets are also available.
Costumes highly encouraged.
Artwork by
Jordan McLaughlin

title: Gosford Park
description: A weekend party at an English mansion in the 1930s leads to murder in this seriocomic whodunit, with Robert Altman directing an all-star cast. The Oscar-winning screenplay came via Julian Fellowes, who later explored the same milieu for Downton Abbey . The remarkable transatlantic cast includes Alan Bates, Bob Balaban (who also produced and came up with the story idea with Altman), Clive Owen, Kristin Scott Thomas, Emily Watson, and Helen Mirren and Maggie Smith, who were both nominated for their performances. The film’s seven nominations include Best Picture, Directing, and Art Direction, with production designer Stephen Altman and set decorator Anna Pinnock mixing authentic English mansions and soundstage sets to evoke the glamour and class divisions of the era.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Primetime
description: Inspired by true events in 2006, "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history. But when a high-stakes operation goes fatally wrong, his veneered dream of fame curdles into a nightmare.

title: THE WILD PARTY
description: Wild girls at a college pay more attention to parties than their classes. But when one party girl, Stella Ames, goes too far at a local bar and lands in trouble, her professor must rescue her. Gossip linking the two escalates until Stella proves that she is decent by shielding an innocent girl and winning the professor’s respect.

title: The Gorgon
description: In their tireless search for new monsters to add to their menagerie Hammer turned here to Greek mythology, unleashing the fatal gaze of the Gorgon on the residents of a German village, c. 1910. Seven Vandorf residents have in recent years been found frozen into statuary, and it falls on the esteemed Prof. Meister of Leipzig (Christopher Lee) to overcome interference by local physician Dr. Namaroff (Peter Cushing) and track down the culprit, Megaera (ballerina-turned-film actor Prudence Hyman), a she-devil with the ability to turn flesh to stone. A small miracle of high style on a pinched budget, praised by Raymond Durgnat in Films and Filming for its “romantic warmth… with oil lamps casting a rich glow on the patchwork counterpanes and through coloured windows, and with some extraordinarily beautiful cloudscapes and dusk skies.” Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: EC: ERNIE GEHR
description: “Ernie Gehr [makes] cinematic magic, often from the least likely materials. Indeed, Gehr’s most famous film, SERENE VELOCITY (1970), in which the filmmaker transforms an institutional hallway in the basement of a classroom building at the State University of New York at Binghamton into a nexus of visual and conceptual energy, merely by adjusting his stationary camera’s zoom lens every four frames for twenty-three minutes, can be read as Gehr’s manifesto. For Gehr the most everyday spaces and the most mundane actions offer the imaginative filmmaker the most interesting potential. No other filmmaker, with the exception of Michael Snow, has so relentlessly and so productively explored the capacity of filmmaking to develop the visual (and auditory) opportunities afforded by the cinematic apparatus itself.” –Scott MacDonald, A CRITICAL CINEMA 5 REVERBERATION (1969, 23 min, 16mm) SERENE VELOCITY (1970, 23 min, 16mm, silent) & STILL 1971, 54 min, 16mm. title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
description: An ardent aficionado of the work of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, Cushing takes over the chambers at 221B Baker Street with aplomb and gives us a Sherlock for the ages in Fisher’s adaptation of the 1902 Holmes adventure of the same name, in which our hero is called to Dartmoor to investigate the mysterious death-by-fright of one Sir Charles Baskerville, leaving his estate in the hands of his heir and nephew, Henry (Christopher Lee). With the invaluable assistance of Jack Asher’s subdued Technicolor photography, Fisher wrings every drop of atmosphere out of Doyle’s tale of mist-shrouded moors and ancestral curses, making this one of Holmes’s very finest big-screen outings. (Special mention is due to Fisher’s ingenious use of child stand-ins for his leads to establish the terrible proportions of the eponymous mastiff.) Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: Perfect Blue
description: A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show.

title: Wicker
description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

title: Macario
description: Vidiots is celebrating Día de los Muertos with a special screening of the haunting Mexican masterpiece Macario .

title: THE TWELVE CHAIRS
description: In 1920s Soviet Russia, a fallen aristocrat, a priest and a con artist search for a treasure of jewels hidden inside one of twelve dining chairs, lost during the revolution.

title: TWENTY YEARS LATER: A MAN MARKED TO DIE - BOOK RELEASE EVENT
description: This evening features a screening of Eduardo Coutinho’s TWENTY YEARS LATER: A MAN MARKED TO DIE (1984), introduced by the internationally acclaimed and Booker-shortlisted writer Itamar Vieira Junior. The evening also celebrates the English publication (by Verso) of Vieira Junior’s new novel, Saving the Fire, which presents the ghosts of a family’s past, lost amid the shadows of Brazil’s history. Vieira Junior masterfully blends the intimate journeys of his characters with faithfully rendered elements of Brazilian life in a world where the scars of colonialism still ache. For more info about Itamar Vieira Junior’s Saving the Fire, visit: https://www.versobooks.com/products/3303-saving-the-fire Eduardo Coutinho TWENTY YEARS LATER: A MAN MARKED TO DIE / CABRA MARCADO PARA MORRER 1984, 119 min, 35mm-to-digital. In Portuguese with English subtitles. “TWENTY YEARS LATER rescues a history doubly interrupted by the brutal military coup of 1964 in Brazil: that of Peasant League activism and of Coutinho’s project, A MAN MARKED TO DIE, a film that was meant to reenact the story of Agrarian Reform struggles leading to the assassination of the Peasant League leader João Pedro Teixeira in 1962. Featuring the leader’s widow and their children, as well as people from a similar community, the film was never finished, and the crew had to flee. In 1981, Coutinho set about locating the actors, in order finally to narrate the history of the Peasant League up to 1964. The 1984 film radiates centripetally from the absence at the core of the interrupted film: its dead protagonist, the assassinated leader. Coutinho was haunted for years by the rushes hidden in a suitcase at a friend’s. He admitted that the original film patronized and idealized the people but claimed to value the unfinished A MAN MARKED TO DIE precisely because of the participation of the organized rural movement. Besides its inordinate value as a record of a traumatic history, the film marks the passage from an idealized documentary representation to a testimonial, reflexive mode incorporating memory and commentary.” –Ivone Margulies

title: Eungyo
description: Renowned poet Lee Juk-yo, 70, has become a recluse, mechanically pushing through his bland days, until they are pleasantly disrupted by high school student Eun-gyo, who comes into his life, bringing fresh energy. Lee starts working on a new novel, the dullness of his life giving way to color, possibilities, even daydreams. But that color starts to dim when Seo Ji-woo, Lee’s former student/assistant, becomes involved with Eun-gyo, and jealousy moves in instead. Based on a novel of the same name by Park Beom-shin, Eungyo explores themes of youth, and the poignant notion of its loss and redemption, with Park Hae-il delivering a notable interpretation of those themes through his character’s numbness and dissociation.

title: The Devils
description: Censored for more than half a century, Ken Russell’s visionary masterpiece returns to the big screen fully restored in 4K and cut to Russell’s direction – the first publicly released version of the film as intended by the filmmaker. Unveiled at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, the definitive version arrives 55 years after the film’s original release. An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, the film lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. In addition to powerhouse performances from Reed and Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils showcases the stunning work of artists at the peak of their craft: Academy Award-winning cinematographer David Watkin ( Out of Africa , Chariots of Fire ); editor Michael Bradsell ( Local Hero , Jabberwocky ); and visual artist Derek Jarman ( Jubilee , Caravaggio ), whose work as production designer marked his feature film debut.

title: Something Special (Willy/Milly)
description: Frustrated by a world in which boys seem to get the best of everything, 14-year-old Milly (Pamela Adlon) makes a wish to swap her sex, and wakes up to find her—or, rather, his—wish has come true. “In my obsession with Something Special, I purchased this 35mm print of it almost 30 years ago. There are a handful of ‘teenage girls passing as boys’ films (She’s the Man is probably the best known). In so many films with gender-crossing characters, the passing is so unconvincing that it renders the film ultimately unsatisfying for a queer audience. But Pamela Adlon’s performance here as Willy is absolutely spectacular.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist Introduction and post-screening discussion by Jenni Olson moderated by filmmaker, film critic and writer Drew Burnett Gregory on Saturday, October 24th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: Rushmore
description: Extracurricular-mad but otherwise unpromising 15-year-old student Max Fisher (Jason Schwartzman) is too busy competing (or so he thinks) with sad sack industrialist Bill Murray for the affections of teacher Olivia Williams to survive “sudden death academic probation” in Anderson’s deeply funny, deeply melancholic—and very class-conscious—sophomore feature. A back-to-school perennial, all dressed up in prep school navy blue and the muted colors of north Texas autumn, positively thrumming with the upstart energy of British Invasion anthems. (“Anderson,” noted admirer Martin Scorsese, “has a fine sense of how music works against an image.”) An irresistible, disarmingly original, delicately wrought comic fable. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: F. W. Murnau’s Faust
description: The haunting tale of a scholar, tempted by the Devil to sign away his soul in exchange for universal knowledge, has been a resonant cultural motif across five centuries. If the essential literary text for the Faustian myth is Johan Wolfgang von Goethe’s 19th century poetic drama, its cinematic equivalent is F. W. Murnau’s visionary 1926 silent adaptation, a masterpiece of haunting visual design that explores rich themes of morality and materialism. Starring Oscar-winning actor Emil Jannings as the terrifying trickster Mephisto, Murnau’s tale emerges from the disturbing underworld into the dreams of lost innocence for one of the most remarkable films from the German Expressionist milieu. A century later, scores of international filmmakers, including Guillermo del Toro, Jennifer Kent, and Robert Eggers, continue to be influenced by this masterwork. The Academy Museum is thrilled to present this film with live accompaniment on the occasion of its centennial and of MUBI’s newest publication, The Faust Bible: The Making of F. W. Murnau’s Masterpiece , which will be available for purchase in the Academy Museum Store. Programmed and note by K.J. Relth-Miller.
director: F. W. Murnau PRODUCED BY: Erich Pommer

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: CITIZEN TOXIE: THE TOXIC AVENGER IV
Primetime
description: Inspired by true events in 2006, "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history. But when a high-stakes operation goes fatally wrong, his veneered dream of fame curdles into a nightmare.

title: Autumn Sonata
description: Ingmar and Ingrid, Bergman and Bergman, together at last. Sweden’s most popular export before the Volvo, in her final screen role, plays a world-renowned concert pianist who returns home to reunite with her now-married daughter (Liv Ullmann), long a distant second to her mother’s career ambitions, the two women exhuming old resentments and struggling towards reconciliation over the course of an emotionally draining 24 hours. “So unrelenting, so harrowing, that I walked out of the theater on shaking legs. If you’re open to the experience that Bergman means to provide, you may leave the film muttering a wrung-out ‘Whew!’ followed quickly by an appreciative ‘Wow!’” —Richard Corliss, Time Magazine Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Midnight in Paris
description: Screenwriter, would-be novelist, and romantic-at-heart Owen Wilson, on vacation in the City of Lights with level-headed fiancée Rachel McAdams, sets out on his own one night after a wine tasting and finds himself suddenly in the Jazz Age Paris of Fitzgerald and Hemingway, Dali and Picasso—an invigorating draught of bohemian freedom that sets our protagonist to seriously interrogating his life choices. “We talked about pushing the color even more in the period scenes, in order to distinguish them from the present-day ones. The Paris of today would be normal and generic, bland and desaturated, and when you entered the Paris of the 1920s the colors would be more warm, lush and flamboyant, with lots of brown and gold and red.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: Paris, Texas
description: A disheveled man who wanders out of the desert, Travis Henderson (Harry Dean Stanton) seems to have no idea who he is. When a stranger manages to contact his brother, Walt (Dean Stockwell), Travis is awkwardly reunited with his sibling. Travis has been missing for years, and his presence unsettles Walt and his family, which also includes Travis's own son, Hunter (Hunter Carson). Soon Travis must confront his wife, Jane (Nastassja Kinski), and try to put his life back together.

title: Your Name [Kimi no Na wa.]
description: Two teenagers share a profound, magical connection upon discovering they are swapping bodies. Things manage to become even more complicated when the boy and girl decide to meet in person.

title: In the Realm of the Senses
description: Still censored in its own country, In the Realm of the Senses (Ai no corrida), by Japanese director Nagisa Oshima, remains one of the most controversial films of all time. A graphic portrayal of insatiable sexual desire, Oshima’s film, set in 1936 and based on a true incident, depicts a man and a woman (Tatsuya Fuji and Eiko Matsuda) consumed by a transcendent, destructive love while living in an era of ever-escalating imperialism and governmental control. Less a work of pornography than of politics, In the Realm of the Senses is a brave, taboo-breaking milestone. Content Warning: This film contains scenes of graphic sex and violence. Further information about content and age-appropriateness for specific films can be found on Common Sense Media , IMDb and DoesTheDogDie.com , as well as through general internet searches.

title: Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler

title: The Cook, the Thief, His Wife & Her Lover
description: When churlish mobster Albert Spica (Michael Gambon) acquires an upscale French restaurant in London, he dines there nightly, effectively scaring off the clientele with his bad manners. His wife, Georgina (Helen Mirren), is especially disgusted by him, and soon begins an affair with another restaurant guest, Michael (Alan Howard). Despite their efforts to keep it a secret, however, Spica finds out about their trysts, and he plans to exact a terrible revenge.

title: Cinematic Void Presents EUREKA
description: Gene Hackman, Mickey Rourke, Rutger Hauer and Theresa Russell are the all-star players in the strange tale, set in the Canadian Wilderness, about a gold prospector who, after a gold strike, moves to a Carribbean island where his reward will be misery and paranoia and pursuit by killers.

title: RIM BATTAL - BOOK RELEASE EVENT
description: To celebrate the publication of the English translation of writer Rim Battal’s autobiographical novel I’ll Look Myself in the Eyes, Anthology presents a special screening of MUSTANG (2015), by Turkish filmmaker Deniz Gamze Ergüven, a film that’s closely tied thematically to Battal’s text. In I’ll Look Myself in the Eyes 17-year-old Rim is caught smoking out her window in her home in Marrakesh, Morocco. This minor transgression unleashes the fury of her mother, who demands that Rim complete a gynecological test certifying her virginity. So begins a nuanced journey into the tangled web of a patriarchal society in which various generations of women seem to complicitly preserve the status quo. Ultimately, it is Rim who breaks the cycle of dysfunction, rebels against tradition, confronts betrayal from the women closest to her, and dares to be her true self. MUSTANG, co-written by Alice Winocour, similarly explores the internalized psychological and moral impact of the patriarchy, through the story of five orphaned sisters growing up with their grandmother and uncle. When, on their way home from school, they play an innocent game with a group of boys on the beach, their grandmother flies into a rage, accusing them of having “pleasured themselves” and forbidding them from leaving the house. Things quickly escalate with the threat of arranged marriages. As in Rim’s novel, we see how far families can go wrong in their perceived mission of protecting the purity of their girls. The screening will be followed by a bilingual reading from the novel by author Rim Battal and her translator Liza Tripp, along with a discussion and audience Q&A. For more info about I’ll Look Myself in the Eyes, visit: https://www.galiotpress.com/authors/rim-battal Deniz Gamze Ergüven MUSTANG 2015, 97 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In Turkish with English subtitles.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Arrival: A Conversation with Denis Villeneuve and Dr. Nina Beguš
description: Inspired by Denis Villeneuve's 2016 sci-fi drama Arrival, the director joins artificial-humanities scholar Dr. Nina Beguš live in the David Geffen Theater for an inspiring conversation about how language acts as a technology; how fiction shapes artificial intelligence; and how encounters with non-human intelligence might transform our most basic understanding of thinking, learning, consciousness, time, and more. To mark the 10th anniversary of this thought-provoking film, an 8pm screening follows the discussion. About Nina Beguš Nina Beguš is a scholar and author working on AI, literature, and film. She is a researcher at the University of California, Berkeley, where she leads the Artificial Humanities research group. Her work examines how stories, concepts, and cultural archetypes shape technology. She is the author of Artificial Humanities: A Fictional Perspective on Language in AI and the editor of First Encounters with AI: Writers on Writing . Beguš holds a PhD in comparative literature from Harvard University and edits the Artificial Humanities book series at the University of Exeter Press. About Denis Villeneuve Denis Villeneuve is an Academy Award-nominated director, screenwriter and producer whose masterful world-building and unique visuals have established him as one of the premier filmmakers working today. In 2021, Dune: Part One earned six Academy Awards and multiple guild and critics' awards. Its sequel, Dune: Part Two (2024), expanded with bolder visual ambition and complexity, surpassing $700 million worldwide and winning two Academy Awards, with additional recognition from BAFTA, Critics Choice and major guilds. Villeneuve will conclude the trilogy with Dune: Part Three this December, reuniting its core cast. He is also set to direct the next James Bond film for Amazon MGM Studios. About the film In director Denis Villeneuve’s thoughtful science-fiction drama, adapted from Ted Chiang’s award-winning novella Story of Your Life , a linguistics expert (Amy Adams) is recruited by the government when massive alien spaceships suddenly land across the globe. The film’s production designer, Patrice Vermette (nominated with set decorator Paul Hotte) also designed the film’s alien language—one of Arrival ’s many remarkable and imaginative visuals. The film was nominated in seven categories, including Best Picture and Production Design; it won an Oscar for Sound Editing.

title: LONDON FESTIVAL OF QUEER SPANISH CULTURE: LA BOLA NEGRA
description: LA BOLA NEGRA tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain and inheritance, across three different eras – 1932, 1937 and 2017. Rich with Lorca's poetry and suffused with desire, grief and hope, it is an intimate love story and a sweeping exploration of memor...

title: British Horror Studio: In the Grip of Terror
description: Introducing a season from the British Horror Studio. An independent British film studio Focusing on Gothic drama and arthouse filmmaking with a distinctive British horror character. In the Grip of Terror marks the long-awaited return of Amicus Productions, the legendary British horror banner famed for its classic portmanteau films. Revived through the British Horror Studio, the picture restores the anthology tradition with a new collection of sinister tales bound together by dread, guilt, psychological torment, and the creeping sense that some stories should never be told aloud. Set within a shadowed world of troubled patients, strange confessions, and institutional unease, the film brings together a repertory cast led by Megan Tremethick, with appearances from Golden Globe nominee Jane Merrow, Laurence R. Harvey, Dorian Todd, Sam McMillan, Michael Daviot, Novarro Ramon, Nick Ford, and Lawrie Brewster https://www.britishhorrorstudio.com/

title: What Ever Happened To Baby Jane?
description: *ON SALE 23rd OCT * Jane Hudson (Bette Davis) is an aging child star left to care for her wheelchair-bound sister Blanche (Joan Crawford), also a former child actress. Stuck living together in a mansion in old Hollywood, Blanche plots to get even with Jane for the car crash that left her crippled years earlier. But Jane is desperate to keep Blanche imprisoned as she plans a new rise to fame, and tries to hide Blanche's existence from doctors, visitors and neighbors while she devises a way to get rid of her sister.

title: The Last Princess
description: In the early 20th century, the last princess of the Korean royal family under Japanese rule is forced to move to Japan to attend school, leaving behind her family, friends, and the only home she has ever known. Kim Jang-han (Park Hae-il), a childhood friend and Japanese army officer, helps to plan an escape route for her. This film, based on the real story of Princess Deokhye (Son Ye-jin), weaves fact with fiction to retell the story of a once-lost princess who stopped at nothing to return to the home she yearned for. –note written by Hannah Farkas.

title: Godzilla (1954)
description: Godzilla is the roaring granddaddy of all monster movies. It’s also a remarkably humane and melancholy drama, made in Japan at a time when the country was reeling from nuclear attack and H-bomb testing in the Pacific. Its rampaging radioactive beast, the poignant embodiment of an entire population’s fears, became a beloved international icon of destruction, spawning almost thirty sequels.

title: Antichrist
description: While a married couple (Willem Dafoe, Charlotte Gainsbourg) is having sex, their infant son in a nearby room falls out a window to his death. She becomes distraught and is hospitalized, but her husband, who is a psychiatrist, attempts to treat her. Deciding that she needs to face her fears, he takes her to a cabin in the woods where she spent a previous summer with the boy. Once they are there, she becomes more unhinged and starts perpetrating sexual violence on her husband and herself.

title: Heat
description: A group of high-end professional thieves start to feel the heat from the LAPD when they unknowingly leave a verbal clue at their latest heist. Original Cut from a 35mm print.

title: Black Narcissus
description: This explosive work about the conflict between the spirit and the flesh is the epitome of the sensuous style of Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger. A group of nuns—played by some of Britain's finest actresses, including Deborah Kerr, Kathleen Byron, and Flora Robson—struggle to establish a convent in the Himalayas, while isolation, extreme weather, altitude, and culture clashes all conspire to drive the well-intentioned missionaries mad. A darkly grand film that won Oscars for Alfred Junge's art direction and Jack Cardiff's cinematography, Black Narcissus is one of the greatest achievements by two of cinema's true visionaries.

title: Souls of Sin 35 mm & Miracle in Harlem 35 mm (12)
The Zone of Interest
description: The commandant of Auschwitz, Rudolf Höss, and his wife Hedwig, strive to build a dream life for their family in a house and garden next to the camp.The commandant of Auschwitz, Rudolf Höss, and his wife Hedwig, strive to build a dream life for their family in a house and garden next to the camp.

title: Nova '78
description: A time capsule of the 1978 Nova Convention, bringing together never-before-seen footage recovered from Howard Brookner’s archive, featuring William S. Burroughs, Philip Glass, Frank Zappa, Patti Smith, Laurie Anderson and other cultural radicals at the explosive crossroads of punk, performance, literature and the avant-garde.

title: MARDI GRAS MASSACRE
description:
While New Orleans parties, a ritual killer turns its nightlife into his hunting ground. Detectives follow a trail of sacrifices through bars, bedrooms and the clammy underside of the carnival.
Jack Weis’s notorious regional splatter film mixes a police procedural with disco-era sleaze and the primitive shock tactics of BLOOD FEAST. Its rough surfaces are part of the experience: a drive-in nightmare with no studio polish to soften the impact. A deeply disreputable entry in the history of the British video-nasty panic.

title: Remake
description: With a special introduction from non-fiction filmmaking legend Ross McElwee at the Sunday, November 1st screening!

title: MY BROTHER'S KILLER
description: In West Hollywood, a gay adult performer’s brutal murder went cold for decades. When filmmakers began documenting his story, the community’s involvement led to shocking discoveries through vintage footage linking suspects to the crime.

title: DATE WITH A KIDNAPPER
description:
An abduction on the backroads becomes a strange, uneasy battle of wills. As a young woman and her captor travel through the rural South, the expected rules of the hostage thriller begin to slip.
Frederick R. Friedel’s regional independent filmmaking gives the danger an unusually intimate texture: dusty locations, awkward silences and people who never quite fit the roles the plot has assigned them. Also known as KIDNAPPED COED, this is a rough-edged drive-in discovery whose unsettling unpredictability is its strongest weapon.

title: Doc'n'Roll FF: 7 Days In May: Mac Demarco and Ryan Paris + Q&A
Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: La La Land
description: Sebastian (Ryan Gosling) and Mia (Emma Stone) are drawn together by their common desire to do what they love. But as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart.

title: Dogtooth [Kynodontas]
description: Newly restored in 4K, DOGTOOTH follows a controlling, manipulative father who locks his three adult children in a state of perpetual childhood by keeping them prisoner within the sprawling family compound.

title: Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler

title: Lost Boundaries (12)
description: This 1949 American drama looks at how 'liberal ideals' presented on screen back then; in which the groundbreaking filmmaker William Greaves stars as a young college graduate.

title: Fantastic Planet
description: On the planet Ygam, the Draags, extremely technologically and spiritually advanced blue humanoids, consider the tiny Oms, human beings descendants of Terra's inhabitants, as ignorant animals. Those who live in slavery are treated as simple pets and used to entertain Draag children; those who live hidden in the hostile wilderness of the planet are periodically hunted and ruthlessly slaughtered as if they were vermin.

title: Doc'n'Roll FF: KitKatClub: Kinks of Berlin + Q&A (zoom)
Nova '78
description: A time capsule of the 1978 Nova Convention, bringing together never-before-seen footage recovered from Howard Brookner’s archive, featuring William S. Burroughs, Philip Glass, Frank Zappa, Patti Smith, Laurie Anderson and other cultural radicals at the explosive crossroads of punk, performance, literature and the avant-garde.

title: SEX WORLD
description:
An exclusive resort promises to make its guests’ fantasies real. Arriving strangers bring desires they can name and anxieties they cannot; the encounters soon reveal a gap between getting what you want and understanding why you want it.
Anthony Spinelli borrows the polished surfaces and speculative premise of seventies science fiction for an unusually ambitious adult ensemble film. Interlocking stories, sleek production design and an electronic score give its experiments in intimacy a distinctive atmosphere. A key example of porno chic treating fantasy as both an attraction and a problem.
This film contains hardcore unsimulated sex scenes.

title: BORED TEENAGERS
description: [BRENNENDE LANGEWEILE] “In the late 1970s, Wolfgang Büld first made a name for himself with his documentary PUNK IN LONDON. The follow-up to this authentic document of youth culture was the ZDF production BORED TEENAGERS, part of the “Das kleine Fernsehspiel” series; it was filmed in 1979 in the wake of the RAF panic – wanted posters are visible in the background several times throughout the film. The movie blends concert footage of the English punk band The Adverts with a loose narrative thread about a young punk named Peter and his hairdresser girlfriend, Karin, as they follow the band – led by TV Smith and Gaye Advert – on their tour through Germany. It is an entertaining yet quirky journey through a late-70s musical subculture.” –OX-FANZINE

title: OUR HERO, BALTHAZAR
description: Ultra-wealthy NYC teenager Balthy makes dramatic gun control videos to impress his activist crush. When an online troll targets his content, Balthy becomes convinced he’s communicating with a potential school shooter and embarks on an ill-advised journey to Texas to confront him.

title: THE DRAWING CENTER PRESENTS: FORM, SHADOW, MOTION (FREE SCREENING!)
description: This program of artist films and videos is presented in conjunction with The Drawing Center’s current exhibition “Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from the Burger Collection, Hong Kong”, opening on October 23, 2026 and on view until January 2027. The screening showcases a selection of artist pieces that extend the exhibition's visual essay on shared historical, poetic, and philosophical concerns, with Hong Kong and New York as twin points of reference and Eastern thought and Western philosophy as its guiding frameworks. “Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from the Burger Collection, Hong Kong” is organized by Olivia Shao, Burger Collection & TOY Meets Art Curator. Cici Wu UNFINISHED RETURN OF YU MAN HON (2019, 19 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Tang Kwok Hin GRANDPA TANG (2017, 13 min, DCP) Chan Hau Chun THE MEMORY OF A CICADA IS LONGER THAN ITS LIFE (2024, 12 min, DCP. Music and sound: Chui Chi Yin.) Simon Liu PROCEDURES (2026, 17 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: Primetime
description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history. When a high stakes operation goes fatally wrong, his veneered dream of fame curdles into a nightmare of performative justice.

title: Mystery Movie
description: Don't miss our fan favourite MYSTERY MOVIE screenings! On a near weekly basis we will serve up a random mystery movie, with No Clues and No Hints as to what they will be. In 2026, we'll be presenting these as STAFF CURATED selections each and every week by our lovely Front of House, Duty Manager, and Projection Team! You can find the schedule below: --- You can find a list of every MYSTERY MOVIE we have ever screened HERE ; if a film is on this list, it is not eligible for future Mystery Movie screenings! --- Content Advice : As these films are a mystery, we aren't able to provide specific ratings / guidance on the film's content. We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: My Dad is 100 Years Old with Rome, Open City
description: My Dad Is 100 Years Old This short tribute casts celebrated actress Isabella Rossellini as herself as well as various filmmakers who influenced or were influenced by her father, filmmaker Roberto Rossellini. Conceived by Isabella on the eve of her father’s centenary, she took a “docu-fantasia” concept to avant-garde filmmaker Guy Maddin after her delightful experience on his 2003 feature, The Saddest Music in the World. A beautiful cinema poem for a beloved father and artist.
director: Guy Maddin PRODUCED BY: Jody Shapiro

title: The Devils
description: Censored for more than half a century, Ken Russell’s visionary masterpiece returns to the big screen fully restored in 4K and cut to Russell’s direction – the first publicly released version of the film as intended by the filmmaker. Unveiled at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, the definitive version arrives 55 years after the film’s original release. An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, the film lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. In addition to powerhouse performances from Reed and Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils showcases the stunning work of artists at the peak of their craft: Academy Award-winning cinematographer David Watkin ( Out of Africa , Chariots of Fire ); editor Michael Bradsell ( Local Hero , Jabberwocky ); and visual artist Derek Jarman ( Jubilee , Caravaggio ), whose work as production designer marked his feature film debut.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: CAMP - A SHORT FILM SHOWCASE
description:
THE NICKEL teams up with cyberfemme studio EVERYONE IS A GIRL for a showcase of short films centred on the theme of CAMP, accompanied with readings.
The Nickel Cinema’s regular roster of B-movies, softcores, and underrated gems has begun to shed some buttery spotlight on underrepresented cinematic traditions. At EIAG, we make collaborative projects about the feminine, the seductive, the virtual, and the covert. For this CAMP showcase, we are joining forces to present films from our community that are not afraid to play, deceive, and perform. Join us for a night of London’s most sparkliest, performative, abject, delicious, and scandalicious emerging cinema.
Programme of films to be announced.

title: Memories of Murder
description: Bong Joon Ho’s phenomenal breakthrough film stars Park Hae-il as an enigmatic young loner and observer whose innocent demeanor seems too wholesome to be true. Inspired by a true story, Memories of Murder centers around the gruesome serial killings of women in South Korea in the 1980s, investigated by Doo-man (Song Kang-ho), a detective who relies on instinct rather than fact. Bong’s vision, which challenges conventional components of storytelling and blurs the boundaries between genres, is meticulously orchestrated in this crime thriller, and Park’s elegantly simple depiction of a complicated character is phenomenal.

title: RIOTS AND LOVE
description: [RANDALE UND LIEBE – ROCKER, POPPER, TEDS UND PUNKS] “Thomas Schmitt’s film offers unique insights into the alternative subculture of 1980s Cologne. Depending on the concert, the Blue-Shell attracted rockers, punks, and Teddy Boys, while the Café d’Or was a popular hangout for the ‘Popper’ crowd. RANDALE UND LIEBE – ROCKER, POPPER, TEDS UND PUNKS is a magnificent document of its time.” –COLOGNE CINEMA NIGHTS

title: Taste of Cherry
description: Winner of the Palme d’Or at the 1997 Cannes Film Festival, Iranian auteur Abbas Kiarostami’s _Taste of Cherry_ is an emotionally complex meditation on life and death. Middle-aged Mr. Badii (Homayoun Ershadi) drives through the hilly outskirts of Tehran—searching for someone to rescue or bury him.

title: The Last Temptation of Christ
description: Jesus, a humble Judean carpenter beginning to see that he is the son of God, is drawn into revolutionary action against the Roman occupiers by Judas - despite his protestations that love, not violence, is the path to salvation. The burden of being the saviour of mankind torments Jesus throughout his life, leading him to doubt. As he is put to death on the cross, Jesus is tempted by visions of an ordinary life married to Mary Magdalene.

title: The Godfather
description: Widely regarded as one of the greatest films of all time, this mob drama, based on Mario Puzo's novel of the same name, focuses on the powerful Italian-American crime family of Don Vito Corleone (Marlon Brando). When the don's youngest son, Michael (Al Pacino), reluctantly joins the Mafia, he becomes involved in the inevitable cycle of violence and betrayal. Although Michael tries to maintain a normal relationship with his wife, Kay (Diane Keaton), he is drawn deeper into the family business.

title: Salo, Or The 120 Days of Sodom
description: Four corrupted fascist libertines round up 9 teenage boys and girls and subject them to 120 days of sadistic physical, mental and sexual torture.

title: THE MUSICAL
description: The PROOF Film Festival is thrilled to announce to screen THE MUSICAL, the feature length version of the 2024 PROOF Film Festival audience award winner. Starring Will Brill, Rob Lowe and Gillian Jacobs, we are so proud of filmmaker Giselle Bonilla and screenwriter & producer Alexander Heller as they bring this hilarious feature that began as a short to the masses.

title: LIVE WIRE
description:
Washington’s politicians are exploding without warning. Bomb-disposal expert Danny O’Neill has to find the weapon before the next victim discovers they are carrying it inside them. His collapsing marriage is about to become part of the investigation.
Pierce Brosnan brings immaculate pre-Bond composure to a thriller with absolutely no intention of behaving sensibly. Liquid explosives, political conspiracy and domestic melodrama race towards the same detonation. Christian Duguay keeps the set pieces moving and the premise gloriously overheated: early-nineties action with an unusually volatile ingredient.

title: NO FUTURE + ALLET UNITED – PUNK IM POTT
description: Michael Braun NO FUTURE – KEIN BOCK AUF ILLUSIONEN 1981, 44 min, 16mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. “In 1981, film and television producer Michael Braun made this film (which for a long time circulated only on atrociously poor-quality VHS copies) about the punk scene in Duisburg, featuring Willi Wucher, the band ARTLESS, and – here and there – Bernie Blitz (RIP). It is a journey back to the early 1980s, to the Ruhr region…back when the area was even bleaker than it is today. In the 80s, Braun hosted the ‘Michael Braun Talkshow’ on WDR television, featuring guests such as the bands DAF and Östro 430; the show was an early precursor to today's late-night talk shows.” –COMPUTERSTAAT Detlev Puls ALLET UNITED – PUNK IM POTT 1983, 25 min, 16mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. This short film – made for German television during the summer of 1983 – focuses on the punk scene in the industrial Ruhr region, and features the bands Die Kanzlers and Starkbier, members of which later went on to form Body Checks. Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: I Hate Myself and Want to Die
description: Join us in the microcinema for a refreshing dark comedy that will give you life – J. Davis’ acerbically hilarious I Hate Myself and Want to Die . Jacob is an unrealized artist, freshly dumped, who’s come home to the desert to quietly end his life. The problem is, nothing goes according to plan. His mom needs a ride to the drugstore, his cousin needs a shoulder to cry on, and his best friend just wants to get high. Over a crazy night of parties, fistfights and car chases, Jacob rethinks his life and— maybe—his death.

title: ASILAH OUI: MELEHI + A THOUSAND AND ONE BERBER NIGHTS
description: This screening – presented on the occasion of the Robert Blackburn Printmaking Workshop’s exhibition “Asilah Oui: Robert Blackburn in Morocco” – pairs two films that explore the links between Morocco and New York: Shalom Gorewitz’s MELEHI (1984) and Hisham Aïdi’s A THOUSAND AND ONE BERBER NIGHTS (2023), which together examine two pioneers of Moroccan art in the twentieth century. Commissioned as part of his 1984 solo exhibition at the Bronx Museum, MELEHI documents the work and life of renowned Moroccan painter and Asilah Cultural Moussem founder Mohamed Melehi through his projects as a teacher, painter, and modernist. Forty years after its production, MELEHI provides a career snapshot of the artist contextualized by his influences across the Moroccan landscape, placing him in the larger history of Morocco and its visual culture. A THOUSAND AND ONE BERBER NIGHTS delves into the transatlantic career of dancer, actor, and choreographer Hassan Ouakrim. In the late 1950s, Ouakrim was a young dancer and actor in Morocco. Little did he know that he would soon become the protegé of La Mama Theatre founder Ellen Stewart, performing across America, forming friendships with the likes of jazz virtuosos Ornette Coleman and Randy Weston, and becoming a pioneer in spreading Berber dance and music in North America. “Asilah Oui: Robert Blackburn in Morocco” at the Blackburn Study Center, September 15-December 12, 2026, focuses on the first decade of the Asilah Cultural Moussem. Established in 1978, this international festival brought together printmakers, musicians, intellectuals, and poets from around the globe to create, as founders Mohamed Benaissa and Mohamad Melehi described it, “a permanent center for cultural diffusion, rich in authenticity and steeped in heritage.” The exhibition illuminates how Robert Blackburn’s Printmaking Workshop served as a conduit in connecting the Moussem’s international artists. This screening is organized by the Robert Blackburn Printmaking Workshop, and co-presented with the Bronx Museum. For more info about the exhibition, visit: https://www.rbpmw-efanyc.org/asilah-oui

title: Pink Palace: WHO KILLED TEDDY BEAR
description: Pink Palace and Lobotomy Room (devoted to Bad Movies for Bad People) present this tough as nails gritty thriller from the mean streets of sixties New York.  We invite you to take a walk on the wild side with this boundary-pushing and ultra-tawdry 1965 exploitation b-movie. Hip, independent and moder...

title: National Theatre Live: Golden Boy
description: Josh O’Connor (The Crown; Challengers) leads the cast in this searing revival of Clifford Odets’ knockout American classic. 1930s New York, at the height of the Depression. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. He must confront what he’s willing to sacrifice, who he’s willing to become and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side. Brought to life with a live string quartet and filmed live from the Almeida Theatre. Olivier Award-winner Sam Yates (Vanya) directs this propulsive drama exploring ambition, identity, and the high price of success.

title: Viva Ingrid! with Journey to Italy
description: Viva Ingrid! A moving documentary tribute to a mother, wife, and actress, this mix of home movies, newsreels, and clips from films by Roberto Rossellini paints a shortform portrait of three-time Academy Award-winning Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman, as realized by one of Rossellini’s grandsons.

title: NFTS Collective Visions of Pleasure: Shakedown
BULKY TRASH + THE FREE ORCHESTRA
description: Helke Misselwitz BULKY TRASH / SPERRMÜLL 1990, 72 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. Filmed in the early summer of 1989, this documentary portrays a band of four young musicians who call themselves “Sperrmüll” (“Bulky Trash”), thanks to their proclivity for producing music by drumming on other people’s discarded items. Misselwitz concentrates especially on Enrico, who decides to stay behind when his mother Erika marries in the West, and who insists on maintaining his cultural identity even after the fall of the Wall. The members of “Sperrmüll” wish to remain citizens of their own state, and their attitude towards the looming reunification is one of skepticism. Originally intended as a call for social change, Misselwitz’s film documents the events of the Wende from the perspective of young East Berliners. Preceded by: Petra Tschörtner THE FREE ORCHESTRA / DAS FREIE ORCHESTER 1988, 17 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. “Day in, day out, Barbara sells screws at a store in the East Berlin Market Hall. She is frustrated about having to tell her customers most of the time: ‘Ham wa nich!’ (‘We don’t have that!’) In the evening, she is the loud and wild singer of the legendary East Berlin avantgarde and punk band Das Freie Orchester. Playing music with her friends helps her escape the monotony of her job, express her dissatisfaction with everyday life in East Germany in the 1980s, and dream of a different life.” –DEFA FILM LIBRARY Total running time: ca. 95 min.

title: RICOCHET
description:
One arrest makes Nick Styles a television hero. Years later, the man he put away comes back with a plan to destroy everything the cameras helped him build: career, family, reputation and trust in his own mind.
Denzel Washington and John Lithgow turn Russell Mulcahy’s revenge thriller into a ferocious contest between charisma and obsession. Lithgow’s villain does not just want his enemy dead; he wants control of the story everyone tells about him. Fast, lurid and wildly excessive, RICOCHET pushes studio action towards a full-blown media nightmare.

title: V For Vendetta
description: In a future British dystopian society, a shadowy freedom fighter, known only by the alias of "V", plots to overthrow the tyrannical government - with the help of a young woman.

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
description: After a painful breakup, Clementine (Kate Winslet) undergoes a procedure to erase memories of her former boyfriend Joel (Jim Carrey) from her mind. When Joel discovers that Clementine is going to extremes to forget their relationship, he undergoes the same procedure and slowly begins to forget the woman that he loved. Directed by former music video director Michel Gondry, the visually arresting film explores the intricacy of relationships and the pain of loss.

title: Excalibur
description: Arthur fulfills his fate by bringing together the Knights of the Round Table at Camelot and unifying the country. However, this flawed monarch faces greater tests ahead in pursuit of love, the Holy Grail, and his nation's survival.

title: Short Cuts : 35mm Roadshow Tour
description: A multi-storied, fish-eyed look at the human condition against the backdrop of contemporary middle-class LA. Twenty two characters intersect, profoundly and fleetingly, through each other’s lives. It runs the emotional gamut from disturbing to humorous. Don't miss a rare opportunity to see Robert Altman's sprawling epic, showing from an original 35mm print as part of our SHORT CUTS 35mm Roadshow Tour. The 35mm Roadshow Tour will begin at the Prince Charles Cinema, before heading to other sites across the UK in a limited run this November. Special thanks to David Levy for helping us make this happen, and to Curzon for giving us and participating sites access to their print.

title: Everytime
description: After a shocking accident befalls a teenage girl in Berlin, her mother, younger sister, and boyfriend drift into a state of suspended grief in Sandra Wollner’s atmospheric, constantly surprising new film, winner of the Cannes Un Certain Regard Prize. Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: GODS OF TIMES SQUARE
description:
Before the corporate billboards swallowed the skyline, Times Square had other voices: street preachers, prophets, conspiracy theorists and people who believed the end was close. Richard Sandler turns his camera towards the pavement and lets them speak.
Filmed across years of transformation, this extraordinary documentary listens to a neighbourhood arguing about God while the ground changes beneath it. Comic, unsettling, tender and apocalyptic by turns, it preserves personalities no redevelopment plan could accommodate. A city symphony made from competing sermons and the stubborn human need to be heard.

title: The Fifth Element
description: The Earth is about to be destroyed by a huge ball of fire racing toward the planet. Cornelius, an old monk, knows how to stop the burning sphere with the help of Korben Dallas, a taxi driver and former secret agent and a woman named Leeloo.

description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebel...

title: GIRLS BITE BACK + ROAD MOVIE
description: Wolfgang Büld GIRLS BITE BACK aka WOMEN IN ROCK 1980, 45 min, 16mm-to-DCP. In English and German with English subtitles. “Canvassing a selection of female musicians squarely at the forefront of the post-punk tide, director Wolfgang Büld finds plenty of restless, spiky personalities and intriguing approaches to music and performance. Metal-heads Girlschool, tribal dub merchants The Slits, No Wave experimentalists Mania D, and operatic rock diva Nina Hagen are all featured in live performances, but best of all is a supremely sarcastic Siouxsie Sioux, filmed and interviewed on tour in Berlin.” –SCHAMROCK LiLiPUT ROAD MOVIE 1982/2006, 29 min, Super-8mm-to-digital Recorded in 1982 by the legendary all-female Swiss punk band LiLiPUT (née Kleenex) while on the road, the film captures both the exhilaration and the tedium of touring. Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: Doc'n'Roll FF: The Best Summer + Q&A
WHO KILLED CAPTAIN ALEX?
description:
Captain Alex is dead, the army wants answers and the Tiger Mafia is taking the fight into the skies above Kampala. Revenge arrives by gunfight, kung fu and helicopter, while Video Joker Emmie supplies a running commentary no conventional action film could survive.
Nabwana I.G.G. and the Wakaliwood team turn scant resources into outrageous invention. The effects are homemade, the commitment is total and the pleasure of making movies is everywhere on screen. An action sensation whose real superpower is the unstoppable creative energy of a community.

title: LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET
description: THE THEATER OF THE MATTERS & TAUFIC PRESENT: JEAN-CLAUDE ROUSSEAU’S ‘THE PASTORAL CONCERT’ + ‘LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET’ This book launch event celebrates the release of Jean-Claude Rousseau’s unclassifiable, long-unavailable film text, The Pastoral Concert, published for the first time in English this October by Taufic. The evening will culminate in a special premiere screening of Rousseau’s new feature film, LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET (winner of a Jury Special Mention at this year’s FIDMarseille), alongside his 2006 short, FAUX DÉPART. The Pastoral Concert marks the first English translation of Rousseau’s early written work Le Concert champêtre, begun in 1968, some fifteen years before his debut film. Rousseau continued shaping the work as a screenplay until its rejection by the Centre National de la Cinématographie in 1983. Unrealized, Le Concert champêtre became the matrix from which Rousseau’s subsequent films would emerge. Taking its title and three central characters (A, B, and C) from the eponymous painting long attributed to Giorgione and now to Titian, The Pastoral Concert begins as a letter written by a young man to his cousin in the countryside on the eve of her wedding, before mutating into a diary entry, a screenplay, and finally a film imagined through the failure of its own realization. In this restless fluctuation between registers, The Pastoral Concert expresses, in the words of Jean-Marie Straub, “something magnificent [and] entirely different from a screenplay or a découpage.” Translated from the French by artist and filmmaker Kevin Weil, this edition includes an extensive appendix of extra-diegetic materials written by Rousseau, as well as correspondence with contemporaries such as Dominique Noguez, Marcel Hanoun, and Jean-Marie Straub, which form a picture of the work’s early reception. For more info about The Pastoral Concert visit: https://taufic.org/the-pastoral-concert Jean-Claude Rousseau LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET / DERNIER ARRÊT POUR LE BILLET CIRCULAIRE 2026, 87 min, DCP. No dialogue. Rousseau’s longest film since THE ENCLOSED VALLEY from 1995 (the summit of his 8mm era), LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET refers to the looped ferry route that plies the waters of Lake Como in Northern Italy. Firmly grounded in place, Rousseau’s solitary camera finds desolate poetry in the void of the spectacular landscape and in the anonymous crowds of passengers seemingly entranced at the edge of an abyss. Musical chords and voices magnify their gestures and the movement of the vessel on the lake. Closing the circle, the specter of the end looms: “On the ferry, among the travelers, I recognized Mrs. Death…” Preceded by: Jean-Claude Rousseau FAUX DÉPART (2006, 13 min, DCP. No dialogue.)

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Take a seat without knowing what is coming. Our mystery screenings explore the bold, disreputable and gloriously unclassifiable world of psychotronic cinema: discoveries that make you wonder how they were made, who they were made for, and why nobody showed you sooner.
The title stays secret until showtime. Curiosity is essential; good taste is negotiable.
Strictly for adult audiences. Films may contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: Everytime
description: After a shocking accident befalls a teenage girl in Berlin, her mother, younger sister, and boyfriend drift into a state of suspended grief in Sandra Wollner’s atmospheric, constantly surprising new film, winner of the Cannes Un Certain Regard Prize. Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: WILD HORSE NINE
description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebel...

title: EINSTURZENDE NEUBAUTEN: LIEBESLIEDER
description: An essential text for anyone with a love for the avant-garde. The explosive soundscapes of industrial music titans Einstürzende Neubauten first shook Berlin – then the whole world – to its core in the 1980s. In LIEBESLIEDER, co-directors Klaus Maeck and Johanna Schenkel wield a fractured feast of killer Neubauten performances from Euro television: ones that highlight the group’s cinematic presence, wild handmade instruments, and totally unique style. For those who are at all curious about industrial or noise music in general, this sweaty documentary is unmissable. For Neubauten fans, this humanizing portrait of their first decade provides a fresh take on the band.

title: Mikey and Nicky
description: Our performance on 14th October is presented with an introduction by Christina Newland Elaine May crafted a gangster film like no other in the nocturnal odyssey Mikey and Nicky, capitalising on the chemistry between frequent collaborators John Cassavetes and Peter Falk by casting them together as small-time mobsters whose lifelong relationship has turned sour. Set over the course of one night, this restless drama finds Nicky (Cassavetes) holed up in a hotel after the boss he stole money from puts a hit out on him. Terrified, he calls on Mikey (Falk), the one person he thinks can save him. Scripted to match the live-wire energy of its stars—alongside supporting players Ned Beatty, Joyce Van Patten, and Carol Grace—and inspired by real-life characters from May’s own childhood, this unbridled portrait of male friendship turned tragic is an unsung masterpiece of American cinema. Our performance on 14th October is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Rio Forever Cult Lates: FLESH GORDON + GUMS
description: Pink Palace presents two cult midnight movies that screened at the Rio back in the 70’s. Trashy low budget porn parodies were very common in this era, and there are two of the very best... hilarious, stupid, unerotic and mercifully short!  First up is the jaw dropping sex comedy Flesh Gordon, a porn...
director: Michael Benveniste + Howard Ziehm / Robert J Kaplan

title: THE WOMEN
description: Norma Shearer, Joan Crawford and Rosalind Russell star in George Cukor’s classic comedy, based on the play by Clare Booth Luce. The star-studded cast consists entirely of women (with over 130 speaking roles) and follows a group of Manhattanites, who convince their happily married friend to leave her husband after he strays.

title: FFC: Coco (PG)
description: One of Pixar’s most complex creations, Coco takes the audience from a village in Mexico to the Land of the Dead in this utterly beautiful, musical family drama.

description: Maya and her dad, director Michel Gondry (Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind) live in different countries As a way to…

title: The Haunted Mansion
description: Based on the iconic Disneyland ride, The Haunted Mansion stars Eddie Murphy as real estate agent Jim Evers, a workaholic who wants to close a mansion deal before going on a much-needed vacation with his wife, Sara, and his kids. Upon their arrival, the family is lured apart by ghosts who believe Sara can set them free by joining them in the afterlife. The Evers family battles ghosts, zombies, and spiders to save Sara from eternal damnation, also encountering – of course -- references to the amusement park ride, including Hidden Mickeys and the theme song, “Grim Grinning Ghosts.”
director: Rob Minkoff PRODUCED BY: Don Hahn, Andrew Gunn

title: Chungking Express
description: Every day, Cop 223 (Takeshi Kaneshiro) buys a can of pineapple with an expiration date of May 1, symbolizing the day he'll get over his lost love. He's also got his eye on a mysterious woman in a blond wig (Brigitte Lin), oblivious of the fact she's a drug dealer. Cop 663 (Tony Leung Chiu Wai) is distraught with heartbreak over a breakup. But when his ex drops a spare set of his keys at a local cafe, a waitress (Faye Wong) lets herself into his apartment and spruces up his life.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Porco Rosso (English Dubbed)
description: From the legendary Studio Ghibli , creators of Spirited Away , and Academy Award-winning director Hayao Miyazaki , comes a dazzling aerial adventure set in and above the scenic port towns of the Adriatic Sea. “Porco Rosso” is a world-weary flying ace-turned-bounty-hunter, whose face has been transformed into that of a pig by a mysterious spell. When he infuriates a band of sky pirates with his heroics, the pirates hire Curtis, a hotshot American rival, to get rid of him. But with the help of the teenage girl Fio, an aspiring airplane designer, and a sultry lounge singer named Gina, Porco takes to the skies for what may be his final high-flying showdown.

title: Bugsy Malone
description: It is 1929 in New York and the city is divided by gang warfare. On one side, Dandy Dan's mob terrorise the district, taking out those they turn against with their new splurge guns. On the other side, Dandy Dan's rival, Fat Sam, runs his successful Grand Slam Speakeasy.

title: HARD BOILED
description:
A teahouse erupts. A warehouse becomes a battlefield. Then a hospital turns into an action sequence that seems determined to test the limits of cinema itself. Inspector Tequila and an undercover cop are on the same side—if they can survive long enough to prove it.
Chow Yun-fat and Tony Leung give John Woo’s gunplay epic its bruised romantic core. The choreography is astonishing, but the real charge comes from loyalty, compromised identities and bodies moving through physical space at impossible speed. Hong Kong action at the height of its invention.

description: Vidiots and the Eagle Rock Historical Society are celebrating 100 Years of Route 66 with a special screening of John Ford’s classic Steinbeck adaptation The Grapes of Wrath .

title: Rossellini Through His Own Eyes
description: “Neo-realism is above all a moral standpoint from which to look at the world,” Roberto Rossellini proclaimed in 1954, and this conviction led him not just to make lasting contributions to the neo-realist mode, but also equipped him to articulate his artistic ideas into spoken language. In this loving documentary portrait of the father of the cinematic movement, scholar Adriano Aprà uses archival footage and interviews with Rossellini to underscore the filmmaker’s unique eloquence, and the ways his life and work combined into his singular vision.

title: IT’LL BE OK / ALLES WIRD GUT
description: “Bernd Sahling’s documentary follows the young punk Michael as he struggles to reconcile his identity and the reality of living in East Germany. He eventually applies for an exit permit and leaves for the West not long before the Fall of the Berlin Wall. The film explores Michael’s strained relationship with his mother, his path toward financial and intellectual autonomy, and thematizes the physical as well as the mental barriers one has to overcome in the pursuit of freedom.” –DEFA FILM LIBRARY

title: Big Trouble in Little China
description: Kurt Russell plays hard-boiled truck driver Jack Burton, who gets caught in a bizarre conflict within, and underneath, San Francisco's Chinatown. An ancient Chinese prince and Chinatown crime lord has kidnapped a beautiful green-eyed woman, who is the fiancee to Jack's best friend. Jack must help his friend rescue the girl before the evil Lo Pan uses her to break the ancient curse that keeps him a fleshless and immortal spirit.

title: WAKE IN FRIGHT
description:
One night in the Yabba should be enough. But a lost bet strands a schoolteacher in an outback town where hospitality means another drink, another dare and another reason he cannot leave.
Ted Kotcheff turns sunshine and friendliness into instruments of terror. Gary Bond’s careful composure is stripped away by a community whose rituals of masculinity are both welcoming and merciless, with Donald Pleasence an unforgettable guide into the abyss. A sun-blasted nightmare of drinking, belonging and the violence that can hide inside the invitation to be one of the boys.
