title: RIOTS AND LOVE
description: [RANDALE UND LIEBE – ROCKER, POPPER, TEDS UND PUNKS] “Thomas Schmitt’s film offers unique insights into the alternative subculture of 1980s Cologne. Depending on the concert, the Blue-Shell attracted rockers, punks, and Teddy Boys, while the Café d’Or was a popular hangout for the ‘Popper’ crowd. RANDALE UND LIEBE – ROCKER, POPPER, TEDS UND PUNKS is a magnificent document of its time.” –COLOGNE CINEMA NIGHTS

title: I Hate Myself and Want to Die
description: Join us in the microcinema for a refreshing dark comedy that will give you life – J. Davis’ acerbically hilarious I Hate Myself and Want to Die . Jacob is an unrealized artist, freshly dumped, who’s come home to the desert to quietly end his life. The problem is, nothing goes according to plan. His mom needs a ride to the drugstore, his cousin needs a shoulder to cry on, and his best friend just wants to get high. Over a crazy night of parties, fistfights and car chases, Jacob rethinks his life and— maybe—his death.

title: WHITE SNAIL
description: NEW YORK PREMIERE! FILMMAKERS IN PERSON! “Following two unconventional documentaries – SPACE DOGS (2019) and DREAMING DOGS (2024) – focused on the lives of stray canines, filmmaking duo Elsa Kremser and Levin Peter return with the narrative feature WHITE SNAIL, where the two protagonists also exhibit a fondness for various animals. Set in contemporary Belarus, the film tells the story of Masha, a blonde, thin, fair-skinned model pursuing her dream job in China, and Misha, a tattooed, thickset painter working at a morgue. Played with extreme naturalness by non-professionals Marya Imbro and Mikhail Senkov, these two loners strike up an unlikely but profound friendship that will force them to confront their secrets and wounds. The worlds to which Masha and Misha belong are completely at odds. But as these characters form a strange bond, the fashion industry and the funeral business reveal equally unlikely coincidences and areas of overlap that subtly proliferate as the plot advances. By depicting how we and our bodies relate to sight and touch, life and death, reality and imagination, flaws and perfection, Kremser and Peter map two universes on to one another, leaving the viewer to determine where they intersect and whether they diverge.” –Cristina Álvarez López, VIENNALE These screenings are co-presented by Deutsches Haus at NYU and Erste Bank, on the occasion of the co-awarding of the 2025 Viennale Erste Bank Film Award to WHITE SNAIL. Since 2011, each annual edition of the Viennale (Vienna International FilmFestival) has featured the granting of the Viennale Erste Bank Film Award to one or more filmmakers whose films are included within the festival. Designed to showcase the best of Austrian cinema, the Award was founded by Erste Bank, the Viennale’s main sponsor, and is awarded according to the findings of an independent jury. The Award brings a cash prize as well as a residency as a visiting filmmaker organized by Deutsches Haus at NYU. Additional support for these screenings has been provided by the Austrian Cultural Forum New York.

title: Short Cuts : 35mm Roadshow Tour
description: A multi-storied, fish-eyed look at the human condition against the backdrop of contemporary middle-class LA. Twenty two characters intersect, profoundly and fleetingly, through each other’s lives. It runs the emotional gamut from disturbing to humorous. Don't miss a rare opportunity to see Robert Altman's sprawling epic, showing from an original 35mm print as part of our SHORT CUTS 35mm Roadshow Tour. The 35mm Roadshow Tour will begin at the Prince Charles Cinema, before heading to other sites across the UK in a limited run this November. Special thanks to David Levy for helping us make this happen, and to Curzon for giving us and participating sites access to their print.

title: Manhunter : The Final Cut
description: A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast , including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen (The Contender, 2000) as his blind love interest. -- This new 4K Final Cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version. Shot in 1985, MANHUNTER was on a frontier in both its subject matter and film form, initiating an impressive list of subsequent films and series. “40 years ago – though armed with Thomas Harris’ excellent novel, “Red Dragon” – its subject matter, the profiling of serial killers, as well as being shocking and raw, was unknown. When adapting, I wanted to make its storytelling deliver audiences into a certain state of threat and emotional engagement. Integral to that was the visualization and use of music with lyrics sometimes working like a libretto. We have carefully remastered the film to try to evoke that mood and intensity, heightened with audio sourced from the original 5.1 35mm analog masters. This latest iteration is that version of the film with which I’m most satisfied.” said director Michael Mann. Under the guidance of Mann, this 4K scan of the original 35mm negative – with a few shots from an interpositive - was conformed and digitally restored at L’Immagine Ritrovata in Bologna. Both the theatrical version and the UHD HDR & SDR video color gradings were performed by Stefan Sonnenfeld at Company 3 in Los Angeles with the director. Sound restoration was done at Audio Mechanics from an original 35mm magnetic 6-track printmaster to release a new 5.1 mix by Luke Schwartzweller at Fox . Technical coordination and deliveries were managed by L’Immagine Ritrovata . This project was supervised by Becca Mann and STUDIOCANAL team, Jean-Pierre Boiget and Delphine Roussel . For Michael Mann, the process is about renewing the film’s immediacy for contemporary audiences: “If the picture was left the way it was, it would be interesting, but you’d feel some distance …you’d be observing it somewhat. I’m more interested in its original intent impacting you the same way it may have in 1986…that is, to bring you into it again in the original way.” As a film distinguished by its striking visual style, including Colleen Attwood’s costume design, Academy Award- winner Mel Bourne’s art direction, Dante Spinotti’s lighting, Mann worked with his long-time collaborator, Stefan Sonnenfeld (Company 3), to develop a new color grade for ‘The Final Cut’ that engages a contemporary audience while honoring the film’s lasting legacy. “A good example is the use of primaries and secondaries in combinations that don’t occur in nature for an unsettling ambiance or the use of blue for night-time imagery. We’ve changed values subtly sometimes, but significantly, to enhance the impact without changing the dramatic intent of the film,” said Stefan Sonnenfeld. He adds: “Michael… wants you to understand the story and the mood and the environment… and then asks you to interpret that in colour… He also tells you what emotion he’s trying to evoke from the scene.” The new version also introduces an HDR presentation, offering an intensified new experience. “So that nobody’s ever seen the movie like that,” noted Sonnenfeld.

title: Rome, Open City
description: Made for less than $20,000 just after the liberation of Italy by US forces, Rossellini’s first installment in his Neo-Realist Trilogy, which also includes Paisan (1946, screening on November 15) and Germany, Year Zero (1948, screening the same day), is also considered the first product of neo-realism. The devastation of Nazi-occupied Rome serves as an all-too-real backdrop for a story that could have been ripped from the headlines: a resistance leader (Aldo Fabrizi) is pursued through town as he seeks shelter and a safe escape. With “the terror of German occupation [...] still vivid in the minds of everyone,” (Patrizio Rossi, 1988) including Rossellini’s lead actress, the great Anna Magnani, Rome, Open City serves as a prototype for a series of films that characterize the best of Italian cinema.

title: BIJOU
description:
A construction worker pockets an invitation and follows it through an unmarked door. Beyond it lies Bijou: a mysterious theatre where watching becomes participation and the ordinary city opens into a maze of private fantasy.
Wakefield Poole uses colour, music and dreamlike cutting to push adult filmmaking towards the avant-garde. Dialogue falls away, theatrical spaces dissolve and desire becomes a way of seeing. A landmark of independent queer cinema whose restless visual imagination reaches far beyond the boundaries of its genre.
This film contains hardcore unsimulated sex scenes.

title: whisper & SHOUT / flüstern & SCHREIEN
description: “In 1988, the East German state film studio DEFA produced the first – and only – documentary report on the country’s rock and punk scene. whisper & SHOUT sold over a million tickets upon release, largely to young people eager to see their favorite bands on screen and to find out what made it past the censors. Their enthusiasm was natural; director Dieter Schumann’s team had hit the road across the GDR not only to film live performances, but also to interview teenage fans about their place in the subculture, their prospects for the future, and the targets of their rebellion. Shot on 35mm and featuring luminary bands like Feeling B (some of whose members went on to found Rammstein), Silly, Chicorée, and Die Zöllner, whisper & SHOUT is both a generational portrait of music and protest behind the Wall and a unique historical artifact of the East German media’s relationship to its country’s underground.” –GOETHE-INSTITUT

title: Repo Man
description: A down-and-out young punk (Emilio Estevez) gets a job working with a seasoned repo man (Harry Dean Stanton), but what awaits him in his new career is a series of outlandish adventures revolving around aliens, the CIA, and a most wanted ’64 Chevy. Musically adorned with a killer punk soundtrack, this offbeat and absurd slice of 80s East LA is one ride you won’t forget.

title: Whisper of the Heart
description: Discover the brilliance of this heartwarming coming-of-age classic from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of My Neighbour Totoro and the Academy Award®-winning Spirited Away. A chance encounter with a mysterious cat sends Shizuku, a girl with her head in the clouds, on a quest for her true talent. Together with Seiji, a boy determined to follow his dreams, and enchanted by The Baron, an antique cat figurine who guides her to listen to the whispers of her heart, Shizuku embarks on a life-changing adventure that takes her beyond the boundaries of her imagination. Based on a screenplay and storyboards from Hayao Miyazaki, WHISPER OF THE HEART is a precious gem in the Studio Ghibli catalogue, directed by veteran animator Yoshifumi Kondo.

description:
Something enormous is stirring beneath the California surf. As swimmers and sailors vanish, a reporter and a marine expert uncover a threat with eight arms, an appetite for tourists and no respect for the summer season.
John Huston, Shelley Winters and Henry Fonda lend improbable Hollywood grandeur to this gloriously wayward Italian creature feature. Ovidio G. Assonitis answers JAWS with a giant octopus, sunlit coastal menace and Stelvio Cipriani’s irresistible score: aquatic exploitation with a cast far too distinguished to stay safely on shore.
Presented in collaboration with CAM Sugar, with a vinyl market in our basement bar between films from 1.30pm

title: All That Jazz
description: When he is not planning for his upcoming stage musical or working on his Hollywood film, choreographer/director Joe Gideon (Roy Scheider) is popping pills and sleeping with a seemingly endless line of women. The physical and mental stress begins to take a toll on the ragged perfectionist. Soon, he must decide whether or not his non-stop work schedule and hedonistic lifestyle are worth risking his life. The film is a semi-autobiographical tale written and directed by the legendary Bob Fosse.

title: Chicago
description: Wannabe celeb Roxie Hart murders her lover and is sent to jail, only to discover that a tabloid scandal may be her best route to true stardom in this stylish and lively version of the stage musical. Rob Marshall, making his feature directing debut, pays due homage to the distinctive style of Bob Fosse’s original Broadway production while bringing his own energetic approach to the material, which features such classic Kander and Ebb songs as “All That Jazz,” “Cell Block Tango,” and “Mister Cellophane.” The first movie musical to win Best Picture in the 34 years since Oliver! (1968), it received 13 nominations and also won for Costume Design, Film Editing, Sound, Catherine Zeta-Jones’s commanding performance as Roxie’s frenemy Velma Kelly. Production designer John Myhre and set decorator Gordon Sim also won for their Art Direction, featuring just the right blend of fantasy and reality.

title: THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS
description: Juliet Bashore THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS, PART 1 1991, 24 min, DCP. In German with English subtitles. THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS, PART 2 1992, 19 min, DCP. In German with English subtitles. “The Wall has fallen. Berlin has reunified. But there are new zones of transgression to be carved out and explored. Mainzer Straße is a hot spot of squatters and anti-fascist fights. One of the squats on this notorious street, the Tuntenhaus (‘House of Queers’), becomes a specific target of both their neo-Nazi neighbors and the iron fist of the capitalist state. Juliet Bashore’s legendary documentary follows the daily struggle of the queens and queers to create and defend a place for themselves in the chaos and unrest after the fall of communism. The extraordinary union of the anarchist/autonomous and gay scenes meets the onlooking yet involved sympathizers, who also end up in conflict with the squatters as a result of their filming. The film is a unique testimony to the violent and momentous eviction of the people from the streets.” –THE BEACON

title: HER WEDDING NIGHT
description: An American movie star vacationing in France gets mixed up with a songwriter, mistaken identity, and winds up married to someone she doesn’t know.

title: I Hate Myself and Want to Die
description: Join us in the microcinema for a refreshing dark comedy that will give you life – J. Davis’ acerbically hilarious I Hate Myself and Want to Die . Jacob is an unrealized artist, freshly dumped, who’s come home to the desert to quietly end his life. The problem is, nothing goes according to plan. His mom needs a ride to the drugstore, his cousin needs a shoulder to cry on, and his best friend just wants to get high. Over a crazy night of parties, fistfights and car chases, Jacob rethinks his life and— maybe—his death.

title: BERLIN SUPER 80: FILMS FROM THE WEST GERMAN UNDERGROUND
description: This program compiles 18 short films shot on Super-8mm by West German experimental film makers between 1978 and 1984, and featuring music by Malaria, Reflections, Einstürzende Neubauten, Frieder Butzmann, Die Tödliche Doris, and others. “In the beginning of the 1980s, West Berlin was a walled-off island of decadence in the middle of the communist DDR. An urban culture of bars and clubs was thriving in the city that lived at night. The cheap Super 8 film format, already becoming obsolete in the early 80s, was the cinematic equivalent of punk in Berlin. Cameras and projectors were available at flea markets for next to nothing, and, with the lightweight equipment, screenings could be arranged spontaneously in the seediest of venues. In a fevered frenzy the musicians, photographers, painters, and filmmakers of the city’s underground art scene collaborated in cross-disciplinary joint projects. Underground filmmaking became a cycle somewhat resembling a circular argument: filmmakers, who were often also musicians, started shooting performances given by their colleagues, which in turn would more often than not include screenings of works by their friends, and so on. The best of these films were dark, apocalyptic visions, which combined various techniques in radical experiments of the filmic form. Music, performance and happening fused together in a variety of Super 8 club events (in such legendary places as Risiko and S.O. 36), as well as at the first Super 8 film festival, Interfilm 1, in 1982.” –AVANTO Brand & Maschmann E DOPO? title: One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest
description: Adapted from Ken Kesey’s novel, the film centres on Randle McMurphy (Nicholson), a convict who simulates mental illness in the hope that a transfer to psychiatric hospital might ensure his early release. But he hasn’t bargained for the rigid regimen of Nurse Ratched (Louise Fletcher, also superb), who dislikes his disruptive — though he’d say liberating — effect on the ward. Inspired casting (Danny DeVito, Brad Dourif and Christopher Lloyd are among the patients) and Forman’s naturalistic direction lend authenticity to the proceedings, so that the film succeeds both as anti-authoritarian parable and as an affecting reminder of the psychiatric practices of the past.

title: Doc'n'Roll FF: You Fuckers Figure It Out: A Jason Molina Story + Q&A
Fallen Angels
description: An assassin goes through obstacles as he attempts to escape his violent lifestyle despite the opposition of his partner, who is secretly attracted to him.

title: THE RED QUEEN KILLS SEVEN TIMES
description:
A family curse says the Red Queen returns every hundred years to take seven lives. When a crimson-cloaked killer begins stalking the people around a fashion-house heiress, old rivalries and a disputed inheritance make the legend horribly useful.
Barbara Bouchet and Marina Malfatti lead Emilio P. Miraglia’s sumptuous collision of Gothic mystery and couture-world giallo. Bruno Nicolai’s score slips beneath images of castles, cameras and lethal elegance. Every gorgeous surface conceals another motive in a whodunit dressed to kill.
Presented in collaboration with CAM Sugar, with a vinyl market in our basement bar between films from 1.30pm

title: Out of the Past
description: Get ready for some Noir in November with Jacques Tourneur’s double crossing classic! The quiet life of small-town gas station owner Jeff Bailey (Robert Mitchum) is interrupted when a figure from his shady past, small-time crook Joe Stephanos (Paul Valentine), recognizes him. Stephanos’ boss, crooked gambler Whit Sterling (Kirk Douglas), had hired Jeff to track down Kathie Moffat (Jane Greer), a girlfriend who shot Whit and made off with $40,000 of his. Jeff and Kathie fell in love, but she left him to go back to Sterling, who now wants Jeff to settle a few old scores.

title: Primetime
description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history. When a high stakes operation goes fatally wrong, his veneered dream of fame curdles into a nightmare of performative justice.

title: Waikiki Brothers
description: Park Hae-il’s big-screen debut is Yim Soon-rye’s second feature, which received critical praise upon its 2001 release, establishing Yim as one of Korea’s most significant directors. Seong-woo, lead singer and guitarist of Waikiki Brothers—a band formed with his friends back in high school—returns to his hometown with his bandmates in hopes of repairing their fragile relationship. But the band stagnates, and Seong-woo is torn between a dream that’s out of reach and his thin grasp on reality. Park, who portrays the teen version of Seong-woo, generates youthful energy, evoking the purity that Seong-woo and his bandmates once carried and now long for. Yim’s insightful and humane perception of the cruel split between dreams and reality in modern Korea permeates this portrayal of her sympathetic and intricate characters.

title: WHITE SNAIL
description: NEW YORK PREMIERE! FILMMAKERS IN PERSON! “Following two unconventional documentaries – SPACE DOGS (2019) and DREAMING DOGS (2024) – focused on the lives of stray canines, filmmaking duo Elsa Kremser and Levin Peter return with the narrative feature WHITE SNAIL, where the two protagonists also exhibit a fondness for various animals. Set in contemporary Belarus, the film tells the story of Masha, a blonde, thin, fair-skinned model pursuing her dream job in China, and Misha, a tattooed, thickset painter working at a morgue. Played with extreme naturalness by non-professionals Marya Imbro and Mikhail Senkov, these two loners strike up an unlikely but profound friendship that will force them to confront their secrets and wounds. The worlds to which Masha and Misha belong are completely at odds. But as these characters form a strange bond, the fashion industry and the funeral business reveal equally unlikely coincidences and areas of overlap that subtly proliferate as the plot advances. By depicting how we and our bodies relate to sight and touch, life and death, reality and imagination, flaws and perfection, Kremser and Peter map two universes on to one another, leaving the viewer to determine where they intersect and whether they diverge.” –Cristina Álvarez López, VIENNALE These screenings are co-presented by Deutsches Haus at NYU and Erste Bank, on the occasion of the co-awarding of the 2025 Viennale Erste Bank Film Award to WHITE SNAIL. Since 2011, each annual edition of the Viennale (Vienna International FilmFestival) has featured the granting of the Viennale Erste Bank Film Award to one or more filmmakers whose films are included within the festival. Designed to showcase the best of Austrian cinema, the Award was founded by Erste Bank, the Viennale’s main sponsor, and is awarded according to the findings of an independent jury. The Award brings a cash prize as well as a residency as a visiting filmmaker organized by Deutsches Haus at NYU. Additional support for these screenings has been provided by the Austrian Cultural Forum New York.

title: NINA HAGEN = PUNK + GLORY
description: Up until his untimely death earlier this year, filmmaker Peter Sempel had a long and close association with Anthology Film Archives and Jonas Mekas (about whom he made four separate feature-length film portraits over the years). In addition to his collaborations with Jonas, Sempel made numerous other experimental films and documentaries about various artists and musicians. Among his best-known works is this film about the legendary singer, songwriter, and actress Nina Hagen. Far from a conventional artist doc, NINA HAGEN = PUNK + GLORY favors spontaneous, fragmentary, and often home-movie-like glimpses of her daily life, performances, and interactions with family, friends, and colleagues (including Lemmy, George Clinton, Blixa Bargeld, Udo Kier, Dee Dee Ramone, Jonas Mekas, and others). Sempel’s goal is less to narrate Hagen’s biography than to capture her unique energy and charisma, and to shed light on her many sides, on- and off-stage.

title: Dead Souls + Alex Cox Q&A
description: On Sunday 8th November, we will be joined by Director Alex Cox for a Live Post-Film Q&A For his directorial swan song, Alex Cox (Repo Man, Straight to Hell) stars in this frontier fable of American Greed, playing the mysterious drifter Strindler as he scours the West for the names of dead Mexican labourers. In this loose adaptation of Nikolai Gogol's 1842 novel Dead Souls, Strindler - or is it Swindler? - raises eyebrows when he offers to pay a pretty penny to add to his list of names. Wandering affably from saloon to ranch, Strindler exercises the old adage that money talks - but sometimes too loudly. Between the town drunk, hot-headed cowherds and local outlaws, Strindler soon finds himself tangled up in his own tall tales. Pistol duels and crooked officials abound, and Spaghetti Western legend Gianni Garko (If You Meet Sartana Pray For Your Death) claims a co-writer credit. But Cox's idiosyncrasy stands out as the film veers tonally through the picaresque, dark satire and other unexpected twists. Dead Souls is a meditative Western that takes place at the borderlands of the American nightmare: where fortunes rest on a dirty deal and legacies are built on blood and gold.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: HITCH HIKE
description:
Their marriage is already a war zone. Picking up a stranger gives it an armed third party. A bitter couple’s journey across the American West becomes a savage contest over stolen money, control and who will get out alive.
Franco Nero, Corinne Cléry and David Hess form a combustible triangle in Pasquale Festa Campanile’s sun-baked road thriller. Ennio Morricone’s score gives the landscape a seductive pulse while the cramped caravan becomes increasingly poisonous. An exploitation film whose most uncomfortable idea is that the stranger may not be the only monster aboard.
Presented in collaboration with CAM Sugar, with a vinyl market in our basement bar between films from 1.30pm

title: Pulp Fiction
description: Vincent Vega (John Travolta) and Jules Winnfield (Samuel L. Jackson) are hitmen with a penchant for philosophical discussions. In this ultra-hip, multi-strand crime movie, their storyline is interwoven with those of their boss, gangster Marsellus Wallace (Ving Rhames) ; his actress wife, Mia (Uma Thurman) ; struggling boxer Butch Coolidge (Bruce Willis) ; master fixer Winston Wolfe (Harvey Keitel) and a nervous pair of armed robbers, "Pumpkin" (Tim Roth) and "Honey Bunny" (Amanda Plummer).

title: Classic Matinee: THE LUNCHBOX
description: For our November Classic Matinee, taking place the day after Diwali, we celebrate Indian cinema with Ritesh Batra’s beautifully observed and bittersweet THE LUNCHBOX . Lonely housewife Ila prepares a special lunch for her neglectful husband, only for Mumbai’s famously efficient lunchbox delivery sys...

title: Oldboy [Oldeuboi]
description: Dae-Su is an obnoxious drunk bailed from the police station yet again by a friend. However, he's abducted from the street and wakes up in a cell, where he remains for the next 15 years, drugged unconscious when human contact is unavoidable, otherwise with only the television as company. And then, suddenly released, he is invited to track down his jailor with a denouement that is simply stunning.

title: Some Like It Hot
description: Marilyn Monroe’s work in director Billy Wilder’s comedic classic is often cited as her best. The film was controversial for its racy humor and story about two musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) who disguise themselves as women to evade the Mafia. But of equal scandal were the Oscar-winning costumes made by Orry-Kelly for Monroe’s Sugar Kane Kowalczyk. Both dresses are on display in the exhibit Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon , on view through February 28, 2027. Some Like It Hot was made during a year of dramatic highs and lows for Monroe, with this film standing as a high point.
director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Billy Wilder

title: Idiocracy
description: **ON SALE 23rd OCT** In 2005, average in every way private Joe Bowers (Luke Wilson) is selected to take part in a secret military experiment to put him in hibernation for a year along with a woman named Rita (Maya Rudolph). The slumbering duo is forgotten when the base they are stored on is closed down and are left in stasis until 2505. When they finally wake up, they discover the average intelligence of humans has decreased so much that Joe is now the smartest man in the world.

title: CRIMES OF PASSION (16MM)
description:
Fashion designer by day, China Blue by night: Joanna Crane has built two lives to keep desire at a manageable distance. A private investigator and a deranged preacher are about to tear down the partition.
Kathleen Turner and Anthony Perkins go gloriously for broke in Ken Russell’s neon psychosexual fever dream. Pop-art colour, outrageous religious imagery and Rick Wakeman’s electronic score turn an erotic thriller into a furious comedy of repression and hypocrisy. Lurid, funny and unexpectedly vulnerable, it makes respectable behaviour look like the strangest fetish of all.
Presented on 16mm with a reel intermission.

title: BULKY TRASH + THE FREE ORCHESTRA
description: Helke Misselwitz BULKY TRASH / SPERRMÜLL 1990, 72 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. Filmed in the early summer of 1989, this documentary portrays a band of four young musicians who call themselves “Sperrmüll” (“Bulky Trash”), thanks to their proclivity for producing music by drumming on other people’s discarded items. Misselwitz concentrates especially on Enrico, who decides to stay behind when his mother Erika marries in the West, and who insists on maintaining his cultural identity even after the fall of the Wall. The members of “Sperrmüll” wish to remain citizens of their own state, and their attitude towards the looming reunification is one of skepticism. Originally intended as a call for social change, Misselwitz’s film documents the events of the Wende from the perspective of young East Berliners. Preceded by: Petra Tschörtner THE FREE ORCHESTRA / DAS FREIE ORCHESTER 1988, 17 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. “Day in, day out, Barbara sells screws at a store in the East Berlin Market Hall. She is frustrated about having to tell her customers most of the time: ‘Ham wa nich!’ (‘We don’t have that!’) In the evening, she is the loud and wild singer of the legendary East Berlin avantgarde and punk band Das Freie Orchester. Playing music with her friends helps her escape the monotony of her job, express her dissatisfaction with everyday life in East Germany in the 1980s, and dream of a different life.” –DEFA FILM LIBRARY Total running time: ca. 95 min.

title: Cinematic Void Presents PHASE IV
description: Ecological suspense tale about a strange biological imbalance creating super intelligent ants which attack a scientific installation in the Arizona desert.

title: Short Cuts : 35mm Roadshow Tour
description: A multi-storied, fish-eyed look at the human condition against the backdrop of contemporary middle-class LA. Twenty two characters intersect, profoundly and fleetingly, through each other’s lives. It runs the emotional gamut from disturbing to humorous. Don't miss a rare opportunity to see Robert Altman's sprawling epic, showing from an original 35mm print as part of our SHORT CUTS 35mm Roadshow Tour. The 35mm Roadshow Tour will begin at the Prince Charles Cinema, before heading to other sites across the UK in a limited run this November. Special thanks to David Levy for helping us make this happen, and to Curzon for giving us and participating sites access to their print.

title: La Bola Negra (15) (AD)
description: A genre-defying queer epic spanning generations, inspired by the legacy of beloved Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca.

title: Boyhood
description: The joys and pitfalls of growing up are seen through the eyes of a child named Mason (Ellar Coltrane), his parents (Patricia Arquette, Ethan Hawke) and his sister (Lorelei Linklater). Vignettes, filmed with the same cast over the course of 12 years, capture family meals, road trips, birthday parties, graduations and other important milestones. Songs from Coldplay, Arcade Fire and other artists capture the time period.

title: Moss
description: Hae-guk (Park Hae-il) receives word that his estranged father has passed away, bringing him to an unusual village for the funeral. Sensing his presence is unwelcome, Hae-guk grows suspicious and begins to sense a deeper truth behind his father's death . Adapted from a Korean webtoon, Moss submerges audiences in a dark and thrilling mystery, blending suspense and horror to create a world of uncertainty. –Note written by Hannah Farkas.

title: IT’LL BE OK / ALLES WIRD GUT
description: “Bernd Sahling’s documentary follows the young punk Michael as he struggles to reconcile his identity and the reality of living in East Germany. He eventually applies for an exit permit and leaves for the West not long before the Fall of the Berlin Wall. The film explores Michael’s strained relationship with his mother, his path toward financial and intellectual autonomy, and thematizes the physical as well as the mental barriers one has to overcome in the pursuit of freedom.” –DEFA FILM LIBRARY

title: BLUE MONDAY - MYSTERY XXX CINEMA
description:
Blue Monday presents undisclosed selections from the deepest recesses of horny cult cinema - encapsulating everything from erotic thrillers, carnal noir, golden age porno and transgressive sleaze from both the underground and the mainstream.
This screening will feature adult-themed content, including sexually explicit and risqué material. Please consider yourself forewarned that these films may (and probably will) contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.
Adults only.

title: The Holy Mountain
description: In a corrupt, greed-fueled world, a powerful alchemist leads a messianic character and seven materialistic figures to the Holy Mountain, where they hope to achieve enlightenment.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: Sunset Boulevard
description: An aging silent film queen refuses to accept that her stardom has ended. She hires a young screenwriter to help set up her movie comeback. The screenwriter believes he can manipulate her, but he soon finds out he is wrong. The screenwriters ambivalence about their relationship and her unwillingness to let go leads to a situation of violence, madness, and death.

title: In the Realm of the Senses
description: Still censored in its own country, In the Realm of the Senses (Ai no corrida), by Japanese director Nagisa Oshima, remains one of the most controversial films of all time. A graphic portrayal of insatiable sexual desire, Oshima’s film, set in 1936 and based on a true incident, depicts a man and a woman (Tatsuya Fuji and Eiko Matsuda) consumed by a transcendent, destructive love while living in an era of ever-escalating imperialism and governmental control. Less a work of pornography than of politics, In the Realm of the Senses is a brave, taboo-breaking milestone. Content Warning: This film contains scenes of graphic sex and violence. Further information about content and age-appropriateness for specific films can be found on Common Sense Media , IMDb and DoesTheDogDie.com , as well as through general internet searches.

title: whisper & SHOUT / flüstern & SCHREIEN
description: “In 1988, the East German state film studio DEFA produced the first – and only – documentary report on the country’s rock and punk scene. whisper & SHOUT sold over a million tickets upon release, largely to young people eager to see their favorite bands on screen and to find out what made it past the censors. Their enthusiasm was natural; director Dieter Schumann’s team had hit the road across the GDR not only to film live performances, but also to interview teenage fans about their place in the subculture, their prospects for the future, and the targets of their rebellion. Shot on 35mm and featuring luminary bands like Feeling B (some of whose members went on to found Rammstein), Silly, Chicorée, and Die Zöllner, whisper & SHOUT is both a generational portrait of music and protest behind the Wall and a unique historical artifact of the East German media’s relationship to its country’s underground.” –GOETHE-INSTITUT

title: HAMLET IN THE RENTED WORLD (A FRAGMENT) + COBRA WOMAN
description: Jerry Tartaglia HAMLET IN THE RENTED WORLD (A FRAGMENT) 1970-73, 27 min, 16mm-to-DCP A portrait of Jack Smith fashioned from the debris of an unfinished project: “You might say that [this 27-minute assemblage put together by Jerry Tartaglia on behalf of the Gladstone Gallery from materials discovered in the Jack Smith Archives dating from the early 1970s] is BLONDE COBRA’s sort of sequel… In trying to bring into existence the derangement of a classic text – a project that Smith himself had abandoned – HAMLET IN THE RENTED WORLD is not a preservation but the reconstruction of a deconstruction.” –J. Hoberman, “Jack Smith’s Hamlet in the Rented World,” ACROSS THE MOVI-VERSE Robert Siodmak COBRA WOMAN 1944, 72 min, 35mm. With Maria Montez. “[Four days before Richard Nixon was reelected president, I saw the complete TRIUMPH OF THE WILL sans subtitles at the old Anthology Film Archives on Wooster Street and was nauseated.] The next night, either by coincidence or design, I caught a salutary, anti-fascist double bill at the New Yorker theater: DUCK SOUP, which I knew by heart, and COBRA WOMAN, which I knew only by reputation as Jack Smith’s favorite film, later noting that ‘The Cobra Dance’ should be spliced into or shown with TRIUMPH OF THE WILL.” –J. Hoberman, “Triumph of the Will and the Artification of Fascism,” ACROSS THE MOVI-VERSE Total running time: ca. 105 min.

title: The Departed
description: To take down South Boston's Irish Mafia, the police send in one of their own to infiltrate the underworld, not realizing the syndicate has done likewise. While an undercover cop curries favor with the mob kingpin, a career criminal rises through the police ranks. But both sides soon discover there's a mole among them.

title: British Horror Studio Season: Spoiling You
description: Introducing a season from the British Horror Studio. An independent British film studio Focusing on Gothic drama and arthouse filmmaking with a distinctive British horror character. Spoiling You is a seductive and deeply unsettling ASMR psychological horror from award-winning filmmaker Megan Tremethick. What begins as a world of soft voices, intimate rituals, and online comfort soon curdles into something far more dangerous, as obsession, identity, and performance collapse into a nightmare of control. Starring Megan Tremethick, Stephen Kerr, and Laurence R. Harvey, Spoiling You blends J-horror unease, internet-age paranoia, and sensual psychological dread into one of The B-Team’s boldest and most disturbing features. Tremethick’s award-winning directorial debut turns the familiar language of online intimacy into a weapon, creating a film that is strange, stylish, uncomfortable, and impossible to shake. https://www.britishhorrorstudio.com/

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: BORED TEENAGERS
description: [BRENNENDE LANGEWEILE] “In the late 1970s, Wolfgang Büld first made a name for himself with his documentary PUNK IN LONDON. The follow-up to this authentic document of youth culture was the ZDF production BORED TEENAGERS, part of the “Das kleine Fernsehspiel” series; it was filmed in 1979 in the wake of the RAF panic – wanted posters are visible in the background several times throughout the film. The movie blends concert footage of the English punk band The Adverts with a loose narrative thread about a young punk named Peter and his hairdresser girlfriend, Karin, as they follow the band – led by TV Smith and Gaye Advert – on their tour through Germany. It is an entertaining yet quirky journey through a late-70s musical subculture.” –OX-FANZINE

title: Ms. 45
description: Eerie and unforgettable, MS. 45 is an essential snapshot of New York City in the early 1980s from Abel Ferrara (DRILLER KILLER, THE ADDICTION)—one of the greatest and most unique living filmmakers on the planet. Thana (Zoë Tamerlis) is a garment worker who’s had the ultimate bad day, as she’s assaulted twice in visceral fashion. Shocked to her core, Thana's nights become consumed by vengeful prowls through the city, which result in men winding up on the wrong end of a bullet. Knocking the DEATH WISH rip-off subgenre into a new stratosphere, MS. 45 showcases a haunting performance from Tamerlis and Ferrara's knack for transforming limited resources into genre revolutions. Content Warning: Contains scenes of sexual assault that some viewers may find distressing. Further information about content and age-appropriateness for specific films can be found on Common Sense Media , IMDb and DoesTheDogDie.com , as well as through general internet searches.

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape. * The first 35 customers to have tickets scanned in each of these performances will recieve an exclusive limited edition " I SURVIVED THE TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE" badge. A replica of one's we gave out back in 1976 when we were the first cinema to debut this iconic film.

title: Short Cuts : 35mm Roadshow Tour
description: A multi-storied, fish-eyed look at the human condition against the backdrop of contemporary middle-class LA. Twenty two characters intersect, profoundly and fleetingly, through each other’s lives. It runs the emotional gamut from disturbing to humorous. Don't miss a rare opportunity to see Robert Altman's sprawling epic, showing from an original 35mm print as part of our SHORT CUTS 35mm Roadshow Tour. The 35mm Roadshow Tour will begin at the Prince Charles Cinema, before heading to other sites across the UK in a limited run this November. Special thanks to David Levy for helping us make this happen, and to Curzon for giving us and participating sites access to their print.

title: Some Like It Hot
description: Marilyn Monroe’s work in director Billy Wilder’s comedic classic is often cited as her best. The film was controversial for its racy humor and story about two musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) who disguise themselves as women to evade the Mafia. But of equal scandal were the Oscar-winning costumes made by Orry-Kelly for Monroe’s Sugar Kane Kowalczyk. Both dresses are on display in the exhibit Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon , on view through February 28, 2027. Some Like It Hot was made during a year of dramatic highs and lows for Monroe, with this film standing as a high point.
director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Billy Wilder

title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . Lotte Reiniger’s The Adventures of Prince Achmed is an enchanting amalgamation of stories from the Arabian Nights animated in cut paper silhouettes, an exquisite artefact of Weimar Cinema and a genre-defying experiment in melding international folk art traditions with the technical possibilities of a new medium. Taken from The Arabian Nights, a wicked sorcerer and the beautiful prince Achmed battle one another in a series of wondrous adventures. Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work.

The Torrance family are heading to The Overlook Hotel to spend the winter - but they're got a big surprise coming to them. One of the greatest horror movies of all time The Shining is a masterpiece by one o...

title: In the Company of Men + The Deep North (15)
description: Two films that explore psychodrama as a way of analysing and addressing racial inequality through group workshops, from 1969 and 1988.

title: THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS
description: Juliet Bashore THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS, PART 1 1991, 24 min, DCP. In German with English subtitles. THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS, PART 2 1992, 19 min, DCP. In German with English subtitles. “The Wall has fallen. Berlin has reunified. But there are new zones of transgression to be carved out and explored. Mainzer Straße is a hot spot of squatters and anti-fascist fights. One of the squats on this notorious street, the Tuntenhaus (‘House of Queers’), becomes a specific target of both their neo-Nazi neighbors and the iron fist of the capitalist state. Juliet Bashore’s legendary documentary follows the daily struggle of the queens and queers to create and defend a place for themselves in the chaos and unrest after the fall of communism. The extraordinary union of the anarchist/autonomous and gay scenes meets the onlooking yet involved sympathizers, who also end up in conflict with the squatters as a result of their filming. The film is a unique testimony to the violent and momentous eviction of the people from the streets.” –THE BEACON

title: THE CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS + SINS OF THE FLESHAPOIDS
description: Wesley Barry THE CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS 1962, 84 min, 16mm “The Now Future arrived in late 1964, when David Bourdon began his lengthy Village Voice review of Andy Warhol’s ‘Flower Paintings’ with a lengthy account of Wesley Barry’s CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS, a sci-fi cheapster as color-coded as RED DESERT and more impoverished than ALPHAVILLE… ‘The denouement comes when the heroine and the hero (a militant anti-humanoid who goes around throwing bombs at uppity “clickers”) discover themselves to be machines. This is the happy ending of what Andy Warhol calls the best movie he has ever seen.’” –J. Hoberman, “The New Futurism and the Then Zeitgeist,” ACROSS THE MOVI-VERSE Mike Kuchar SINS OF THE FLESHAPOIDS 1965, 48 min, 16mm. With Bob Cowan, George Kuchar, Donna Kerness, Gina Zuckerman, Maren Thomas, and Julius Middleman. “In the winter of 1964-65, even before THE CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS was listed, along with feathered boas and Warhol’s SLEEP, in a random list of things The New York Times Magazine deemed as ‘generally agreed’ examples of ‘Pure Camp,’ Mike Kuchar – a 22-year-old photo retoucher living in the Bronx – conceived his own 16mm version of Warhol’s favorite movie…the junkyard analog to the cycle of European films that includes RED DESERT, ALPHAVILLE, and THE TENTH VICTIM.” –J. Hoberman, “The New Futurism and the Then Zeitgeist,” ACROSS THE MOVI-VERSE Total running time: ca. 135 min.

title: Grace of My Heart
description: Vidiots is thrilled to welcome cinema legends Alison Anders and Illeana Douglas for a special 30th Anniversary Screening of Grace of my Heart !

title: EINSTURZENDE NEUBAUTEN: LIEBESLIEDER
description: An essential text for anyone with a love for the avant-garde. The explosive soundscapes of industrial music titans Einstürzende Neubauten first shook Berlin – then the whole world – to its core in the 1980s. In LIEBESLIEDER, co-directors Klaus Maeck and Johanna Schenkel wield a fractured feast of killer Neubauten performances from Euro television: ones that highlight the group’s cinematic presence, wild handmade instruments, and totally unique style. For those who are at all curious about industrial or noise music in general, this sweaty documentary is unmissable. For Neubauten fans, this humanizing portrait of their first decade provides a fresh take on the band.

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: War for the Planet of the Apes
description: The third film in the contemporary version of the Planet of the Apes series finds the ape leader Caesar (another remarkable motion capture performance by Andy Serkis) seeking a safe haven for the survivors of a human-led massacre, only to wind up in a labor camp run by a vicious military officer (Woody Harrelson). The film was nominated for the visual effects by Joe Letteri, Daniel Barrett, Dan Lemmon and Joel Whist, who depict the film’s ape characters and wintry, post-apocalyptic setting with astonishing realism.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: Benedetta
description: With this orgiastic immersion in the mystic reveries of a real-life historical figure, the king of the erotic thriller Paul Verhoeven gives the nunsploitation flick a high-art makeover. Elegant, perverse, and teasingly scandalous, Benedetta critiques religious hypocrisy with an impish grin.

title: Kingdom of Heaven: Director's Cut
description: Ridley Scott's extended cut of an epic adventure about a common man who finds himself thrust into a decades-long war. Orlando Bloom plays a humble blacksmith who discovers that he is the son of a knght, and travels to the Holy Land to fight in the crusades. A stranger in a strange land, he serves a doomed King, falls in love with an exotic and forbidden Queen, and rises to knighthood. Ultimately, he must protect the people of Jerusalem from overwhelming forces, while striving to keep a fragile peace.

title: The Love Witch
description: “She Loved Men... To Death.” Addicted to love, Elaine – the love witch – casts love and sex spells to seek her perfect man, finding herself with more dead bodies than she does a long-term partner… A visually-striking, humorous and thought-provoking film by the continuously playful Anna Biller, The Love Witch has caused immense debate by audiences through its feminist themes. Visually drenched in 1970s fashion and cinematography, the film´s style feels as magical as the love witch herself. The Love Witch is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Imamura: History of Postwar Japan as Told by a Bar Hostess
Short Films by William Greaves 1959-1974 (15)
description: From Cinema Verité docs and observational filmmaking, to public information films exploring Black history, this selection from the renowned filmmaker shows the versatility in his works and styles.

title: NIGHTMARES COME AT NIGHT
description:
A dancer wakes from dreams of murder convinced that she may have committed the crimes herself. Inside a remote villa, reassurance only makes things stranger: every lover, doctor and memory seems to have another purpose.
Diana Lorys gives Jesús Franco’s elusive thriller a fragile centre as the story drifts between gaslighting, desire and nightmare. Mirrors, bedrooms and unstable recollections take the place of firm ground. Its pleasure lies in that disorientation: an intimate psychological mystery that keeps changing shape just when you think you have found a way through.
Presented by Cosmik Debris.

title: Never Watching Movies: SMOKE SIGNALS
description: NEVER WATCHING MOVIES presents Smoke Signals (1998), the first feature film written, directed and produced by an all Native American filmmaking crew (going on to win the audience award and filmmaker trophy at Sundance 1998). The film follows childhood friends Victor  and Thomas as they travel off th...

title: POSTCOLONIAL MOTION: TAXIS AND TRAVELOGUES
description: While not as long-standing as the romance with trains, cinema has a love affair with taxis. A cab ride is often more than just a means of getting from one place to another. The taxi is a cinematic apparatus in motion, a confessional, an urban microcosm, a transition, a temporary intimacy, an archive of daily life, a nightmare of forced conversation, an eavesdropper’s dream. Yet beneath such metaphors are material threats: the gig economy, prior and enduring precarities and exploitation of labor, movements of migration conditioned by colonization. POSTCOLONIAL MOTION: TAXIS AND TRAVELOGUES draws together three films combining oral testimonies and the kinetics of transport. Frank Sweeney, Karimah Ashadu, and Timoteus Anggawan Kusno each consider the movements of people, goods and images, tracing how workers warp the barriers of historical categories and economic constraints as they cross borders. Guest-programmed by Yasmina Price, who wrote the introduction and individual film descriptions. Frank Sweeney GO YE AFAR 2026, 24 min, DCP Irish research-based artist Frank Sweeney’s latest work, GO YE AFAR (2026), stages a historical examination of economy, religion, national identity, and state power through the nocturnal taxi journey of a Nigerian driver in Dublin and Calabar. Making a link between the IMF’s role in imposing a debt structure on Ireland in the 2010s and the economic dependency still inflicted on the African continent, Sweeney makes a taxi journey an illuminating lens onto the dubious legacies of Catholic missionaries and European philanthropy, global privatization and the erosion of the commons. Karimah Ashadu BROWN GOODS 2020, 12 min, DCP BROWN GOODS (2020), by British-born Nigerian artist and director Karimah Ashadu, both shares and reconfigures a similar terrain. The film scans the intermingled economies and geographies of Africa and Europe, conjuring Nigeria from its viewpoint in Germany. The setting is specifically Hamburg, a hub of international trade and multinational corporations. Ashadu’s agile camerawork delves through docks, weaving amongst ship containers and stacks of tires as Emeka – the self-sufficient central figure, excluded from formal work due to his humanitarian status – voices a sharp analysis of manufacturing and industrial monopolies, the politics of resources and global capital. Timoteus Anggawan Kusno OBSCURA 2026, 14 min, DCP Indonesian filmmaker and visual artist Timoteus Anggawan Kusno’s OBSCURA (2026) echoes the unsettling, spectral dreaminess and mediatized archival memory of GO YE AFAR. Operating between Indonesia and the Netherlands, the film critically reworks the form of the ethnographic travelogue and colonial imagery through a story of theft (another kind of informal job). Gallery workers liberate a painting and carry it out in a truck, performing how images physically travel, are taken apart, literally unframed and reframed. Total running time: ca. 55 min. The screening will be followed by a conversation with filmmaker and artist Frank Sweeney!

title: NARROW ROOMS: DRUNKEN NOODLES
description: Lucio Castro DRUNKEN NOODLES 2025, 83 min, DCP. In English and Spanish with English subtitles. When Adnan (Laith Khalifeh) arrives in New York to work at a Lower East Side gallery for the summer, he’s newly single and ready to mingle. He cruises strangers in the park at night and begins a flirtation with a delivery driver. At work, he’s helping to exhibit the recently discovered work of Sal Salandra, a real-world gay artist and elder who crafts tableaus of gay orgies and sex club scenes in vibrant needlepoint. These artworks – and Sal himself, played by Ezriel Kornel – become the connective thread for a time-jumping narrative that unfolds in four parts. Made for little money, with a small crew and total creative control, the latest by Lucio Castro (END OF THE CENTURY) is a delightful, sexually-charged short-story collection with whimsical elements of dreamy magical realism. Released during the full flower of NYC PRIDE season, DRUNKEN NOODLES is well worth watching – or rewatching – before making your Best-of-2026 lists. We’ll be joined by director Lucio Castro and cast members for a Q&A following the screening!

title: NFTS Collective Visions of Pleasure: The Cruel Woman
FEMALE VAMPIRE
description:
Countess Irina Karlstein moves through an island landscape with a hunger she cannot escape. Those drawn to her become victims; the poet who recognises her loneliness offers the possibility of something more dangerous than feeding: intimacy.
Lina Romay gives Jesús Franco’s vampire reverie its strange mixture of command and vulnerability. Drifting camera movements, misty locations and Daniel White’s score suspend the story between erotic fantasy and a melancholy dream. A film less interested in the mechanics of vampirism than in the terrible solitude of wanting what you cannot keep.
Presented by Cosmik Debris.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: Have A Gd Trip presents Welcome To Hell & Bag of Suck Double Feature
description: For one night only, Have A Gd Trip brings Skateboarding Film Club back to Prince Charles Cinema for an essential double bill celebrating two definitive eras of skate culture. Kicking off the night is the 20th anniversary of Enjoi’s Bag of Suck (2006)—a Transworld Video of the Year winner that balanced jaw-dropping technical progression (anchored by Jerry Hsu’s legendary parts) with the irreverent, fun-first humour that made Enjoi an instant classic. Followed by the 30th anniversary of Toy Machine’s Welcome to Hell (1996)—a relentless masterpiece that set the standard for high-impact handrail skating, immortalised Jamie Thomas’s raw style, and helped launch legends like Elissa Steamer. Welcome to Hell 1996 | 45mins | USA | (18) | Skateboarding Video Directed by Jamie Thomas, Video introduction by Ed Templeton Starring Jamie Thomas, Ed Templeton, Elissa Steamer, Chad Muska, Brian Anderson, Donny Barley Bag of Suck 2006 | 50mins | USA | (18) | Skateboarding Video Directed by Matt Eversole and Kyle Camarillo, Video introduction by Louie Barletta Starring Jerry Hsu, Louie Barletta, Marc Johnson, Caswell Berry, Stevie Williams, Cairo Foster "Pandas, heavy handrails, and pure raw energy." Two iconic videos, three decades of skate history, together for one night only. Rarely seen on the big screen—don't miss out.

title: Network - 50th Anniversary
description: When veteran anchorman Howard Beale is forced to retire his 25-year post because of his age, he announces to viewers that he will kill himself during his farewell broadcast. Network executives rethink their decision when his fanatical tirade results in a spike in ratings.

title: Master and Commander : The Far Side of the World
description: During the Napoleonic Wars, a brash British captain pushes his ship and crew to their limits in pursuit of a formidable French war vessel around South America.

title: Bitter Christmas

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: Some Like It Hot
description: Marilyn Monroe’s work in director Billy Wilder’s comedic classic is often cited as her best. The film was controversial for its racy humor and story about two musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) who disguise themselves as women to evade the Mafia. But of equal scandal were the Oscar-winning costumes made by Orry-Kelly for Monroe’s Sugar Kane Kowalczyk. Both dresses are on display in the exhibit Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon , on view through February 28, 2027. Some Like It Hot was made during a year of dramatic highs and lows for Monroe, with this film standing as a high point.
director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Billy Wilder

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Porco Rosso (Japanese with English Subtitles)
description: From the legendary Studio Ghibli , creators of Spirited Away , and Academy Award-winning director Hayao Miyazaki , comes a dazzling aerial adventure set in and above the scenic port towns of the Adriatic Sea. “Porco Rosso” is a world-weary flying ace-turned-bounty-hunter, whose face has been transformed into that of a pig by a mysterious spell. When he infuriates a band of sky pirates with his heroics, the pirates hire Curtis, a hotshot American rival, to get rid of him. But with the help of the teenage girl Fio, an aspiring airplane designer, and a sultry lounge singer named Gina, Porco takes to the skies for what may be his final high-flying showdown.

title: FOR Y'UR HEIGHT ONLY
description:
Agent 00 has a kidnapped scientist to rescue, an evil mastermind to stop and a gadget for almost every occasion. The odds are absurd. Weng Weng treats them as an invitation.
Eddie Nicart’s Filipino spy adventure gives its star a full arsenal of rooftop escapes, martial-arts encounters and Bond-style ingenuity. What makes it irresistible is the commitment: the film plays its impossible mission with an infectious mixture of swagger and invention. A scrappy international cult favourite powered by a performer who makes every entrance his own.

title: Jason and the Argonauts
description: Jason, a fearless sailor and explorer, returns to his home land of Thessaly after a long voyage to claim his rightful throne. He learns, however, that he must first find the magical Golden Fleece. To do so, he must embark on an epic quest fraught with fantastic monsters and terrible perils.

title: Bitter Christmas

title: The Time Masters
description: Directed by visionary science-fiction animator René Laloux (Fantastic Planet) and designed by the legendary Jean Giraud (a.k.a. Mœbius) The Time Masters is a visually fantastic foray into existentialist space adventure. After his parents are killed on the dangerous planet Perdide, young Piel (voiced by Frédéric Legros) survives by maintaining radio contact with Jaffar (Jean Valmont), a pilot transporting the exiled Prince Matton (Yves-Marie Maurin) and Princess Belle (Monique Thierry) from their former kingdom. Jaffar seeks the help of Silbad (Michel Elias), a cheerful old-timer who knows how to circumvent Perdide’s hazards, including brain-devouring insects and watery graves. Along the way, Jaffar and company encounter a pair of impish homunculi stowaways, identity-less angels controlled by an amorphous hive mind, and the Masters of Time, mysterious beings who can bend reality and perhaps reveal to the heroes their secret origins and destinies. Restored in 4K in 2023 at the initiative of CITE FILMS in collaboration with the Fondazione Cineteca di Bologna and with the support of the CNC

title: BARBARA
description: With Jeanne Balibar, Mathieu Amalric, Vincent Peirani, Aurore Clement, and Grégoire Colin. Amalric’s seventh feature-length film as a director is both a heartfelt tribute to the legendary chanteuse Barbara (1930-97), and a vehicle for another peerlessly talented French luminary, the actress and singer Jeanne Balibar. Amalric’s films are remarkable for their intuitive freedom, and their emphasis on emotional textures and states of feeling rather than on straightforward narrative construction or easily grasped meanings. BARBARA is a case in point: eschewing anything like a coherent, birth-to-death account of the events of her life, the film instead orchestrates fragments of the singer’s life and performances into a free and quasi-abstract meditation on Barbara’s identity and cultural presence. And by casting Balibar not as Barbara per se but more self-referentially as an actress making a film-within-the-film about the singer, his film becomes an even broader investigation into the concept of biographical filmmaking, representation, and identity. An experimental biopic in the tradition of Stanley Kwan’s CENTER STAGE, Peter Watkins’s EDVARD MUNCH, and Paul Leduc’s FRIDA, it features a typically riveting, charismatic performance from Balibar.

title: An Unfinished Film
description: ★★★★★ “An utterly unique and very important movie about Covid, the crisis that affected all of us.” – The Guardian Director Xiaorui convinces his cast and crew to resume the shooting of a film halted ten years earlier. In January 2020, with the shoot almost complete, rumours regarding an illness begin to circulate. A hairdresser from Wuhan is sent home, while the crew follows the news on their phones. The director has to decide whether to halt the filming once again. Some of the crew and actors manage to leave before the hotel is locked down by security guards and everyone left on set is confined to their hotel rooms. As all communication is reduced to phone screens, Wuhan is locked down. The crew continues to communicate via video calls, whilst the quarantined main actor Jiang Cheng struggles to support his wife who is now locked-down with their month-old baby in Beijing.

title: Blood Simple
description: Sexy, smart, and smoldering, this shocking neo-noir shot the Coen brothers into the upper echelons of filmmakers right off the bat. Far beyond your average freshman fare, the Coen Brothers debut film Blood Simple is stylish, brutal, and tinged with that signature Coen wit. The owner of a seedy small-town Texas bar discovers that one of his employees is having an affair with his wife. A chaotic chain of misunderstandings, lies, and mischief ensues after he devises a plot to have them murdered.

title: Pushkin House: Hard to Be a God
LPFF 2026: Opening Night - Who is Still Alive (15*) + ScreenTalk
The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: Black Fire
description: Since 2013, artist Kevin Jerome Everson and author and historian Claudrena N. Harold have cooperated on a series of lyrical short films—13 to date—that explore Black intellectual, social, and political life at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, where both are professors. Collectively titled Black Fire , these works highlight the spaces where Black students have studied, learned, and organized through the years, including the school's student-run newspaper and a bus stop that became a locus for collective action. Through short films spotlighting figures such as Paulette Jones Morant, one of the first Black woman scholastic athletes at UVA, and Vivian Gordon, the director of UVA’s Black Studies program from 1974–1980, Black Fire creates significant space for otherwise under-the-radar figures. Employing interviews and reenactment, often casting their students as performers, Everson and Harold's films bring the history of UVA, as well as the historical experiences of Black students and faculty across the US, into meaningful conversation with the present day. Filmmakers Kevin Jerome Everson and Claudrena N. Harold appear in conversation after the films, moderated by filmmaker Cauleen Smith. Special thanks to Madeleine Molyneaux, Sam Raphael, and Now Instant Image Hall.

title: Evangelion: Death (True)² + The End of Evangelion : Double Feature
description: EVANGELION: DEATH (TRUE)²: A recap of the first 24 episodes of Neon Genesis Evangelion. Fifteen years after the Second Impact, apathetic teen Shinji joins his father's group NERV to fight the Angels. But the truth may destroy them all. THE END OF EVANGELION: Concurrent theatrical ending of the TV series Neon Genesis Evangelion (1995). Seele orders an all-out attack on NERV, aiming to destroy the Evas before Gendo can trigger Third Impact and Instrumentality under his control.

title: HOLD ME TIGHT / SERRE MOI FORT
description: With Vicky Krieps, Arieh Worthalter, Anne-Sophie Bowen-Chatet, and Sacha Ardilly. “Propelled by a fierce, tour-de-force performance by Vicky Krieps, who is fast becoming one of the most sought-after actors on the international scene, HOLD ME TIGHT is an ingenious memory piece exploring the grief of separation and the paradoxical comforts and claustrophobia of the domestic home. As Clarisse flees her family at daybreak and hits the open road, leaving her husband and two children behind, the film shuttles between time and space, becoming a mental landscape whose contours are gradually revealed like fleeting moments of reminiscence – those that ultimately make up a life. With its beguiling, puzzle-piece structure that builds to a shattering denouement, HOLD ME TIGHT powerfully keeps its audience in a state of hypnotic reverie as we share in the protagonist’s profound sense of disorientation, the sort of disembodied surrealism that uncertainty can unleash. Yet Krieps gives a surprisingly earth-bound, visceral performance as a woman negotiating a new path for herself, all while trying to stay close to those she loves and attempting to make sense of it all.” –Andréa Picard, TIFF

title: The Return of the Living Dead
description: The most fun you’ll ever have with the undead! A gang of Punks and New Wave ne’er-do-wells get trapped in a cemetery as the dead begin to rise and start to crash their party. And these aren’t your average zombies. They can talk, reason, and even make jokes, but make no mistake — they are still out for your brains. A total blast from start to finish, this monster bash features killer special effects, a rockin’ soundtrack, and one of scream queen Linnea Quigley’s most iconic moments. You’d be a ghoul to miss it!

title: FFC: Ernest and Celestine - Winter Tales (U*)
description: The delightful duo, Ernest and Celestine – a grumpy bear and a feisty mouse – are back in a series of four short stories perfect for a family cinema snuggle!

title: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
description: Another gem from Aardman Productions, adapted by Gideon Defoe from his children's book. The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists! follows a crew…

title: Troy
description: In year 1250 B.C. during the late Bronze age, two emerging nations begin to clash. Paris, the Trojan prince, convinces Helen, Queen of Sparta, to leave her husband Menelaus, and sail with him back to Troy. After Menelaus finds out that his wife was taken by the Trojans, he asks his brother Agamemnon to help him get her back. Agamemnon sees this as an opportunity for power. They set off with 1,000 ships holding 50,000 Greeks to Troy.

title: Frankenweenie
description: Based on Tim Burton’s 1984 short film, Frankenweenie follows young Victor Frankenstein as he goes about his childhood making short films with his four-legged canine friend, Sparky. When Sparky is killed by a car, a distraught Victor resurrects him. Soon other children start resurrecting their own pets, and a horde of undead creatures wreaks havoc, spurring the adults to plot Sparky’s permanent demise. This black-and-white stop motion Frankenstein adaptation features a score by frequent Burton collaborator Danny Elfman and is filled with homages to the classic horror films Burton grew up loving, resulting in a scary and sweet fairytale that will dazzle children and charm adults.
director: Tim Burton PRODUCED BY: Allison Abbate, Tim Burton

title: TWO SEASONS, TWO STRANGERS
description: Based on two mangas by Yoshiharu Tsuge, Miyake’s bifurcated live-action feature observes (and draws parallels and contrasts from) a summertime meet-cute between Nagisa and Natsuo and a snowbound winter encounter between screenwriter Li and innkeeper Benzo.

title: PRIFF Programme 1
description: BETWEEN WORLDS brings together two stories of people searching for their place in the world. In Manila, half-Filipina Nia trains in secret with queer outcast Malic to join a Filipino Martial Arts team, learning that winning begins with accepting who she is. In a remote Senegalese village, young albino Ousmane faces daily insults and threats rooted in superstition, until he and his mother set out across the desert towards Europe, facing exhaustion, dehydration and ruthless smugglers along the way. Together, these films explore what it means to be different, and how difference can become a source of rejection or of shared strength.

title: The Princess Bride
description: A fairy tale adventure about a beautiful young woman and her one true love. He must find her after a long separation and save her. They must battle the evils of the mythical kingdom of Florin to be reunited with each other.

description: Mitsuha and Taki are total strangers living completely different lives. But when Mitsuha makes a wish to leave her mountain town for the bustling city of Tokyo, they become connected in a bizarre way. She dreams she is a boy living in Tokyo, while Taki dreams he is a girl from a rural town he has ne...

title: PRIFF Programme 2
description: INHERITANCE brings together six films about what we inherit from our families and the systems that shape our lives. Alone in an empty church, a writer sets out to sever his relationship with God, only for a childhood memory of violence to turn his accusation back on himself. Malaika prepares for her wedding while struggling to live up to the ideal bride imposed by her mother and her Kenyan heritage. Released from prison, young father Obi arrives at a Nigerian café in a spacesuit, stretching the lie that he has been in space just long enough to win over his curious daughter. In racially divided 1950s Britain, an Afro Caribbean miner struggles to find acceptance above ground. Sound recordist Dina turns to her craft to preserve the presence of her mother, a classical singer, as her health fades. And Out of the Ashes follows the organisers who, in 2020, built a fund of their own for Black and brown communities, challenging centuries of deciding who deserves help.
