title: DÉJÀ VU
description: Called in to recover evidence in the aftermath of a horrific explosion on a New Orleans ferry, Federal agent Doug Carlin (Denzel Washington) gets pulled away from the scene and taken to a top-secret government lab that uses a time-shifting surveillance device to help prevent crime. But can it help Carlin change the past? Hold on to your seat for an explosive and intriguing thrill ride you’ll want to experience again and again.

title: LPFF 2026: Who is Still Alive (15*) + ScreenTalk
description: Nine voices from Gaza. Nine people who tell of their lives before and amid the destruction, in the neighbourhoods whose outlines they draw in chalk on the ground.

title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
description: In the 1930s, the Grand Budapest Hotel is a popular European ski resort, presided over by concierge Gustave H. (Ralph Fiennes). Zero, a junior lobby boy, becomes Gustave's friend and protege. Gustave prides himself on providing first-class service to the hotel's guests, including satisfying the sexual needs of the many elderly women who stay there. When one of Gustave's lovers dies mysteriously, Gustave finds himself the recipient of a priceless painting and the chief suspect in her murder.

title: MUSIC IS MUSIC + BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE
description: Mathieu Amalric MUSIC IS MUSIC 2017, 20 min, DCP “In a poetic composition of song, narration, and images, this film follows Canadian soprano and orchestra conductor Barbara Hannigan, accompanied by the Ludwig Orchestra, as she records her album ‘Crazy Girl Crazy’. Why did she choose these three pieces, in essence so different, but which intimately resonate with her: Berio’s ‘Sequenza III’, Berg’s ‘Lulu Suite’, and Gershwin’s ‘Girl Crazy’?” –INTERNATIONAL FESTIVAL OF FILMS ON ART Mathieu Amalric BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE / AVANT QU’IL NE SOIT TROP TARD 2023, 65 min, DCP “After 47 years together, the Emerson String Quartet records their last album, ‘Infinite Voyage’, in three days. For this farewell, they invited soprano Barbara Hannigan, and a film was born. Their precise work, the moments of enthusiasm and fear, the research and the jokes, the age limit of these men and Hannigan’s flamboyance, the admiring friendship full of irony and rigor, the profession and yet the discovery, humor as a cog towards concentration, the individual and the group…all this composes a portrait of the usually invisible production of music. Before everyone resumes their path.” –DOCLISBOA Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: TIMES SQUARE
description:
Two teenagers escape a psychiatric hospital and turn the streets of New York into their stage. As the Sleez Sisters, Pamela and Nicky invent a noisy new identity that parents, police and respectable society cannot comfortably contain.
Trini Alvarado and Robin Johnson give Allan Moyle’s cult film its bruised, rebellious heart. A tremendous punk and new-wave soundtrack propels a vision of friendship as self-invention, against a Midtown that has since disappeared. Ragged, romantic and fiercely attached to its outsiders, TIMES SQUARE is a love song to girls making themselves heard.

title: On the Waterfront
description: I coulda been a contender. I coulda been somebody, instead of a bum, which is what I am, let’s face it. You might know that iconic quote, and you might be aware that Marlon Brando’s performance in this movie was a game-changer in film history, helping to popularize the more naturalistic style known as Method acting. But don’t let that overshadow the film itself, a masterpiece that earned eight Academy Awards (including Best Picture) and remains just as powerful 70 years later. Brando plays Terry Malloy, a longshoreman and former boxer who grows to resent the mobsters who control his local union. And in her film debut, Eva Marie Saint is luminous as Terry’s love interest, who acts as his conscience and inspires him to take a stand and fight back – no matter what the cost.

title: EC: INTOLERANCE
description: Griffith’s immensely influential silent epic intercuts four parallel tales from history (spanning Babylon, Christ’s Judea, Reformation Europe, and turn-of-the-century America) to embroider a moral tapestry on personal, social, and political repression through the ages. The visual poetry is overwhelming, especially in the massed crowd scenes, and the unbridled eroticism of the Babylon harem scenes demonstrates just what Hollywood lost when it later bowed to the Hays Code. While the (partly self-financed) production ruined Griffith financially and baffled audiences with its multiple plots and labyrinthine structure, it has been enormously influential on generations of filmmakers, including Eisenstein, who studied the film closely. title: Predator
description: A team of elite commandos on a secret mission in a Central American jungle come to find themselves hunted by an extraterrestrial warrior.

title: ZORN I + II
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN I (2010-2016) 2017, 54 min, DCP “The tense, but smiling face of maverick composer legend John Zorn listening to music might just restore your faith in human beauty. Every muscle moves in harmony with sounds and chords, it’s like seeing a soul wandering off into another realm. Mathieu Amalric has been filming this zestful musician for more than 12 years now. They first met when the actor and filmmaker narrated Zorn’s vocal album Shir Hashirim live in Paris. Those familiar with Amalric’s haptic cinema will immediately understand what drew him to Zorn and vice versa. They connect through their constant and obsessive drive for feelings and sensations, their tireless energy devoted to the art, their hunger for life. In the style of a home movie, Amalric accompanies Zorn at concerts, city walks, inside the sound studio or at practice.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Mathieu Amalric ZORN II (2016-2018) 2018, 59 min, DCP “In the second part of his ongoing portrait of the prolific musician, Amalric shows the artist as a social man. Like a sponge, Zorn takes in whatever surrounds him: people (mostly colleagues from the New York Underground scene), dreams, technology, cinema (screening films by Maya Deren or Harry Smith during his performances), places and the emotions evoked by sounds. […] Amalric chooses a more structured approach than in the first part. Text inserts reveal details about the composer’s life and his philosophy. The camera gets more in tune with Zorn’s eruptive movements, as he goes onstage at sold-out concert halls as if he were just discovering the instruments there during an evening stroll. He plays each note as if it was the first or last, and Amalric tries to film him accordingly.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Total running time: ca. 120 min.

description: As the nights draw in, we're very excited to be screening one of the earliest horror masterpieces, The Phantom of the…

title: Fargo
description: Minnesota car salesman Jerry Lundegaard's inept crime falls apart due to his and his henchmen's bungling and the persistent police work of the quite pregnant Marge Gunderson.

title: STAY
description:
STAY tells the story of an artist (The Artist) sentenced to do time in The Curfew Tower, with only a handheld puppet of Elvis (Puppet Elvis) as company. While doing time, The Artist is expected to write the second-best song he has ever written. And this song is for the Ghost of Elvis and is to be performed at The 25 Comeback Special. In reality The Artist is just trying to escape the gathering storm clouds of his inevitable midlife crisis. That, and the reality of being a bad father. The only dialogue in the film is an internal one between The Artist and Puppet Elvis.
STAY is probably the bleakest film you could ever watch. It contains no sex or violence, no kissing or killing, not even any fucking or fighting, or any of those other things some might want to vicariously experience via the medium of film. STAY is a film without HOPE.
The screening at The Nickel is to be the only screening in UK in 2026. Tracey Moberly, Tony Wright & Puppet Elvis will be there for a post screening interrogation. The former Bill Drummond will be there to chair the interrogation. He will also be there to stamp people’s wrists as they enter the building.
WARNING: It is expected that everyone attending this screening will bring their own handheld puppet to watch the film with them – No Puppet, No Entry. Also... Puppet Elvis will be the judge of the post Interrogation Puppet Contest.

title: Pretty in Pink
description: Put on your dancing shoes and get ready for this all-time teen classic of high school romance, jealousy, resourcefulness, and classism. Molly Ringwald plays Andie, a creative outcast from the wrong side of the tracks who falls for a rich kid (80’s heartthrob Andrew McCarthy) and ends up causing rifts in both their worlds. This sweet and stylish romance features incredible performances from the entire cast including Annie Potts as the fashionista record store owner, Jon Cryer as the Otis Redding lip-syncing obsessed best friend, James Spader as the vilest of the upper crust, and of course Vidiots favorite Harry Dean Stanton as her single father.

title: Jealousy Is My Middle Name
description: Park Hae-il plays Lee Won-sang, the hero of Park Chan-ok’s debut feature, in his second big-screen appearance. Lee is a 27-year-old graduate student in literature, finishing up his thesis before he leaves for London. When he starts writing an article for a magazine as a favor, he realizes that the head editor, Han Yun-shik, is the reason his girlfriend left him. Lee’s complicated feelings toward Han, a mixture of admiration and jealousy, brings more confusion when he is introduced to a mesmerizing photographer, Park Sung-yeon, a cool, down-to-earth woman who is also having an affair with Han. Calm on the surface but roiling underneath, the story explores human emotions in a macro lens, excavating endless variables that shape characters while they struggle to stay composed. Park’s undefinable approach to Lee allows his character’s purity and honesty to roam free.

title: EC: EGGELING / GRANT / JACOBS & FLEISCHNER
description: Viking Eggeling SYMPHONIE DIAGONALE (1924, 8 min, 35mm, silent) “This early experimental short is one of only two films completed by Swedish-born artist Viking Eggeling, who worked in Paris, Milan, and ultimately Germany. It utilizes paper cutouts, tin foil, and frame-by-frame photography to create a playful show in which cubist, even art deco, circles and lines dance – diagonally – across the black screen.” –FACETS Dwinell Grant COMPOSITION #2 CONTRATHEMIS (1941, 5 min, 16mm, silent) “An attempt to develop visual abstract themes and to counterpoint them in a planned, formal composition.” –Dwinell Grant STOP MOTION TESTS (1942, 3 min, 16mm, silent) A pixillated self-portrait of the filmmaker in his studio. COLOR SEQUENCE (1943, 3 min, 16mm, silent) “Pure solid-color frames which fade, mutate and flicker. A research into color rhythms and perceptual phenomena.” –William Moritz Ken Jacobs & Bob Fleischner BLONDE COBRA 1959-63, 35 min, 16mm-to-35mm blow-up. With Jack Smith. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from The Film Foundation. “BLONDE COBRA is an erratic narrative – no, not really a narrative, it’s only stretched out in time for convenience of delivery. It’s a look in on an exploding life, on a man of imagination suffering pre-fashionable Lower East Side deprivation and consumed with American 1950s, 40s, 30s disgust. Silly, self-pitying, guilt-strictured and yet triumphing – on one level – over the situation with style… enticing us into an absurd moral posture the better to dismiss us with a regal ‘screw off.’” –Ken Jacobs Total running time: ca. 60 min. title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: ZORN III
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN III (2018-2022) 2022, 82 min, DCP. With John Zorn and Barbara Hannigan. “Why can’t Mathieu Amalric stop filming John Zorn? It’s because consciously or unconsciously, he understands that he can only get closer to this man if he imitates his restlessness. It’s this Sisyphean tirelessness, the fact that we must imagine Zorn (whose surname translates into German as anger) as a happy man, which is at the core of his art. He makes music in order to be alive. This time, however, Zorn is not the only protagonist, as the Canadian soprano Barbara Hannigan enters the wild world of the composer. Much more straightforward than its previous iterations, the film captures Hannigan’s rehearsals for a performance of Zorn’s song cycle ‘Jumalattaret’ together with pianist Stephen Gosling. The work pushes her vocal capacities to the limit, with the sudden shifts in register, extended high notes and bird-like chirping demanding everything from her.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE

title: Cinema Paradiso [Nuovo Cinema Paradiso]
description: A winner of awards across the world including Best Foreign Language Film Oscar, 5 BAFTA Awards including Best Actor, Original Screenplay and Score, the Grand Prize of the Jury at the Cannes Film Festival and many more. Giuseppe Tornatore's loving homage to the cinema tells the story of Salvatore, a successful film director, returning home for the funeral of Alfredo, his old friend who was the projectionist at the local cinema throughout his childhood. Soon memories of his first love affair with the beautiful Elena and all the highs and lows that shaped his life come flooding back, as Salvatore reconnects with the community he left 30 years earlier.

title: VALERIE AND HER WEEK OF WONDERS
description:
A pair of enchanted earrings offers Valerie protection as her village fills with vampires, corrupt holy men and relatives who will not stay in the same shape. Growing up here means discovering that familiar faces can become the strangest masks.
Jaromil Jireš makes a fairy tale from the collision of innocence, fear and awakening. Jan Curík’s luminous images and Luboš Fišer’s haunting score give the Czech New Wave fantasy the vividness of a half-remembered dream. Beautiful and deeply uncanny, it draws folk horror out of sunlight as readily as shadow.
Presented by Softcore Cinema Club.

title: Stop Making Sense
description: We’re bringing the party back to the big screen to kick off our birthday weekend like rock stars! Join us for one of our favorite cinematic/musical experiences with a reprise of legendary Director Jonathan Demme’s ecstatic musical masterpiece Stop Making Sense. Filmed at the Hollywood Pantages Theater in December 1983, this fascinating piece of musical memorabilia showcases the Talking Heads boundless creativity and showmanship on stage and off. A one-of-a-kind experience, join Vidiots as we revel in 41 years of Vidiots and the 42nd anniversary of this groundbreaking film, newly remastered in a stunning 4K presentation.

title: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
description: Another gem from Aardman Productions, adapted by Gideon Defoe from his children's book. The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists! follows a crew…

title: Labyrinth - 40th Anniversary
description: Step back into the fantastical world of Jim Henson’s Labyrinth as the beloved classic returns to cinemas for a special 40th-anniversary re-release. Starring David Bowie in one of his most entertaining film performances as the enigmatic Goblin King, this 4K re-issue brings Jim Henson’s dazzling puppetry, imaginative landscapes, and iconic musical moments back to the big screen where they belong. Join the adventure as Sarah (Jennifer Connelly) races against time to navigate the mysterious Labyrinth and rescue her baby brother in this spellbinding cult favourite.

title: Mildred Pierce
description: When Mildred Pierce's wealthy husband leaves her for another woman, Mildred decides to raise her two daughters on her own. Despite Mildred's financial successes in the restaurant business, her oldest daughter, Veda, resents her mother for degrading their social status. In the midst of a police investigation after the death of her second husband, Mildred must evaluate her own freedom and her complicated relationship with her daughter.

title: The Care Bears Movie
description: Join hands and form the circle of friendship with your favorite cuddly toy-turned-cartoon characters. The Care Bears team up with a troubled brother and sister who just moved to a new town to help a neglected young magician’s apprentice whose evil spell book causes sinister things to happen. Who says little furry creatures can’t make a difference?

title: THE PATSY
description: An awkward teenager hopelessly in love with her older sister’s boyfriend tries to make him notice her.

title: An Unfinished Film
description: ★★★★★ “An utterly unique and very important movie about Covid, the crisis that affected all of us.” – The Guardian Director Xiaorui convinces his cast and crew to resume the shooting of a film halted ten years earlier. In January 2020, with the shoot almost complete, rumours regarding an illness begin to circulate. A hairdresser from Wuhan is sent home, while the crew follows the news on their phones. The director has to decide whether to halt the filming once again. Some of the crew and actors manage to leave before the hotel is locked down by security guards and everyone left on set is confined to their hotel rooms. As all communication is reduced to phone screens, Wuhan is locked down. The crew continues to communicate via video calls, whilst the quarantined main actor Jiang Cheng struggles to support his wife who is now locked-down with their month-old baby in Beijing.

title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
description: Writer-director Wes Anderson was inspired by Austrian novelist Stefan Zweig (1881-1942) for his seriocomic and visually dazzling story about a posh resort, its vain concierge (Ralph Fiennes in a peerless comic performance) and a young lobby boy (Tony Revolori). Anderson directed an all-star international cast and brought his distinctive visual sensibilities to his original story (written with Hugo Guinness), set in a fictional European country on the eve of war. The film received nine nominations including Best Picture and won Oscars for Alexandre Desplat’s effervescent score, Milena Canonero’s costume design, the makeup and hair creations of Frances Hannon and Mark Coulier, and the production design of Adam Stockhausen and his set decorator, Anna Pinnock, who transformed a vacant German department store into the eponymous hotel.

title: MAÎTRES ANCIENS – COMÉDIE
description: “Like Reger – the character [Austrian novelist and playwright] Thomas Bernhard placed on a museum bench facing a painting by Tintoretto, an ‘Old Master’ if ever there was one – an actor finds himself alone and thwarted after a notorious virus forces the indefinite closure of theaters. He wanders through an empty auditorium, paces the now-useless backstage areas, and bursts out into a street haunted by masked passersby. Having persuaded a firefighter to keep watch over him and his explosives, he pours out – to the guard and the surrounding silence alike – his loathing for, among other things, Heideggerians, a lack of punctuality, people who admire rather than respect, and the State’s appropriation of children. At the intersection of cinema and theater, despair and the will to survive, 1980s Austria and 2020s France, Bernhard’s text takes on a new resonance: ‘And as for culture in this country, your stomach exists only to turn.’” –Marie Hermann, FIDMarseille Preceded by: Mathieu Amalric C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE (2015, 16 min, digital. With Barbara Hannigan.) “In C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE, I explore a mystery that fascinates me: where do these inhuman voices come from? From where in the body does the unsettling anomaly of singing originate?” –Mathieu Amalric Total running time: ca. 100 min.

title: Highlander
description: After inexplicably surviving a mortal wound during a clan battle in the Scottish Highlands in 1536, Connor MacLeod (Christopher Lambert) is accused of witchcraft and banished from his village. Years later, he meets Ramirez (Sean Connery), a swordsman who teaches MacLeod the truth about himself: he belongs to an immortal race who can only die when the head is cut from the body. MacLeod fights his way through the centuries until the time of The Gathering, when the few immortals who have survived the ages will come together to fight until just one remains. In 1980s New York City the final fight is about to begin and, in the end, there can be only one...

title: MYSTERY DOJO: SURPRISE KUNG FU MATINEES
description:
Enter the 36 Chambers of Grindhouse Cinema, with these Sunday mystery martial-arts matinees that harken back to the glory days of 42nd Street.
Expect deep-cut chopsocky plucked from the 70s and 80s screening on both digital and VHS - with bone-crushing bashers from the genre that mixed Chinese folklore and fantasy, spaghetti westerns, melodrama, Japanese samurai films and American genre cinema into an electrifying combo that inspired both the future of action films - and hip hop.
These Kung Fu flicks became an international sensation in the 1970s, particularly at the Grindhouse cinemas that proliferated in impoverished inner-cities. Here were movies in which working-class heroes stood up to oppression, speaking loud and clear to the marginalised underclasses around the world.
Bring the ruckus!

title: Paisàn
description: The second installment in his WWII trilogy and one of Rossellini’s favorites of his films, the episodic Paisàn is another depiction of the tribulations of the Italians under German occupation. Its title translates to “fellow countryman” and takes a broader view of Italy than his previous Rome, Open City (1945) , moving the action outside the capital to focus on the interactions between American armed forces and the country residents impacted by conflict. Future Italian auteur Federico Fellini co-wrote the screenplay, which came together on the fly, with dialogue of each sequence written just before it was filmed.
director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Rod E. Geiger, Roberto Rossellini

title: Imamura: Pirates of Bubuan + Outlaw-Matsu Returns Home
Imitation of Life (1959) on 35mm
description: Lana Turner, Juanita Moore, and Sandra Dee light up the screen in this Douglas Sirk tearjerking melodrama of single mothers and racial identity. The second screen adaptation of Fannie Hurst’s incendiery novel, Douglas Sirk ratchets up the drama, the color, and the story of this powerful tale of women’s resilience from its predecessor with Claudette Colbert. Lora Meredith (suspected murderess Lana Turner), a white single mother who dreams of being on Broadway, takes in a black widow Annie (Juanita Moore) and her mixed race daughter (Susan Kohner) to live with her and her daughter (Sandra Dee). Together, the women deal with the maelstrom of life’s ups and downs including the toll of success and Annie’s daughter desperately trying to erase her racial identity and come off as white. With incredible female characters and actors, that gorgeous Sirkian Technicolor touch, and a story of race that was decades ahead of its time, this classic melodrama is ready to pull you in and give you all the feels!

description: Misa suffers from severe PMS, which can unravel her otherwise demure disposition with violent disregard for personal or professional company. Finally holding down a job assembling science kits for kids, she befriends Takatoshi, a withdrawn colleague prone to debilitating panic attacks.

EC: UNE SIMPLE HISTOIRE
description: “Based on a true incident, the film chronicles the wanderings of a woman and child looking for work and lodging in Paris. This is the only plot, and Hanoun has little interest in embellishing it with background and motivation: he never even makes it clear, for example, whether the woman is the child’s mother, guardian or companion. UNE SIMPLE HISTOIRE is, more than a narrative, a formal stylistic exercise so rigorously disciplined and understated that it makes the visual asceticism of Robert Bresson seem almost Fellini-esque by comparison.” –TIME CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: In a Lonely Place
description: A screenwriter with a violent temper is a murder suspect until his lovely neighbor clears him. However, she soon starts to have her doubts.

title: ZORN I + II
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN I (2010-2016) 2017, 54 min, DCP “The tense, but smiling face of maverick composer legend John Zorn listening to music might just restore your faith in human beauty. Every muscle moves in harmony with sounds and chords, it’s like seeing a soul wandering off into another realm. Mathieu Amalric has been filming this zestful musician for more than 12 years now. They first met when the actor and filmmaker narrated Zorn’s vocal album Shir Hashirim live in Paris. Those familiar with Amalric’s haptic cinema will immediately understand what drew him to Zorn and vice versa. They connect through their constant and obsessive drive for feelings and sensations, their tireless energy devoted to the art, their hunger for life. In the style of a home movie, Amalric accompanies Zorn at concerts, city walks, inside the sound studio or at practice.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Mathieu Amalric ZORN II (2016-2018) 2018, 59 min, DCP “In the second part of his ongoing portrait of the prolific musician, Amalric shows the artist as a social man. Like a sponge, Zorn takes in whatever surrounds him: people (mostly colleagues from the New York Underground scene), dreams, technology, cinema (screening films by Maya Deren or Harry Smith during his performances), places and the emotions evoked by sounds. […] Amalric chooses a more structured approach than in the first part. Text inserts reveal details about the composer’s life and his philosophy. The camera gets more in tune with Zorn’s eruptive movements, as he goes onstage at sold-out concert halls as if he were just discovering the instruments there during an evening stroll. He plays each note as if it was the first or last, and Amalric tries to film him accordingly.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Total running time: ca. 120 min.

title: DONT LOOK BACK + BOB DYLAN CONCERT FOOTAGE
description:
Dylan on stage is only half the story. In hotel rooms, backstage corridors and combative interviews during his 1965 British tour, he is inventing—and resisting—the public figure everyone wants him to become.
D. A. Pennebaker’s camera catches the wit, the cruelty, the boredom and the sudden electricity without a narrator telling us what to think. From the cue cards of “Subterranean Homesick Blues” to performances alive with concentration, this landmark music documentary puts you in the room at the moment a musician becomes an enigma.
Presented with a programme of Bob Dylan concert footage.

title: LPFF 2026: Partition + The Flowers Stand Silently, Witnessing + ScreenTalk
EC: JEROME HILL
description: These 35mm prints are the result of a preservation project undertaken by the Museum of Modern Art. DEATH IN THE FORENOON (1934/66, 2 min, 35mm) CANARIES (1969, 4 min, 35mm) & FILM PORTRAIT (1971, 81 min, 35mm) “FILM PORTRAIT is an autobiography in the sense that it deals explicitly with Jerome’s most personal life’s relationship to film. It draws on film clips taken in his childhood and his whole childhood involvement in art and life. It comes closest to any kind of filmic answer to Proust. […] FILM PORTRAIT is, I believe, the only direct autobiography we have in film. There is Jonas Mekas’s WALDEN, which is diary but not autobiography in a strict sense. We have Cocteau’s BLOOD OF A POET, ORPHEUS, and TESTAMENT OF ORPHEUS. One could say that this last is autobiographical, but it is also allusive and poetic; whereas Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT is a very straight attempt to present autobiography on film. Of course, subsequently, James Broughton’s TESTAMENT and my own SINCERITY & DUPLICITY series of autobiographical films were very much inspired by Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT as well as by Jonas’s WALDEN. […] Jerome Hill’s films are great because they are poised on wit and achieve a balance – a gentle, intentional, particularly American balance.” –Stan Brakhage, FILM AT WIT’S END Total running time: ca. 90 min. The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: Germany Year Zero
description: Released the same year the first theories of neo-realism were published in film magazines Esprit, La Revue du Cinéma , and Bianco e Nero by acclaimed critics, including André Bazin, Germany Year Zero rounds out Rossellini’s WWII trilogy and brings a continental scope to the devastating impact of Hitler’s final solution. By centering the story on a young boy navigating the devastating implications of war, Rossellini accentuates the stark contrast between generations. A major influence on François Truffaut’s The 400 Blows (1959) and cast with people the director found by exploring the four zones of Berlin, Germany Year Zero would, Rossellini hoped, “reproduce the truth exactly as the camera saw it for that audience through the entire world which has a heart capable of love and a brain capable of thought.”

title: PAT GARRETT AND BILLY THE KID + BOB DYLAN CONCERT FOOTAGE
description:
Pat Garrett takes a badge and a job: kill the friend who represents the life he has left behind. Billy the Kid keeps moving, even as the West is being bought, fenced and brought to heel around him.
James Coburn and Kris Kristofferson give Sam Peckinpah’s elegiac western its weathered soul. Bob Dylan drifts through as Alias and supplies songs that seem to mourn the landscape itself. Less a chase than a long farewell, this is a film about friendship becoming history—and the terrible price of choosing the winning side.
Presented with a programme of Bob Dylan concert footage.

title: EC: HUGO / JACOBS / LEVITT / MAAS
description: Ian Hugo BELLS OF ATLANTIS (1952, 10 min, 16mm. Preserved by the Library of Congress through the Avant-Garde Masters program funded by The Film Foundation and administered by the National Film Preservation Foundation.) A film poem, based on Anaïs Nin’s HOUSE OF INCEST, narrated by and featuring Nin. “[BELLS OF ATLANTIS was] inspired by the prologue to my HOUSE OF INCEST and the line: ‘I remember my first birth in water.’ The film evoked the watery depths of the lost continent of Atlantis. It is a lyrical journey into prenatal memories, the theme of birth and rebirth from the sea.” –Anaïs Nin Ken Jacobs LITTLE STABS AT HAPPINESS (1959-63, 18 min, 16mm. With Jack Smith.) “Material was cut in as it came out of the camera, embarrassing moments intact. 100’ rolls timed well with music on old 78s. I was interested in immediacy, a sense of ease, and an art where suffering was acknowledged but not trivialized with dramatics. Whimsy was our achievement, as well as breaking out of step.” –Ken Jacobs Helen Levitt, Janice Loeb, and James Agee IN THE STREET (1952, 12 min, 16mm, silent. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives.) “Informality is indeed the crucial and virtually definitive quality of IN THE STREET; it is even the guiding principle and vision. […] This is the extreme realization of a classic ‘naturalistic’ genre, the German ‘street film,’ where the street was imaged as the arena of the everyday and random, the channel in which the ‘stream of life’ conveniently became microcosmic.” –Ken Kelman, THE ESSENTIAL CINEMA Willard Maas GEOGRAPHY OF THE BODY (1943, 7 min, 16mm, b&w. Preserved by Anthology with support from The National Film Preservation Foundation.) “The terrors and splendors of the human body as the undiscovered, mysterious continent.” –Willard Maas Total running time: ca. 55 min. title: Whiplash
description: Andrew Neiman (Miles Teller) is an ambitious young jazz drummer, in pursuit of rising to the top of his elite music conservatory. Terence Fletcher (J.K. Simmons), an instructor known for his terrifying teaching methods, discovers Andrew and transfers the aspiring drummer into the top jazz ensemble, forever changing the young man's life. But Andrew's passion to achieve perfection quickly spirals into obsession, as his ruthless teacher pushes him to the brink of his ability and his sanity.

title: Empire of Passion
description: With an arresting mix of eroticism and horror, Oshima plunges the viewer into a nightmarish tale of guilt and retribution in Empire of Passion (Ai no borei). Set in a Japanese village at the end of the nineteenth century, the film details the emotional and physical downfall of a married woman and her younger lover following their decision to murder her husband and dump his body in a well. Empire of Passion was Oshima's only true kaidan (Japanese ghost story), and the film, a savage, unrelenting experience, earned him the best director award at the Cannes Film Festival.

title: Taxi Driver
description: Suffering from insomnia, disturbed loner Travis Bickle (Robert De Niro) takes a job as a New York City cabbie, haunting the streets nightly, growing increasingly detached from reality as he dreams of cleaning up the filthy city. When Travis meets pretty campaign worker Betsy (Cybill Shepherd), he becomes obsessed with the idea of saving the world, first plotting to assassinate a presidential candidate, then directing his attentions toward rescuing 12-year-old prostitute Iris (Jodie Foster).

title: The Misfits
description: Penned by Arthur Miller, this contemporary Western centers on the recently divorced Roslyn (Marilyn Monroe) and her relationship with an aging former cowboy, Gay (Clark Gable), who now survives by rounding up wild mustangs to sell them to a slaughterhouse. Considered a commercial failure at the time of its original release, the film has since been regarded as a classic by critics and audiences, perhaps notably because it was the final completed film of both Gable and Monroe, and a fitting bookend to Monroe’s career—she credited Huston for her first big break in his The Asphalt Jungle (1950).

title: The Squid & The Whale
description: * ON SALE 23rd OCT * With excruciating honesty, The Squid and the Whale chronicles the experiences of two young brothers growing up in 1980s Park Slope, Brooklyn, as they navigate the jagged contours of the divorce of their parents, both writers. The acclaimed third feature by Noah Baumbach marked a critical development for the filmmaker as he turned toward an increasingly personal style—a move that garnered him an Academy Award nomination for best original screenplay. Shot in Super 16 mm and featuring a quartet of nuanced, understated performances from Jeff Daniels, Laura Linney, Jesse Eisenberg, and Owen Kline, this comic and poignant drama, peppered with autobiographical elements, deftly captures the heartache and confusion of a fracturing family.

title: Trainspotting - 30th Anniversary
description: Heroin addict Mark Renton (Ewan McGregor) stumbles through bad ideas and sobriety attempts with his unreliable friends -- Sick Boy (Jonny Lee Miller), Begbie (Robert Carlyle), Spud (Ewen Bremner) and Tommy (Kevin McKidd). He also has an underage girlfriend, Diane (Kelly Macdonald), along for the ride. After cleaning up and moving from Edinburgh to London, Mark finds he can't escape the life he left behind when Begbie shows up at his front door on the lam, and a scheming Sick Boy follows.

The camera gets more in tune with Zorn’s eruptive movements, as he goes onstage at sold-out concert halls as if he were just discovering the instruments there during an evening stroll. He plays each note as if it was the first or last, and Amalric tries to film him accordingly.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Total running time: ca. 120 min.

title: TOKYO DRIFTER
description:
Tetsu wants to leave the yakuza behind. Loyalty keeps dragging him back. Sent away from Tokyo, he becomes a wandering target in a gangster story that seems to shed another piece of realism with every mile.
Seijun Suzuki turns a studio assignment into pure pop-art invention: snowbound pursuits, neon nightclubs, startling colour and a final space almost abstract enough to swallow the actors. Tetsuya Watari’s cool presence and recurring theme song hold the delirium together. A crime film that dances away from the rules while still carrying a gun.

title: Cinematic Void Presents W.R.: MYSTERIES OF THE ORGANISM
description: What does the energy harnessed through orgasm have to do with the state of communist Yugoslavia circa 1971? Only counterculture filmmaker extraordinaire Dušan Makavejev has the answers (or the questions). His surreal documentary-fiction collision WR: MYSTERIES OF THE ORGANISM begins as an investigation into the life and work of controversial psychologist and philosopher Wilhelm Reich and then explodes into a free-form narrative of a beautiful young Slavic girl’s sexual liberation. Banned upon its release in the director’s homeland, the art-house smash WR is both whimsical and bold in its blending of politics and sexuality.

title: DORSKY & HILER, PGM 1: NATHANIEL DORSKY
description: CARACOLE (FOR IZCALI) 2023, 17.5 min, 16mm, silent “In the last few years I have been making a series of cinematic portraits of young filmmaking friends acting as collaborators in portraiture. There is always a surprise as to what the Bolex reveals of a person that is not revealed with the naked eye. This happened in a very strong way with Jacob while shooting PAVANE. But I was not prepared for the surprise that took place when I looked through the camera at Linda. I suddenly saw her as never before and asked without hesitation if she were Aztec. She responded enthusiastically that indeed she was, in fact, her middle name is Izcali, after the important Aztec festival month of rebirth.” –Nathaniel Dorsky NAOS 2022, 12 min, 16mm, silent “A Naos is the inner room of an ancient Greek temple in which the image of the deity celebrated by that temple is depicted (usually in the form of a statue of that deity). Jacob, a young filmmaker, offered to help me with some shooting and became the center of the film itself.” –Nathaniel Dorsky DREAMS REVEAL A WEIGHTLESS WORLD 2016/24, 20 min, 16mm, silent “OSSUARY was made up of the Kodachrome outs and trims from more than a decade of shooting and making films in Kodachrome. This new film, DREAMS REVEAL A WEIGHTLESS WORLD, is made from the Kodachrome outs from editing OSSUARY… It is the outs of the outs, so to speak.” –Nathaniel Dorsky Total running time: ca. 55 min.

title: Love Exposure
description: The story of a teenage boy named Yu, who falls for Yoko, a girl he runs into while working as an "up-skirt" photographer in an offshoot of the porn industry. His attempts to woo her are complicated by a spot of cross-dressing – which convinces Yoko that she is lesbian – dalliances with kung-fu and crime, and a constant struggle with the guilt that's a legacy of his Catholic upbringing. Contains very strong bloody violence and sex references

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick bent the conventions of the historical drama to his own will in this dazzling vision of a pitiless aristocracy, adapted from a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray. In picaresque detail, Barry Lyndon chronicles the adventures of an incorrigible trickster (Ryan O’Neal) whose opportunism takes him from an Irish farm to the battlefields of the Seven Years’ War and the parlours of high society. For the most sumptuously crafted film of his career, Kubrick recreated the decadent surfaces and intricate social codes of the period, evoking the light and texture of eighteenth-century painting with the help of pioneering cinematographic techniques and lavish costume and production design, all of which earned Academy Awards. The result is a masterpiece—a sardonic, devastating portrait of a vanishing world whose opulence conceals the moral vacancy at its heart. Please Note: The film will be presented with a brief 5-10min intermission.

title: LPFF 2026: Shorts Programme - From Ground Zero+ (15*)
L’amore
description: “I’ve made films in episodes because I feel more at ease like that.” —Roberto Rossellini, 1952 Rossellini’s appreciation for episodic storytelling, which his later forays into television allowed him to explore with more freedom, first began in feature-length filmmaking. Part one, titled “Una voce umana,” is based on a play by Jean Cocteau and features the filmmaker’s then-lover, esteemed actress Anna Magnani, known only as the woman on the phone, speaking to a former flame. In part two, “Il miracolo,” a woman is sure she is pregnant with the child of a saint. Dubbed the best foreign film that year by New York critics, Amore was also met with derision when Rossellini was charged with blasphemy by the city’s archbishop due to the content of the film’s second half.

title: British Horror Studio: Black Chariot
description: Introducing a season from the British Horror Studio. An independent British film studio Focusing on Gothic drama and arthouse filmmaking with a distinctive British horror character. Black Chariot is a supernatural noir horror film steeped in guilt, grief, and the lingering shadows of a crime gone wrong. Set within a world of doomed criminals, haunted survivors, private detectives, and sinister apparitions, the film draws on the mood of classic noir and the dread of Gothic horror to tell a character-driven story of violence, memory, and consequence. Starring Laurence R. Harvey, Megan Tremethick, Novarro Ramon, Dorian Todd, Sam McMillan, Richard Pate, and Nick Ford, Black Chariot places damaged characters at the centre of its supernatural mystery. As the past tightens its grip, the film becomes a dark meditation on trauma, masculinity, guilt, and the terrible price of trying to outrun the dead. https://www.britishhorrorstudio.com/

title: SEX AND FURY
description:
Ocho Inoshika has the men who killed her father in her sights. A pickpocket, gambler and swordswoman moving through Meiji-era Tokyo, she finds her revenge tangled with yakuza interests, corrupt politicians and a British spy.
Reiko Ike commands Norifumi Suzuki’s pinky-violence landmark with an extraordinary combination of stillness and explosive force. Christina Lindberg adds another volatile presence to its political intrigue and pop-art spectacle. Snow, tattoos, blades and delirious colour turn a revenge story into a film whose visual audacity refuses to stay within any single genre.

title: ZORN III
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN III (2018-2022) 2022, 82 min, DCP. With John Zorn and Barbara Hannigan. “Why can’t Mathieu Amalric stop filming John Zorn? It’s because consciously or unconsciously, he understands that he can only get closer to this man if he imitates his restlessness. It’s this Sisyphean tirelessness, the fact that we must imagine Zorn (whose surname translates into German as anger) as a happy man, which is at the core of his art. He makes music in order to be alive. This time, however, Zorn is not the only protagonist, as the Canadian soprano Barbara Hannigan enters the wild world of the composer. Much more straightforward than its previous iterations, the film captures Hannigan’s rehearsals for a performance of Zorn’s song cycle ‘Jumalattaret’ together with pianist Stephen Gosling. The work pushes her vocal capacities to the limit, with the sudden shifts in register, extended high notes and bird-like chirping demanding everything from her.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE

title: The Colour of Pomegranates [Sayat Nova]
description: Sergei Parajanov's celebrated masterpiece paints an astonishing portrait of the 18th century Armenian poet Sayat Nova, the 'King of Song'. Parajanov's aim was not a conventional biography but a cinematic expression of his work, resulting in an extraordinary visual poem. Key moments in his subject's life are illustrated through a series of exquisitely orchestrated tableaux filled with rich colour and stunning iconography, each scene a celluloid painting alive with stylised movement.

title: The Warriors
description: A turf battle between New York City street gangs that rages from Coney Island to the Bronx. The Warriors are mistakenly fingered for the killing of a gang leader. Soon they have every gang in the city out to get revenge and they must make their way across the city to their own turf.

title: Bitter Christmas

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: Escape from New York
description: In 1997, a major war between the United States and the Soviet Union is concluding, and the entire island of Manhattan has been converted into a giant maximum security prison. When Air Force One is hijacked and crashes into the island, the president (Donald Pleasence) is taken hostage by a group of inmates. Snake Plissken (Kurt Russell), a former Special Forces soldier turned criminal, is recruited to retrieve the president in exchange for his own freedom.

title: Bitter Christmas

title: Before Sunrise
description: On his way to Vienna, American Jesse (Ethan Hawke) meets Celine (Julie Delpy), a student returning to Paris. After long conversations forge a surprising connection between them, Jesse convinces Celine to get off the train with him in Vienna. Since his flight to the U.S. departs the next morning and he has no money for lodging, they wander the city together, taking in the experiences of Vienna and each other. As the night progresses, their bond makes separating in the morning a difficult choice.

title: Who Can Kill a Child?
description: Tom and Evelyn (Lewis Fiander and Prunella Ransome), a young couple from England, plan an idyllic getaway to a remote Spanish island, in anticipation of the birth of their third child. When they arrive, they find their destination almost entirely deserted, with the exception of a number of children, all of whom are acting strangely. When the couple begin to find evidence of a number of atrocities on the island, they quickly find themselves embroiled in a terrifying battle for survival, as well as being forced to confront a previously unthinkable question… Directed by Narciso Ibáñez Serrador (El televisor, The House That Screamed), the legendary master of horror dubbed the ‘Spanish Hitchcock’, Who Can Kill A Child? is his undisputed masterpiece, an extreme and unbearably tense work that remains deeply shocking in its disregard for societal taboos. With a cult reputation that has continued to grow among genre aficionados since its release in 1976, Who Can Kill A Child? is now considered not just as a landmark work of Euro-horror, but as one of the greatest horror films ever made (Slant Magazine). Content warning: Please be aware that this version of the film contains a restored eight-minute documentary prologue composed of real archival footage of children suffering in global conflicts including The Holocaust, The Vietnam War and the Nigerian Civil War. The filmmakers included it to underline how adults have historically used and harmed children as helpless victims of conflict, but the use of real-life tragedies has proved controversial and disturbing for audiences. Presented from a brand-new 4K restoration of the film courtesy of Radiance Films.

title: An Unfinished Film
description: ★★★★★ “An utterly unique and very important movie about Covid, the crisis that affected all of us.” – The Guardian Director Xiaorui convinces his cast and crew to resume the shooting of a film halted ten years earlier. In January 2020, with the shoot almost complete, rumours regarding an illness begin to circulate. A hairdresser from Wuhan is sent home, while the crew follows the news on their phones. The director has to decide whether to halt the filming once again. Some of the crew and actors manage to leave before the hotel is locked down by security guards and everyone left on set is confined to their hotel rooms. As all communication is reduced to phone screens, Wuhan is locked down. The crew continues to communicate via video calls, whilst the quarantined main actor Jiang Cheng struggles to support his wife who is now locked-down with their month-old baby in Beijing.

title: LA PRISONNIÉRE
description:
A gallery owner’s private photographs draw a young woman into a world where looking is never innocent. Fascination becomes an experiment in control, and the distance between observer and captive grows dangerously small.
Henri-Georges Clouzot’s final film trades the monochrome menace of DIABOLIQUE for optical art, saturated colour and fractured reflections. The images are seductive precisely because they are traps. A feverish study of voyeurism and obsession from a master of suspense discovering new ways to make the act of seeing feel unstable.

title: DORSKY & HILER, PGM 2: JEROME HILER
description: CARELESS PASSAGE 2024, 20 min, 16mm, silent “More than ever, origins have been on my mind. In the case of CARELESS PASSAGE, the origins of sight. Particularly, how, after millions of years, our ancestors developed that bubble-like globe that allowed them to see the world. Subsequently, I found that, before this liquid-filled sphere developed, a form of sight existed whereby a small ‘pinhole’ on the surface of an organism allowed a bit of light in to reflect on an interior surface. I had the delightful realization that ‘cinema’ preceded eyesight itself. (I knew it all along). My film, as usual, is a walk around town but haunted by surrogate shapes of ‘bubbles,’ ‘eyes’ and soupy things in emergence. Squares, those uniquely human shapes enter as well and try to find their place in a slippery world.” –Jerome Hiler WORDS OF MERCURY 2011, 25 min, 16mm, silent “WORDS OF MERCURY is my loving farewell to color reversal 16mm film. The Bolex camera, which has served me so well for over fifty years, became a container for a process of distillation. I wanted to extract as much as I could from my remaining rolls of Ektachrome 7285. Film emulsion is so rich with latent colors and images, it was a simple decision to make a film of superimpositions which were all shot in the camera. […] The film takes a journey from darkness and a bare world through the seasonal spreading of seeds to a place almost choked and repugnant with color – a place that invites death. The final couplet from Shakespeare’s ‘Love’s Labour’s Lost’ speaking of the place of death, supplies me with my title. I seem to make the same film again and again in different ways.” –Jerome Hiler NEW SHORES 1971-87/2014, 35 min, 16mm, silent “Like [IN THE STONE HOUSE], NEW SHORES consists of earlier footage edited in recent years. It could be seen as a sequel to IN THE STONE HOUSE especially since it begins with a cross-country journey to the West Coast, where I settled, and concludes with a visit, in 1987, to the ‘stone house’ in rural New Jersey. Even though there is some sort of time line that can be imagined, the film stands on its own. It is simply a series of episodes that touch upon facets of living in a new area with new weather, new people, new identities and stubborn old fears.” –Jerome Hiler Total running time: ca. 85 min.

title: DEVO: RESTORATIONS AND REVELATIONS
description: COLLECTED FILM AND VIDEO WORKS 1976-84 PRESENTED BY FILM RESTORATIONIST PETER CONHEIM Formed in the wreckage of the Kent State shootings in 1973, where co-founders Gerald V. Casale and Mark Mothersbaugh were students during the massacre, and still blowing the horn five decades later, Akron’s DEVO would take their subversive pop-art to staggering mainstream success. All the while, they considered themselves to be filmmakers as much as they were a “band.” From their first film onward (1976’s THE BEGINNING WAS THE END: THE TRUTH ABOUT DE-EVOLUTION), they fused their love of Dadaist image-making with their constantly shapeshifting music, confounding their record label by plowing their meager promo budgets into companion films for songs. This program unveils painstaking new restorations and reconstructions of much of this pivotal work (including SATISFACTION, FREEDOM OF CHOICE, WHIP IT, and much more) alongside a host of rarely (and never)-seen live footage, encounters with hapless interviewers, and other spud ephemera, curated specially for Anthology Film Archives by film archivist and musician Peter Conheim (Mono Pause, ex-Negativland, Wet Gate, et al). Total running time: ca. 80 min + discussion and Q&A.

title: Kingdom of Heaven: Director's Cut
description: Ridley Scott's extended cut of an epic adventure about a common man who finds himself thrust into a decades-long war. Orlando Bloom plays a humble blacksmith who discovers that he is the son of a knght, and travels to the Holy Land to fight in the crusades. A stranger in a strange land, he serves a doomed King, falls in love with an exotic and forbidden Queen, and rises to knighthood. Ultimately, he must protect the people of Jerusalem from overwhelming forces, while striving to keep a fragile peace.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: THE TELEPHONE BOOK
description:
Alice receives an obscene phone call so extraordinary that she falls in love with the caller. Finding him means crossing a New York populated by voyeurs, fantasists and people with rather specialised ideas about communication.
Nelson Lyon’s lost countercultural comedy makes sexploitation collide with pop art, media satire and underground filmmaking. Stark monochrome photography and a restless parade of eccentrics turn the romantic quest into something wonderfully unstable. Dirty jokes become questions about loneliness and images, with the city itself answering back in the wrong voice.

title: The Third Man
description: Set in postwar Vienna, Austria, "The Third Man" stars Joseph Cotten as Holly Martins, a writer of pulp Westerns, who arrives penniless as a guest of his childhood chum Harry Lime (Orson Welles), only to find him dead. Martins develops a conspiracy theory after learning of a "third man" present at the time of Harry's death, running into interference from British officer Maj. Calloway (Trevor Howard) and falling head-over-heels for Harry's grief-stricken lover, Anna (Alida Valli).

title: No Country For Old Men
description: While out hunting, Llewelyn Moss (Josh Brolin) finds the grisly aftermath of a drug deal. Though he knows better, he cannot resist the cash left behind and takes it with him. The hunter becomes the hunted when a merciless killer named Chigurh (Javier Bardem) picks up his trail. Also looking for Moss is Sheriff Bell (Tommy Lee Jones), an aging lawman who reflects on a changing world and a dark secret of his own, as he tries to find and protect Moss.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: The Big Lebowski
description: Jeff "The Dude" Lebowski, mistaken for a millionaire of the same name, seeks restitution for his ruined rug and enlists his bowling buddies to help get it.

title: Daisies (Sedmikrásky)
description: After realizing that all world is spoiled, Marie and Marie are committed to be spoiled themselves. They rip off older men, feast in lavish meals and do all kinds of mischief. But what is all this leading to?

title: WANDA
description:
Wanda gives up custody of her children and drifts through Pennsylvania’s coal country with no plan that will survive the day. A petty criminal offers her a place beside him, but belonging comes with another set of orders.
Barbara Loden wrote, directed and stars in this extraordinary independent film, finding immense emotional force in pauses, uncertain gestures and shabby rooms. The camera grants attention to a woman other stories would hurry past. Unsentimental and profoundly humane, WANDA asks what freedom can mean when almost every available choice belongs to somebody else.

title: DORSKY & HILER, PGM 3: NATHANIEL DORSKY’S ‘ARBORETUM CYCLE’
description: “For the past several years California experienced an extreme drought. But this past winter good fortune brought a bountiful amount of storms and liquid refreshment. The spring that followed took on magical and celebratory qualities of energy, joy, fullness, and rebirth. In walking distance from my apartment is San Francisco’s Arboretum located in Golden Gate Park. I decided that I would make a film now on a single subject and that subject would be the light – not the objects, but the sacredness of the light itself in this splendid garden. What I did not know is that the great beauty of this magnificent spring would bring forth not one, but seven films, each one immediately following the previous. I began to photograph on the second week of February and finished the editing of the seventh film during the last days of December. These seven films spontaneously manifested as the stages of life: early childhood, youth, maturity, old age, and death. ELOHIM was photographed in early spring, the week of the lunar new year, the very spirit of creation. ABATON was photographed a few weeks later in the full ripeness of spring, the very purity and intoxication of passion. CODA was photographed in late spring, in the aftermath of this purity, the first shades of mortality and knowledge. ODE, photographed in early summer, is a soft textured song of the fallen, the dissonant reds of death, seeds, and rebirth. SEPTEMBER is indeed, Indian summer, the halcyon swan song of earthly blessings. MONODY, shot in the fading autumnal glory is an energized declaration of the end. And EPILOGUE, photographed in early December, rests in quietude, the garden’s energy now descending into the dark, damp earth.” –Nathaniel Dorsky, 2017 ELOHIM (2017, 31 min, 16mm, silent) ABATON (2017, 19 min, 16mm, silent) CODA (2017, 16 min, 16mm, silent) ODE (2017, 20 min, 16mm, silent) SEPTEMBER (2017, 20 min, 16mm, silent) MONODY (2017, 16 min, 16mm, silent) EPILOGUE (2017, 15 min, 16mm, silent) Total running time: ca. 140 min.

title: OCA
description: NEW YORK PREMIERE! Winner of the Silver Hugo Award in the New Directors Competition at the Chicago International Film Festival, this atmospheric and mystical debut feature by Karla Badillo tells the story of Rafaela, a young nun from a dwindling congregation who embarks on a pilgrimage after the arrival of a new archbishop. Along the way, she encounters travelers from diverse walks of life, and her journey becomes a lyrical and often poignant meditation on faith, doubt, and resilience in a world shaped by both spiritual and material forces. Featuring a stellar ensemble cast of professional actors – including Natalia Solián (HUESERA: THE BONE WOMAN), Cecilia Suárez (THE HOUSE OF FLOWERS), and Raúl Briones (LA COCINA) – alongside non-professional performers, the film offers a quietly critical lens on devotion and institutional life, reimagining the spiritual cinema of Luis Buñuel through a contemporary, distinctly female perspective, and tracing the winding path between belief, destiny, and self-discovery.

title: Tampopo
description: We’re serving up the ultimate cinematic feast, Juzo Itami’s delectable “ramen western,” just in time for feasting season!  After the death of her husband, the widow of the proprietor of a noodle shop must rely on a cabal of gastronomes to help her find the perfect recipe. Deliciously funny, sexy and surreal, this hilarious satire satisfies down to the soul. Get ready to devour this treasure of Japanese and culinary cinema in its new 4K restoration on our big delicious screen! And come hungry, our concessions stand will have delicious ramen to slurp during the film!

title: Music Video Preservation Society with special guest Tim Pope
description: We are delighted to announce a very exciting edition of Music Video Preservation Society at the Prince Charles Cinema - with one of the most brilliant music video directors of all time: the one and only Tim Pope. Tim is among the most significant figures in the history of music videos, a pioneer in establishing its potential as an artform. He directed videos of boundless imagination, spirit and wit in service of the musicians and music he loves. And what a list of artists he’s worked with. From blagging his way into the just-emerging music video industry to direct promos for Soft Cell in the early 80s he blazed a trail with the likes of David Bowie, The The, Neil Young, Queen, Style Council, Talk Talk and, of course, The Cure - the band he is most closely associated with, for whom he has made by his own calculation, over 30 videos and several concert films. Tim has now written about his fascinating (and often hilarious) adventures making pop videos in the 80s, 90s and beyond - plus a nightmarish brush with Hollywood making ‘The Crow 2’ for Harvey Weinstein - in his brilliant memoir ‘I Shoot Rock Stars’, published in August and now a Sunday Times bestseller. And on November 18th, Tim is coming to The PCC to tell some stories from the book and more, in conversation with MVPS host David Knight - and he will also present a selection of his greatest music videos, now remastered back to their original glory, on the big screen. There will be classics, there will be surprises, there will be laughs, maybe a few tears... Will we be showing Tim's notorious video for Sex Dwarf? We're not saying until we have consulted our lawyers. But rest assured, this meeting of Music Video Preservation Society is going to be awesome. Tickets on sale now at the box office.

title: The Getaway
description: “Doc” McCoy (Steve McQueen) is unexpectedly freed from a lengthy prison sentence to take part in a bank robbery, but there may be no one he can trust, not even his seemingly loyal wife (Ali MacGraw). For one of his first produced screenplays, Walter Hill adapted one of noir master Jim Thompson’s darkest novels into a more light-hearted but still cynical romantic thriller, with director Sam Peckinpah staging the film’s action sequences with his usual vividness.

title: Mystery Movie
description: Don't miss our fan favourite MYSTERY MOVIE screenings! On a near weekly basis we will serve up a random mystery movie, with No Clues and No Hints as to what they will be. In 2026, we'll be presenting these as STAFF CURATED selections each and every week by our lovely Front of House, Duty Manager, and Projection Team! You can find the schedule below: --- You can find a list of every MYSTERY MOVIE we have ever screened HERE ; if a film is on this list, it is not eligible for future Mystery Movie screenings! --- Content Advice : As these films are a mystery, we aren't able to provide specific ratings / guidance on the film's content. We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: FREEWAY: CONFESSIONS OF A TRICKBABY
description:
White Girl and Cyclona break out of detention and head for Mexico, trusting a promise of sanctuary that sounds suspiciously like another trap. Their trail of bad decisions turns into a filthy, violent rewrite of HANSEL AND GRETEL.
Natasha Lyonne and María Celedonio make an explosive double act in Matthew Bright’s grotesque fugitive fairy tale, with Vincent Gallo waiting at the far end of the road. Beneath its gleefully offensive surfaces is a world that keeps turning vulnerable people into predators. An abrasive midnight movie with a very crooked grin.

title: "The Greatest Love of All Time" / THE MARGIN

title: Vertigo
description: A former San Francisco police detective juggles wrestling with his personal demons and becoming obsessed with the hauntingly beautiful woman he has been hired to trail, who may be deeply disturbed.

title: The Time Masters
description: Directed by visionary science-fiction animator René Laloux (Fantastic Planet) and designed by the legendary Jean Giraud (a.k.a. Mœbius) The Time Masters is a visually fantastic foray into existentialist space adventure. After his parents are killed on the dangerous planet Perdide, young Piel (voiced by Frédéric Legros) survives by maintaining radio contact with Jaffar (Jean Valmont), a pilot transporting the exiled Prince Matton (Yves-Marie Maurin) and Princess Belle (Monique Thierry) from their former kingdom. Jaffar seeks the help of Silbad (Michel Elias), a cheerful old-timer who knows how to circumvent Perdide’s hazards, including brain-devouring insects and watery graves. Along the way, Jaffar and company encounter a pair of impish homunculi stowaways, identity-less angels controlled by an amorphous hive mind, and the Masters of Time, mysterious beings who can bend reality and perhaps reveal to the heroes their secret origins and destinies. Restored in 4K in 2023 at the initiative of CITE FILMS in collaboration with the Fondazione Cineteca di Bologna and with the support of the CNC

title: Bitter Christmas
description: The incomparable Pedro Almodóvar explores the artist’s tenuous relationship with fiction and reality in this film about an actress writing a script inspired by the lives of those around her—which is itself the invention of an Almodóvar-like filmmaker.

title: The Piano
description: In the mid-19th century a mute woman is sent to New Zealand along with her young daughter and prized piano for an arranged marriage to a farmer, but is soon lusted after by a farm worker.

title: Whisper of the Heart
description: Discover the brilliance of this heartwarming coming-of-age classic from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of My Neighbour Totoro and the Academy Award®-winning Spirited Away. A chance encounter with a mysterious cat sends Shizuku, a girl with her head in the clouds, on a quest for her true talent. Together with Seiji, a boy determined to follow his dreams, and enchanted by The Baron, an antique cat figurine who guides her to listen to the whispers of her heart, Shizuku embarks on a life-changing adventure that takes her beyond the boundaries of her imagination. Based on a screenplay and storyboards from Hayao Miyazaki, WHISPER OF THE HEART is a precious gem in the Studio Ghibli catalogue, directed by veteran animator Yoshifumi Kondo.

title: An Unfinished Film
description: ★★★★★ “An utterly unique and very important movie about Covid, the crisis that affected all of us.” – The Guardian Director Xiaorui convinces his cast and crew to resume the shooting of a film halted ten years earlier. In January 2020, with the shoot almost complete, rumours regarding an illness begin to circulate. A hairdresser from Wuhan is sent home, while the crew follows the news on their phones. The director has to decide whether to halt the filming once again. Some of the crew and actors manage to leave before the hotel is locked down by security guards and everyone left on set is confined to their hotel rooms. As all communication is reduced to phone screens, Wuhan is locked down. The crew continues to communicate via video calls, whilst the quarantined main actor Jiang Cheng struggles to support his wife who is now locked-down with their month-old baby in Beijing.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Byzantium
description: “We are a brotherhood. There are no women amongst us” Hunted for two centuries, Clara and Eleanor Webb are the only female vampires alive: a mother who feeds on human blood and will go to any lengths to survive, and her daughter who despises what she is and tries to live a moral life. Forced to find refuge in a run-down coastal hotel, they realise that they can not hide forever; not when their past and secrets are coming back to haunt them. Blood waterfalls, razor-sharp claws and cults of knowledge; from the director of Interview with the Vampire (1994), Byzantium is deliciously gothic, seductively atmospheric, and inescapably tragic. A must-watch title in the vampire genre, Neil Jordan depicts vampire lore in a contemporary way while staying true to its archaic themes. Byzantium is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: THE HAUNTED MOUSTACHE + Q&A
description:
After inheriting a century-old moustache from an eccentric great-aunt, David Bramwell follows the trail of its former owner through séances, spiritualist churches, Brighton basement clubs and an increasingly strange occult odyssey.
Blending filmed monologue, memoir and psychedelic folklore, this funny and affecting modern fireside tale won a Special Mention Audience Award at CINECITY 2025. The screening is followed by an on-stage Q&A.

title: CINEMATIC CORRESPONDENCES: THERESA HAK KYUNG CHA AND HER FILMIC INFLUENCES
description: This special screening is presented in conjunction with “Theresa Hak Kyung Cha: Multiple Offerings”, a retrospective on view at Artists Space through November 21. The program features cinematic works by artists and filmmakers represented in “Apparatus, Cinematographic Apparatus: Selected Writing”, a seminal volume edited by Theresa Hak Kyung Cha (1951-82) and published in the 1980s by Tanam Press, an independent, artist-led publishing entity. Alongside these films will be a few examples of Cha’s work from the mid-1970s, including her notable structuralist piece PERMUTATIONS, a 1976 work composed of six shots filmed at one-second intervals that examines what the artist calls, “Film Time and Film Space.” The artist’s sister appears in a frame that echoes the format of a passport photo; Cha herself appears once. Through the repetition and permutation of these images, the sequence creates a rhythmic flicker, generating an optical sense of movement. Cha was deeply influenced by both canonical and contemporary films from around the world, and by cinema theory, and actively explored the distinctions between the film, its author, and the spectator. Among the filmmakers whose work illuminates these concerns is Dziga Vertov, whose 1929 film MAN WITH A MOVIE CAMERA offers a radical exploration of cinematic perception and the possibilities of the medium, using dynamic editing, multiple exposures, split screens, and self-reflexive images of the camera and filmmaking process. Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet’s 1977 film EVERY REVOLUTION IS A THROW OF THE DICE brings together Stéphane Mallarmé’s poem “A Throw of the Dice Will Never Abolish Chance” with a collective recitation staged at Père-Lachaise Cemetery, beside the wall where the last defenders of the Paris Commune were executed in 1871. The film’s interweaving of literary text, historical memory, and the material conditions of its own performance resonates with Cha’s sustained interest in the relationship between language, image, and the conditions of viewing. Taken together, the program brings into view the formal, literary, and cinematic correspondences that run through Cha’s work. Co-presented by Anthology Film Archives and Artists Space, with an introduction by a special guest. For more info about the Artists Space exhibition visit: https://artistsspace.org/exhibitions/theresa-hak-kyung-cha-multiple-offerings Dziga Vertov MAN WITH A MOVIE CAMERA / CHELOVEK S KINO-APPARATOM 1929, 90 min, 35mm, silent. With no intertitles. Preceded by: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha PERMUTATIONS (1976, 10 min, 16mm) Theresa Hak Kyung Cha TRANSLATIONS FROM A WILLOW TREE (1976, 4 min, Super-8mm-to-DCP) Jean-Marie Straub & Danièle Huillet EVERY REVOLUTION IS A THROW OF THE DICE / TOUTE RÉVOLUTION EST UN COUP DE DÉS (1977, 11 min, 35mm) Total running time: ca. 120 min.

title: Ten Years of Monkey Tennis (with Peter Serafinowicz)
description: “One of the best TV and film podcasts” – The Telegraph “What’s the best thing?” It’s a question for our times. It’s the question of our lives. And it’s one of Alan Partridge’s best-known phone-in topics. Finally, as part of their 10-year birthday celebrations, the hosts of Monkey Tennis (the award-winning, chart-topping Alan Partridge fan podcast) will tackle it live, armed with only four microphones and a live audience. Join them as they pit elements of the APU (Alan Partridge Universe) against each other to determine, once and for all, the answer to Alan’s largest question: “What’s the Best Thing?” Will it be 'Alpha Papa’ or Sidekick Simon, a shop-soiled chocolate orange or a can of Sprünt, Flench and Sons Tanning or Bangkok Chick Boys? Afterwards, they’ll also be speaking to star of I’m Alan Partridge (as well as Guardians of the Galaxy , Amandaland , Parks & Recreation , Shaun of the Dead , Spaced and 100+ more), Peter Serafinowicz, about his epic career and his time as Alan’s antagonist and lover of American things, Tex. In the meantime, catch up on over 150 episodes of the Monkey Tennis podcast, covering almost everything Alan's ever done, at podfollow.com/monkeytennis

title: EROTIC WITCHCRAFT
description:
Raised by a magician, a young man inherits a duty stranger than any ordinary family legacy: guarding La Goulve, the Daughter of the Golem. When occult power meets his desires, the boundary between the everyday and the supernatural begins to give way.
Mario Mercier and Bepi Fontana’s elusive French fantasy is a discovery from the wilder edges of seventies occult cinema. Sorcery, desire and the Golem legend make an unusual combination, promising a detour from familiar vampire and witchcraft stories into a much less mapped corner of the fantastic.

title: Minotaur
description: Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes, Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev’s riveting, razor-sharp tale of personal, patriarchal, and governmental corruption follows a wealthy CEO who begins to suspect his wife is having an extramarital affair. France’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Crash (1996)
description: Technology and sexuality meet in a head-on collision in David Cronenberg's controversial adaptation of writer J.G. Ballard's hugely transgressive 1973 novel, starring James Spader and Holly Hunter. Spader stars as James Ballard, a film producer whose deviant sexual desires are awakened by a near-fatal automobile accident with Dr. Helen Remington (Hunter). Soon, the pair, alongside Ballard's wife Catherine (Deborah Kara Unger), are drawn into an underground world of car crash fetishism presided over by renegade scientist Vaughan (Elias Koteas). Danger, sex and death become entwined as eroticism and technology join together in a disturbing, deadly union.

title: A Streetcar Named Desire
description: Based on the play by Tennessee Williams, this renowned drama follows troubled former schoolteacher Blanche DuBois (Vivien Leigh) as she leaves small-town Mississippi and moves in with her sister, Stella Kowalski (Kim Hunter), and her husband, Stanley (Marlon Brando), in New Orleans. Blanche's flirtatious Southern-belle presence causes problems for Stella and Stanley, who already have a volatile relationship, leading to even greater conflict in the Kowalski household.

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.
