title: Solve Along A Murder She Wrote
description: Cult hit event Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote returns to the Prince Charles Cinema with an interactive screening of a classic Murder, She Wrote episode. Watch as Cabot Cove gets caught up in a murder mystery only JB Fletcher (or you!) can solve! Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. See the show Time Out rated one of 2021 and 2019’s 50 Great Nights Out in London that has played to sell-out audiences across the UK and Australia. Hosted by super-fan Tim Benzie, Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote features: * A race to solve to the crime, via the Fameometer and the Suspiciometer! * A Cabot Cove quiz! * A singalong to the theme tune with new lyrics! * Clips and biogs of the campy guest stars! Tim Benzie is obsessed with Murder, She Wrote, having watched the original series when it was first broadcast, and now relishing the repeats on television everywhere. Tim is the writer/performer of “It’s a Mystery!”, all about our love of whodunnits. An award-winning playwright and co-writer of the Royal Vauxhall Tavern’s 2017-2023 pantos (‘Goosed’, ‘Rubbed’, ‘Slipped’, ‘Pricked’, ‘Cracked’ and ‘Tossed’). He is the co-producer of the camp club night PopHorror. Visit us at www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com , or follow us on Instagram, Twitter and Facebook @solvealonga. 2026 SCHEDULE: Tuesday 8th September 2026 "Dead Man's Gold" Directed by Seymour Robbie Starring Angela Lansbury, Leslie Nielsen, Tom Bosley 1986 | 120mins | USA Thursday 22nd October 2026 Encore Halloween special - "The Witch's Curse" Directed by Jerry Jameson Starring Angela Lansbury, Robert Vaughn, Mary Crosby 1992 | 120mins | USA Thursday 26th November 2026 New episode TBC Thursday 17th December 2026 Encore screening - "A Christmas Secret" Directed by Anthony Pullen Shaw Starring Angela Lansbury, Larry Wilcox, Amy Brenneman 1992 | 120mins | USA *** The Critics speak! “You’ll be swept away with Jessica Fletcher feels … it has the BEST HOST.” - Time Out London "A cinematic, theatrical and hilarious experience ... Before the night I had never seen an episode of Murder, She Wrote before, unlike some dedicated fans who had even dressed up. However, this really was an evening everyone could enjoy.” - Nottingham Post "As soon as I saw it was on at the [Edinburgh] Fringe I elbowed my way through the other BW reviewers, pushed a couple of them over … just so I could get to the front of the queue and see this show again. And it did not disappoint ... I'd go again in a heartbeat.” 5 stars ***** - Broadway World "The self-confessed super-fan and award-winning playwright will lead you into a silly whirlwind of nostalgic giggle, using his wealth of camp trivia and sound logic to solve these killings.” 5 stars ***** - One4Review "Benzie knows how to put on a great show ... I would happily see it again, with all the fervour of the ‘Jessica Fletcher eating popcorn’ meme." 5 stars ***** - Everything Theatre “Whodunnit? Tim dunnit – and he did it so well I can’t wait for the next one!" 5 stars ***** - Fairy-Powered Productions “I’d challenge anyone to sit through this show and not get utterly invested in figuring out whodunit.” 4 stars **** - West End Wilma “This is a highly entertaining production even if you have never seen an episode, filled with outrageous fun." 4 stars **** - British Theatre Guide "For a funny, campy evening, there is little that could beat Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote’s unique qualities and Benzie’s wit and charm. Personally this reviewer can’t wait to revisit Cabot Cove. Never mind 'whodunnit', more like 'yougottadoit!" 4 stars **** - The Reviews Hub “A lighthearted two hours of entertainment that both die-hard devotees and Cabot Cove novices will enjoy ... A solve-along, sing-along hit." 4 stars **** - Broadway Baby “Benzie's passion and knowledge shines through." 4 stars **** - West End Best Friend "Tim Benzie is the perfect host ... Benzie’s insights help keep the audience engaged with the show and not just passively watching the episode unfold.” 4 stars **** - The Nerd Party “It didn’t take long for Benzie to have the audience in stitches and he had the whole crowd in the palm of his hand the entire evening.” - Bristol 24/7 “A unique and thoroughly enjoyable theatre experience” - Blue Curtains Brisbane *** For links to the full reviews visit www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com

title: SMOOTH TALK
description:
For Connie, summer means music, shopping trips and practising the person she wants to become. Then an older stranger pulls up outside her house while she is alone, and ordinary flirtation begins turning into something she cannot easily name—or escape.
Laura Dern and Treat Williams are extraordinary in Joyce Chopra’s adaptation of Joyce Carol Oates. Sunlit teenage restlessness gives way to a confrontation whose menace grows almost imperceptibly. The film understands the thrill of being seen and the terror of being claimed, making its shift from coming-of-age drama to psychological nightmare devastating.

title: Planes, Trains & Automobiles
description: Easily excitable Neal Page (Steve Martin) is somewhat of a control freak. Trying to get home to Chicago to spend Thanksgiving with his wife (Laila Robins) and kids, his flight is rerouted to a distant city in Kansas because of a freak snowstorm, and his sanity begins to fray. Worse yet, he is forced to bunk up with talkative Del Griffith (John Candy), whom he finds extremely annoying. Together they must overcome the insanity of holiday travel to reach their intended destination.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: A Confucian Confusion
description: Art versus commerce, friendship versus status, independence versus conformity—values clash and collide in Edward Yang's study of an increasingly Westernized country heading into the twenty-first century without moral guideposts. Moving from breakout hit A Brighter Summer Day's investigation of the past to a critical survey of the present, A Confucian Confusion charts the tangled web of emotional and professional manipulations among a group of young urbanites. At its center is Molly (Ni Shu-chun), director of a floundering public-relations firm. Alienated by the childish fiancé (Bosen Wang) who bankrolls her enterprise—and frustrated by the demands of an assistant, Qiqi (Chen Shiang-chyi), and her own fiancé, Ming (Wang Wei-ming)—Molly lashes out at everyone in her path and threatens to dismantle the company altogether. Meanwhile (amid several other subplots), Molly's talk-show-host sister (Chen Li-mei) attempts to dissuade her separated husband from continuing to write a dark novel about the return of Confucius to a jaded modern society. Injecting comedic elements into his patented brand of earnest soul-searching, Yang finds humor as well as pathos in the desperate behavior of a lost and lonely generation.

title: Singin’ in the Rain
description: Arguably the greatest movie musical ever made, and considered by many  to be one of the greatest films of all time, Singin’ in the Rain remains a singular masterpiece of music, comedy, romance, and dance, set against a breathtaking Technicolor backdrop of imagination and artistry. Gene Kelly and Debbie Reynolds electrify the screen in back-to-back legendary musical numbers. Jean Hagen delights as the perfectly hilarious villain. The entrancing Cyd Charisse shows off her spectacular moves in a dazzling pas de deux with Kelly. It’s an inspiring, entertaining, stunning, and remarkable work of cinematic majesty.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: North by Northwest
description: The ultimate Hitchcock thrill ride, centered on the Master of Suspense’s favorite theme: an innocent man accused of a crime he didn’t commit. Here, the poor sucker is an effortlessly cool Cary Grant (or is that redundant?), playing an advertising exec who’s mistaken for a spy named George Kaplan — and then mistaken for a murderer! His efforts to clear his own name and unravel a sinister conspiracy will take across the United States, from an epic train ride to an assassination attempt by airplane to a chase across Mount Rushmore. But hey, he does get to romance Eva Marie Saint along the way, so maybe it’s all worth it?

title: THE HEARTBREAK KID
description:
Lenny is three days into his honeymoon when he spots the woman he thinks he should have married. The bride is upstairs with sunburn. He is downstairs selling himself a completely different future.
Elaine May makes romantic self-delusion almost unbearably funny. Charles Grodin turns every conversation into a sales pitch, while Jeannie Berlin gives the discarded Lila a presence the film refuses to let him wish away. A romantic comedy with surgical instincts, exposing the monstrous entitlement hidden inside one ordinary man’s idea of the perfect match.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: Unzipped
description: Designer Isaac Mizrahi proved a force of nature on the road to his legendary fall 1994 collection, a career-defining triumph that was documented with an effervescent intimacy by Douglas Keeve, Mizrahi’s then-partner. Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait—sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock—transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs. Digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. Funding provided by Isaac Mizrahi Entertainment. Laboratory services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Media Audio Services.

title: LIAF: Open Night: Elizabeth Hobbs: History, Heresy & Hyenas (15*)
ANDY WARHOL’S 'SCREEN TESTS' + CONRAD VENTUR’S 'SCREEN TESTS REVISITED', PGM 1
description: These two programs pair Warhol’s seminal and often exquisite SCREEN TESTS – the silent, black-and-white, three-and-a-half minute filmic portraits he made between 1964-66, which grew to encompass 472 separate reels, portraying 189 individual subjects (many of them sitting for multiple portraits) – with Conrad Ventur’s 21st-century remakes. For Ventur’s (ongoing) project, he has sought out as many of the surviving SCREEN TESTees as possible, and restaged their portraits, resulting in a poetic tribute to Warhol’s films and to the transformations wrought by time. Conrad Ventur in person on Sat, Nov 21!

title: NAKED LUNCH
description:
The bug powder is addictive. The typewriter is alive. And Bill Lee’s latest assignment may be coming from an insect intelligence service. Fleeing into the Interzone, he tries to write a report from a reality that will not stay still.
David Cronenberg fuses William S. Burroughs’s fiction and biography into a wonderfully deadpan nightmare of addiction and authorship. Peter Weller plays the impossible with perfect weary conviction, while grotesque organic machines make language horribly physical. A literary adaptation that succeeds by becoming its own mutant creature.

title: Desperately Seeking Susan
description: Susan Seidelman’s stylish New York fairy tale features an effervescent young Madonna in her first film role. Rosanna Arquette stars as Roberta, a bored suburban housewife who is fascinated with a mystery woman, Susan, played by Madonna. When she spots an ad meant for Susan in the personals, Roberta goes to the rendezvous too, and in a series of events involving amnesia and mistaken identity, she steps out of her own sterile existence and into the danger and romance of Susan’s life. With incredible 80s style, two iconic leads, and laughs, intrigue, and tons of fun to boot, we’ve got your Black Friday covered!

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: Sing-A-Long-A Rocky Horror Picture Show
description: The Campest Cult Classic of all time gets the Singalonga treatment it’s been SCREAMING for! Featuring the film, starring Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon, Meatloaf and Richard O’Brien, it’s the most outrageous, riotous, kitsch, wonderful romp ever. If you’ve done The Time Warp before, you’ll never have done it quite like this! The evening begins with your host leading a vocal warm-up before they show you how to use your free interactive props bag. Fancy dress is not obligatory but highly recommended! Please Note : The 15 rating we have placed upon this screening is due to the Adult content of the hosted pre-show which may not be suitable for those under 15. Please Note : This is a screening of the movie not a live stage show. Also this screening may contain sudden loud noises and flashing lights. For Sing-a-long-a Grease, Rocky Horror, Dirty Dancing and The Greatest Showman at the Prince Charles Cinema, London we can offer a discount for groups of 10+. Simply get in touch with us via email at [email protected] before buying so we can arrange!

title: ANDY WARHOL’S 'SCREEN TESTS' + CONRAD VENTUR’S 'SCREEN TESTS REVISITED', PGM 2
description: These two programs pair Warhol’s seminal and often exquisite SCREEN TESTS – the silent, black-and-white, three-and-a-half minute filmic portraits he made between 1964-66, which grew to encompass 472 separate reels, portraying 189 individual subjects (many of them sitting for multiple portraits) – with Conrad Ventur’s 21st-century remakes. For Ventur’s (ongoing) project, he has sought out as many of the surviving SCREEN TESTees as possible, and restaged their portraits, resulting in a poetic tribute to Warhol’s films and to the transformations wrought by time. Conrad Ventur in person on Sat, Nov 22!

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Take a seat without knowing what is coming. Our mystery screenings explore the bold, disreputable and gloriously unclassifiable world of psychotronic cinema: discoveries that make you wonder how they were made, who they were made for, and why nobody showed you sooner.
The title stays secret until showtime. Curiosity is essential; good taste is negotiable.
Strictly for adult audiences. Films may contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: Enter the Dragon
description: Bruce Lee kicks all the ass in the ultimate martial arts action masterpiece, Enter the Dragon . A martial artist with a bone to pick, Lee vows to take down a reclusive crime lord by beating him in his own Kung Fu tournament. With remarkable combat choreography by Bruce Lee himself, this is one action-packed classic that never gets old and one of the greatest action movies ever made!

title: Category H: MALATESTA’S CARNIVAL OF BLOOD + FINAL DESTINATION 3
description: The smell of doughnuts and candyfloss, vomiting on the waltzers and rides that probably haven’t passed any kind of safety test - don’t we all have fond memories of the fun fair? At Category H Film Club, we’re bringing the terror of the fairground Rio’s screen two with a late night double bill of MAL...

title: FFC: Chilly Pics Shorts Programme (U*)
description: Come along for a morning of wintry wonderlands in this short film programme curated especially for Family Film Club audiences.

title: Jurassic Park
description: In Steven Spielberg's massive blockbuster, paleontologists Alan Grant (Sam Neill) and Ellie Sattler (Laura Dern) and mathematician Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) are among a select group chosen to tour an island theme park populated by dinosaurs created from prehistoric DNA. While the park's mastermind, billionaire John Hammond (Richard Attenborough), assures everyone that the facility is safe, they find out otherwise when various ferocious predators break free and go on the hunt.

title: Gremlins
description: Accessible screening On the last Saturday of every month, the museum's Family Matinee is an accessible screening where we offer open captioning, keep the theater dimly lit, and maintain a lower volume for viewers who are neurodiverse. When Billy receives a mysterious creature called a mogwai, affectionately named Gizmo, from his father for Christmas, he must follow three rules: keep it away from sunlight, don’t get it wet, and above all else, never feed it after midnight. When the creature accidentally gets wet and more mogwai spawn with much more devious intentions than the docile Gizmo, mayhem erupts. With the town’s adults out of their depth, it is up to Billy and Gizmo to defeat these menacing creatures. The violence in the PG-rated Gremlins was one of the reasons the Motion Picture Association later created the PG-13 rating; the film is often cited as kick-starting a trend of small creature features in the 1980s. Please note: This film contains discussions about Santa Claus that might not be appropriate for younger viewers.
director: Joe Dante PRODUCED BY: Michael Finnell

title: My Neighbor Totoro
description: Satsuki and Mei's mother has taken ill. In order to be closer to her while she recovers in a rural convalescent hospital, their father moves the two sisters from their home in a city to the countryside. The house they move into is a ramshackle old place in the shadow of an ancient camphor tree, and Satsuki and Mei embark on adventures with the wondrous forest spirits who live nearby.

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: The Worst Person in the World
description: On the verge of turning thirty, Julie is faced with a series of choices that force her to pursue new perspectives on her life in contemporary Oslo. Over the course of four years, she navigates love affairs and existential uncertainty as she starts deciding who she wants to become.

title: DIVA
description:
A postman secretly records the opera singer who refuses to be recorded. Another cassette contains evidence that powerful people would kill to suppress. When the two worlds collide, Paris becomes a maze of hired killers, impossible escapes and sudden romance.
Jean-Jacques Beineix makes every surface sing: blue light, wet streets, lofts and métro tunnels turn a thriller into an art-pop daydream. Opera and street culture, immaculate design and scruffy obsession exist in the same enchanted city. A defining burst of cinéma du look, made for anyone who has ever loved an image—or a voice—too much.

title: Cléo from 5 to 7
description: One of the most delightful films of the French New Wave, iconic filmmaker Agnès Varda eloquently captures Paris in the sixties with this real-time portrait of a singer set adrift in the city. A chronicle of the minutes of one woman’s life as she awaits test results of a biopsy, Cléo from 5 to 7 is a spirited mix of vivid vérité and melodrama, featuring a score by Michel Legrand and cameos by Jean-Luc Godard and Anna Karina.

title: EC: JENNINGS / KIRSANOFF
description: Humphrey Jennings LISTEN TO BRITAIN (1941, 19 min, 35mm) Jennings’s film is a masterpiece of sound mixing; it creates an audio landscape of Britain during the war, with images both accompanying and conflicting with the multitude of sounds. Dimitri Kirsanoff MÉNILMONTANT (1924-25, 38 min, 35mm, silent) “[T]o a remarkable degree, MÉNILMONTANT seems an autonomous creation, as sophisticated and demanding as any narrative film of the silent period, without obvious imitators. Although Richard Abel has astutely called attention to aspects the film shares with Abel Gance’s LA ROUE (1923) and Leon Moussinac’s LE BRASIER ARDENT (1923)…and with Jean Epstein’s COEUR FIDELE (1923)…any comparison of the film as a whole with those admirable works would have to underline the intensity, uniqueness, and exceptional rigor of Kirsanoff’s achievement.” –P. Adams Sitney, THE CINEMA OF POETRY Total running time: ca. 60 min. CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: The Mummy [1999]
description: The Mummy is a rousing, suspenseful and horrifying epic about an expedition of treasure-seeking explorers in the Sahara Desert in 1925. Stumbling upon an ancient tomb, the hunters unwittingly set loose a 3,000-year-old legacy of terror, which is embodied in the vengeful reincarnation of an Egyptian priest who had been sentenced to an eternity as one of the living dead.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: PORTRAITS OF THE ARTIST
description: Beginning with Gerard Malanga’s ANDY WARHOL (1964), in which the author of the SCREEN TESTS sits for his own extended portrait, this program finds the directors turning the camera on their fellow filmmakers, or even trading places for complementary films (as in the case of the Friedl vom Gröller and Christiana Perschon films that close the screening). Gerard Malanga ANDY WARHOL: PORTRAITS OF THE ARTIST AS A YOUNG MAN (1964, 21 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Ludwig Schönherr PORTRÄTFILM: KURT KREN (1969, 3.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP, silent) Ludwig Schönherr PORTRÄTFILM: ELISABETH ERKNER (1969, 14 min, 16mm-to-DCP, silent) Barry Gerson PORTRAIT OF ANDREW NOREN (1972, 4 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller I DON’T WANT TO BE FILMED BUT RATHER SHOOT MYSELF / ICH WILL NICHT GEFILMT WERDEN, SONDERN SELBER FILMEN (2023, 3 min, 16mm, silent) Christiana Perschon FRIEDL (2023, 2.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Friedl vom Gröller FLO UND KEN JACOBS (2001, 3 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller PETER KUBELKA UND JONAS MEKAS (1994, 2.5 min, 16mm, silent) Jeff Weber PETER (2026, 5.5 min, 35mm, silent) Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: Sonic Cinema: Daïchi Saïto
description: Sonic Cinema and the Japan Foundation present the films of Montreal-based artist Daïchi Saïto, projected from his personal 35mm prints. A rare encounter with a singular voice in artisanal film practice, this programme highlights Saïto’s skill in bridging metaphysical concepts with sensory experience. Originally from Japan, Daïchi Saïto makes films of intense beauty and power, grounded in abstract approaches to landscape, rhythm, and perception. Produced through expressive use of optical manipulation and painstaking frame-by-frame photochemical treatments, the films in this programme carry a tactile and elemental intensity, teasing out the sensual poetry of the natural world and human subjectivity. Drawing on Saïto's studies in philosophy, literature, and the languages of Hindi and Sanskrit, as much as the language of cinema, these are films built on a poetic dialogue of sound and image. Guided by the expressive improvised soundtracks of Malcolm Goldstein and Jason Sharp, we'll traverse exterior and interior landscapes, from the darkened primordial deserts of Saïto's most recent film earthearthearth (2021), through the stained glass forest of Trees of Syntax , Leaves of Axis (2009), before the torrent of memories and cool mountain vistas carries us away in Engram of Returning (2015). Daïchi will join us in person for a Q&A with series curator Oliver Dickens following the screening. Programme earthearthearth , Canada 2021, 30 min., 35mm Trees of Syntax, Leaves of Axis , Canada 2009, 10 min., 35mm Engram of Returning , Canada, Japan 2015, 18’30 min., 35mm Programmed by Oliver Dickens for Sonic Cinema, presented in partnership with the Japan Foundation.

title: LIAF: A Tribute to Phil Mulloy + Screen Talk (15*)
Twister
description: Let’s go storm-chasing, Vidiots! Helen Hunt and Bill Paxton are a bitterly divorced couple and a pair of determined climatologists out for the adventure of a lifetime in storm country as a record-breaking number of tornados threatens the lives and livelihoods of the Oklahomans in their wake. This unprecedented storm season is the perfect time to risk their lives and attempt to release “Dorothy,” a groundbreaking instrument for storm tracking, and maybe even the perfect setting to rekindle their relationship. More fun than an airborne cow, with the perfect delirious blend of thrills and schmaltz, this is one high-flying adventure that really gets off the ground — and stays there!

title: EC: THE GENERAL
description: With Buster Keaton, Marion Mack, Glen Cavendar, Jim Farley, and Joseph Keaton.“ In the funniest of all silent feature comedy classics, the imperturbable Buster Keaton is cast as a daring Federal Spy with an outlandish plan to change the course of the Civil War. This sophisticated and grotesque screen farce – eloquently touching, uproariously hilarious – is a perfect example of Keaton’s art. Engulfed by switches, stolen engines, valves, and other mechanical contrivances, the immortal comedian – an engine driver literally on the wrong side of the tracks – solemnly attempts to behave normally in a world which is plainly bewitched.” –CINEMA 16 program notes, 1958 Preceded by: Buster Keaton & Edward F. Cline NEIGHBORS (1920, 18 min, 16mm, silent) CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: FILM NO. 5 (SMILE)
description: “[S]hot with a high-speed camera…FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) reveals John Lennon’s face, recorded at 333 frames per second for an extended duration, outdoors, in color, and accompanied by a sound track of outdoor sounds recorded at the same time the imagery was recorded. FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) divides roughly into two halves, one continuous shot each. During the first half, the film is a meditation on Lennon’s face, which is so still that on first viewing I wasn’t entirely sure for a while that the film was live action and not an optically printed photograph of Lennon smiling slightly. Though almost nothing happens in any conventional sense, however, the intersection of the high speed filming and our extended gaze creates continuous, subtle transformations. […] While the second shot is more active than the first, the amount of activity remains minimal by conventional standards (and unusually so even for avant-garde film). It is as though those of us in the theater and Lennon are meditating on each other from opposite sides of the cinematic apparatus, joined together by Ono in a lovely, hypnotic stasis.” –Scott MacDonald, “Yoko Ono: Ideas on Film” Preceded by: Yoko Ono FLUXFILM NO. 16: aka NO. 4: BOTTOMS 1966, 6 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent. Camera: Jeff Perkins, Anthony Cox. Starring: Susannah Campbell, Philip Corner, Anthony Cox, Bici Hendricks, Geoffrey Hendricks, Kyoko Ono, Yoko Ono, Ben Patterson, Jeff Perkins, Susan Poland, Jerry Sablo, Carolee Schneemann, James Tenney, Pieter Vanderbeck, Verne Williams. “The rebellious, erotic, liberatory nature of the film, which reflects the tenor of Fluxus, acts in direct opposition to the nineteenth-century scientific treatment of the body as a ‘dynamic field of action in need of regulation and control.’” –Chrissie Iles, “Erotic Conceptualism: The Films of Yoko Ono” Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: Unzipped
description: Designer Isaac Mizrahi proved a force of nature on the road to his legendary fall 1994 collection, a career-defining triumph that was documented with an effervescent intimacy by Douglas Keeve, Mizrahi’s then-partner. Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait—sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock—transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs. Digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. Funding provided by Isaac Mizrahi Entertainment. Laboratory services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Media Audio Services.

title: Europe ’51
description: According to Roberto Rossellini, Europe ’51 is a retelling of his film The Flowers of St. Francis ( Francesco, giullare di Dio , 1950) , from a female perspective. Ingrid Bergman portrays a wealthy American socialite living in Rome, moving through grief and guilt over the death of her son. As she sets out on a journey of newfound selflessness, devoting her time and money to the less fortunate, her husband and the community question her sanity. With Rossellini often pushing his actors to improvise dialogue, Ingrid would receive her lines only minutes before rolling. She would often reference this time as a difficult challenge. Working with first-time actors, with no written dialogue, and all during a Roman heat wave while Ingrid was pregnant with twins Isabella and Isotta, the director and actress proved their grit as a filmmaking duo.
director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Roberto Rossellini

title: Stop Making Sense
description: Stop Making Sense stars core band members David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz, and Jerry Harrison along with Bernie Worrell, Alex Weir, Steve Scales, Lynn Mabry and Edna Holt. The live performance was shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood's Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and features Talking Heads' most memorable songs.

title: Oldboy
description: One of the greatest – and most twisted – revenge thrillers of all time, this visceral thrill ride from Park Chan-wook never gets old. Come see the original “hallway fight” and so much more when Park Chan-wook’s Oldboy returns, restored and remastered in stunning 4K. For over twenty years, this cult classic has been thrilling audiences and inspiring other filmmakers. Grab a friend (or an octopus) and come experience Oldboy on the big screen.

title: Studio Ghibli All-Nighter
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS Celebrate the legacy of 'the greatest animation house on the planet' with some of the most adored and iconic characters of all-time in this All-Night Movie Marathon! MY NEIGHBOR TOTORO: When two girls move to the country to be near their ailing mother, they have adventures with the wondrous forest spirits who live nearby. KIKI’S DELIVERY SERVICE: Along with her black cat Jiji, Kiki settles in a seaside town and starts a high-flying delivery service. Here begins her magical encounter with independence and responsibility, making lifelong friends and finding her place in the world. HOWL’S MOVING CASTLE: When an unconfident young woman is cursed with an old body by a spiteful witch, her only chance of breaking the spell lies with a self-indulgent yet insecure young wizard and his companions in his legged, walking castle. PRINCESS MONONOKE: After a deadly curse forces him from home, young warrior Ashitaka journeys west and is drawn into a conflict between ancient forest spirits, an iron town, and a wolf-raised girl. SPIRITED AWAY: During her family's move to the suburbs, a sullen 10-year-old girl wanders into a world ruled by gods, witches and spirits, and where humans are changed into beasts. ------------------------------------------------------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! AGE RESTRICTIONS: This is strictly a 16+ event. Due to the event running through the night, anyone under the age 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian [aged 18+] for the full duration of the marathon.

title: Something Wicked This Way Comes: a folk + cosmic horror rave
description: After experiencing our horrors through the silver screen they’ve graciously offered to visit in person for a heretical multimedia rave experience. The bog witches and poltergeists, old gods and jinn, eldritch and uncanny alike, will descend upon the Rio Cinema for a manifestation of love only their ...

title: The Films of Matt Johnson Marathon
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS One of modern cinema's great cult heroes gets the all-night PCC treatment as we celebrate the films of Matt Johnson with back-to-back screenings of THE DIRTIES, OPERATION AVALANCHE, BLACKBERRY, NIRVANNA THE BAND THE SHOW THE MOVIE, and TONY. THE DIRTIES: The line between reality and fiction starts to blur when two best friends start making a movie about getting revenge on bullies. OPERATION AVALANCHE: In 1967, four undercover CIA agents were sent to NASA posing as a documentary film crew. What they discovered led to one of the biggest conspiracies in American history. BLACKBERRY: Two mismatched entrepreneurs – egghead innovator Mike Lazaridis and cut-throat businessman Jim Balsillie – joined forces in an endeavour that was to become a worldwide hit in little more than a decade. The story of the meteoric rise and catastrophic demise of the world's first smartphone. NIRVANNA THE BAND THE SHOW THE MOVIE: When their plan to book a show at the Rivoli goes horribly wrong, Matt and Jay accidentally travel back to the year 2008. TONY: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life. ------------------------------------------------------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! AGE RESTRICTIONS: This is strictly a 16+ event. Due to the event running through the night, anyone under the age of 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian [aged 18+] for the full duration of the marathon.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: The Royal Tenenbaums
description: Royal Tenenbaum and his wife Etheline had three children and then they separated. All three children are extraordinary --- all geniuses. Virtually all memory of the brilliance of the young Tenenbaums was subsequently erased by two decades of betrayal, failure, and disaster. Most of this was generally considered to be their father's fault. "The Royal Tenenbaums" is the story of the family's sudden, unexpected reunion one recent winter.

title: Andrew Lloyd Webber's Starlight Express - Live On
description: Filmed live at the specially designed Starlight Auditorium at Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre, ANDREW LLOYD WEBBER'S STARLIGHT EXPRESS - LIVE ON STAGE will immerse audiences in a world of speed, song and storytelling as an incredible cast of 40 whizz across the screen, performing some of musical theatre’s most beloved songs. As a child’s train set magically comes to life and the engines race to become the fastest in the world, Rusty the steam train has little hope of winning until he is inspired by the legend of the ‘Starlight Express’. A show seen around the world by over 30 million people, and with music by Andrew Lloyd Webber and lyrics by Richard Stilgoe, ANDREW LLOYD WEBBER'S STARLIGHT EXPRESS - LIVE ON STAGE is an electrifying experience for all ages.

title: WE, THE HATED (Just Stop Oil doc) + Q&A
description: A filmmaker gets more than he bargained for when his girlfriend is part of starting a controversial protest movement: Just Stop Oil. ‘We, The Hated’ tells the inside story of how everyday concerned citizens hatch a contentious plan of civil disobedience to wake the country up to the climate emergenc...

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Wong Kar Wai’s loose sequel to In the Mood for Love combines that film’s languorous air of romantic longing with a dizzying time-hopping structure and avant-sci-fi twist. Tony Leung Chiu Wai reprises his role as writer Chow Mo-Wan, whose numerous failed relationships with women who drift in and out of his life (and the one who goes in and out of room 2046, down the hall from his apartment) inspire the delirious futuristic love story he pens. 2046’s dazzling fantasy sequences give Wong and two of his key collaborators—cinematographer Christopher Doyle and editor/costume designer/production designer William Chang Suk Ping—license to let their imaginations run wild, propelling the sumptuous visuals and operatic emotions skyward toward the sublime.

title: SUNDAY SABBATH - MYSTERY HORROR MATINEE
description:
Give your Sunday afternoon to something unsettling. Sunday Sabbath uncovers secret selections from horror’s less-travelled roads: neglected masterpieces, regional nightmares and strange little films that found their own way to get under the skin.
The title remains undisclosed until showtime. It might be a Gothic chill, a creature feature, a psychological trap or something that refuses the usual categories. Come for the surprise; stay for the discovery you could not have chosen from a familiar poster.
Adults only.

title: Once Upon a Time...in Hollywood
description: Quentin Tarantino’s alternate history of the late-’60s film scene focuses on the intertwining lives of three figures: fading TV Western star Rick Dalton (Best Actor nominee Leonardo DiCaprio), his stunt double and best friend Cliff Booth (Supporting Actor winner Brad Pitt) and the real-life starlet Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie), whose life is destined to cross paths with Charles Manson and his followers. With its massive, stellar cast (including Margaret Qualley, Timothy Olyphant, Austin Butler, Dakota Fanning, Bruce Dern, Damian Lewis, and Al Pacino) and evocative, needle-drop score, Once Upon a Time elegantly evokes a lost era of Hollywood. Nominated for 10 Oscars including Best Picture, it won for production designer Barbara Ling and set decorator Nancy Haigh, who incorporate real-life locations such as the Musso & Frank Grill and the Playboy Mansion while creating believable living spaces for the protagonists.

title: FFF x Silent Film & Live Music: Protea (U*)
EC: RAPT
description: “RAPT is, paradoxically, both a film which looks back anachronistically toward the silent era and a work which belongs to the vanguard of sound cinema. Part of that paradox can be resolved by an understanding of the film’s complex utilization of music. RAPT employs very little dialogue, and in this respect it is reminiscent of the part-talkie genre…. It is linked to such abstract and hybrid avant-garde works as VAMPYR and L’ÂGE D’OR. The radical nature of RAPT, however, resides in its vision of a cinematic musical score. In making the film, Kirsanoff worked closely with the composers Honegger and Hoerce.” –Lucy Fisher CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: SELF-PORTRAITS
description: Just as the realm of two-dimensional portraiture has always encompassed self-portraiture, so too has the corresponding practice within cinema. This program collects instances of filmmakers turning the camera on themselves, or using the techniques of animation to explore their own appearances and identities. Gérard Courant CINÉMATON N°1000: GÉRARD COURANT (1987, 3.5 min, 16mm-to-digital) Kurt Kren 36/78 RISCHART (1978, 3 min, 16mm) Shigeko Kubota SELF-PORTRAIT (ca. 1970-1971, 5 min, video) Tehching Hsieh TIME CLOCK PIECE (ONE YEAR PERFORMANCE 1980-1981) (1980-81, 7 min, 16mm, silent) Gotot Prakosa SELF-PORTRAIT (1982, 3 min, digital) Valie Export SELF-PORTRAIT WITH HEAD / SELBSTPORTRAIT MIT KOPF (1966-67, 4 min, DCP, silent) Vito Acconci WATCH (1971, 9 min, Super-8mm-to-16mm, silent.
